### Restaurants in Berlin
https://www.placetta.com/guides/berlin/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Berlin takes 11 filings with 10 agencies, starting with the Commercial register entry for the GmbH and ending with the EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004). None of them has a fixed government fee and 11 fees are set by the space or the business. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Commercial register entry for the GmbH, Local court (Registergericht), through a notary. The articles are notarised and every managing director's signature on the application is certified by a notary, who files it electronically with the register court. The GmbH exists only once registered. Fee: Varies. https://www.handelsregister.de
2. Transparency register (beneficial owners), Transparency register (Bundesanzeiger Verlag). The company records its beneficial owners online. Fee: Varies. https://www.transparenzregister.de
3. Trade registration (Gewerbeanmeldung), Bezirksamt (district office) for the address, Ordnungsamt. Every shop, restaurant and trading business registers its trade with the district's Ordnungsamt when it starts, online or in person; the office passes it to the tax office and the inspectors. Fee: Varies. https://service.berlin.de/dienstleistung/121921/
4. Tax registration questionnaire (tax number and VAT ID), Finanzamt (tax office), through ELSTER. Filed online through ELSTER within a month of starting; the tax office then sends the tax number by post, and the VAT ID follows. Fee: Varies. Takes: Due within a month of starting. https://www.elster.de
5. Statutory accident insurance registration, The trade's Berufsgenossenschaft (statutory accident insurer). Every new business registers within a week with its trade's statutory accident insurer, including companies based abroad with staff in Germany. Fee: Varies. Takes: Due within a week of opening. https://www.dguv.de/de/versicherung/unternehmensnummer/anmeldung/index.jsp
6. Building permit for works or a change of use, Bezirksamt (district office) for the address, Stadtentwicklungsamt, Bau- und Wohnungsaufsicht. Works that aren't exempt, or turning a shop into a restaurant, need the district building office's permit, which reviews fire safety too; it is filed online. Fee: Varies. https://service.berlin.de/dienstleistung/350893/
7. Employer number for social insurance (Betriebsnummer), Bundesagentur für Arbeit, Betriebsnummern-Service. Applied for online before the first employee starts; payroll reports to social insurance carry it. Fee: Varies. https://www.arbeitsagentur.de/unternehmen/betriebsnummern-service
8. Infection protection instruction certificate for food staff, Bezirksamt (district office) for the address, Gesundheitsamt. Everyone who will prepare or sell food takes the health office's instruction and gets the certificate before starting work. Fee: Varies. https://service.berlin.de/dienstleistung/324295/
9. Permit for the shop sign (Werbeanlage), Bezirksamt (district office) for the address, Stadtentwicklungsamt, Bau- und Wohnungsaufsicht. A sign that isn't exempt needs the district building office's simplified permit, filed online. Fee: Varies. https://service.berlin.de/dienstleistung/350896/
10. Food business registration, Bezirksamt (district office) for the address, Veterinär- und Lebensmittelaufsicht. Each food business registers its premises with the district's veterinary and food inspection office on the registration form under Article 6 of Regulation (EC) 852/2004, before it opens. Fee: Varies. https://www.berlin.de/ba-spandau/politik-und-verwaltung/aemter/ordnungsamt/veterinaer-und-lebensmittelueberwachung/lebensmittelaufsicht-bezirksamt-spandau-1344989.php
11. EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), European Union (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), checked by the national food inspectors. Nothing to file: every food business keeps to the hygiene rules and runs food safety procedures based on HACCP principles, which the local food inspectors check. The registration it requires is the country's own food business registration. Fee: Varies. https://food.ec.europa.eu/food-safety/biological-safety/food-hygiene_en

Filed online through ELSTER within a month of starting; the tax office then sends the tax number by post, and the VAT ID follows. Fee: Varies. Takes: Due within a month of starting. https://www.elster.de
5. Statutory accident insurance registration, The trade's Berufsgenossenschaft (statutory accident insurer). Every new business registers within a week with its trade's statutory accident insurer, including companies based abroad with staff in Germany. Fee: Varies. Takes: Due within a week of opening. https://www.dguv.de/de/versicherung/unternehmensnummer/anmeldung/index.jsp
6. Building permit, including a change of use, Landeshauptstadt München, Referat für Stadtplanung und Bauordnung, Lokalbaukommission (LBK). New building, extensions, alterations and changes of use as a rule need a building permit from the city's lower building authority; a new restaurant's licence waits for the LBK's written release. Fee: Varies. https://stadt.muenchen.de/service/info/referat-fur-stadtplanung-und-bauordnung/10331531/
7. Employer number for social insurance (Betriebsnummer), Bundesagentur für Arbeit, Betriebsnummern-Service. Applied for online before the first employee starts; payroll reports to social insurance carry it. Fee: Varies. https://www.arbeitsagentur.de/unternehmen/betriebsnummern-service
8. EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), European Union (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), checked by the national food inspectors. Nothing to file: every food business keeps to the hygiene rules and runs food safety procedures based on HACCP principles, which the local food inspectors check. The registration it requires is the country's own food business registration. Fee: Varies. https://food.ec.europa.eu/food-safety/biological-safety/food-hygiene_en

9. Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation, European Union (Regulation (EU) 2025/40), with each country's producer register for packaging. Goods imported in packaging meet the regulation's packaging requirements, and the importer registers as the producer of that packaging in each country it sells in (extended producer responsibility). Fee: Varies. https://environment.ec.europa.eu/topics/waste-and-recycling/packaging-waste_en

### Restaurants in Frankfurt
https://www.placetta.com/guides/frankfurt/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Frankfurt takes 7 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the Commercial register entry for the GmbH and ending with the EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004). None of them has a fixed government fee and 7 fees are set by the space or the business. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to grocery stores, milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Commercial register entry for the GmbH, Local court (Registergericht), through a notary. The articles are notarised and every managing director's signature on the application is certified by a notary, who files it electronically with the register court. The GmbH exists only once registered. Fee: Varies. https://www.handelsregister.de
2. Transparency register (beneficial owners), Transparency register (Bundesanzeiger Verlag). The company records its beneficial owners online. Fee: Varies. https://www.transparenzregister.de
3. Trade registration (Gewerbeanmeldung), Stadt Frankfurt am Main, Ordnungsamt. Every shop, restaurant and trading business registers its trade with Frankfurt's trade office when it starts. Fee: Varies. https://frankfurt.de
4. Tax registration questionnaire (tax number and VAT ID), Finanzamt (tax office), through ELSTER. Filed online through ELSTER within a month of starting; the tax office then sends the tax number by post, and the VAT ID follows. Fee: Varies. Takes: Due within a month of starting. https://www.elster.de
5. Statutory accident insurance registration, The trade's Berufsgenossenschaft (statutory accident insurer). Every new business registers within a week with its trade's statutory accident insurer, including companies based abroad with staff in Germany. Fee: Varies. Takes: Due within a week of opening. https://www.dguv.de/de/versicherung/unternehmensnummer/anmeldung/index.jsp
6. Employer number for social insurance (Betriebsnummer), Bundesagentur für Arbeit, Betriebsnummern-Service. Applied for online before the first employee starts; payroll reports to social insurance carry it. Fee: Varies. https://www.arbeitsagentur.de/unternehmen/betriebsnummern-service
7. EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), European Union (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), checked by the national food inspectors. Nothing to file: every food business keeps to the hygiene rules and runs food safety procedures based on HACCP principles, which the local food inspectors check. The registration it requires is the country's own food business registration. Fee: Varies. https://food.ec.europa.eu/food-safety/biological-safety/food-hygiene_en

### Restaurants in Madrid
https://www.placetta.com/guides/madrid/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Madrid takes 6 filings with 5 agencies, starting with the limited company (SL) deed and commercial register entry and ending with the EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004). None of them has a fixed government fee and 6 fees are set by the space or the business. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to grocery stores, milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Limited company (SL) deed and commercial register entry, Notary and Registro Mercantil. The company name is reserved with the central commercial register, the capital is deposited, and all partners sign the deed of incorporation before a notary, which is then entered in the provincial commercial register. It can also be started online through CIRCE. Fee: Varies. https://paeelectronico.es/es-es/CreaEmpresaPorTiMismo/Paginas/CIRCE.aspx
2. Company tax number (NIF), Agencia Tributaria. The company asks the tax agency for its NIF before any operation with tax effect, and within a month of its incorporation or establishment in Spain. Fee: Varies. https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
3. Tax census declaration (Modelo 036) for VAT and income tax, Agencia Tributaria. Filed online with the tax agency before the business starts, registering it for VAT and the other taxes it owes. Fee: Varies. https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
4. Responsible declaration to open (or a licence where required), Ayuntamiento de Madrid, Agencia de Actividades (or an authorised ECU). Most shops and restaurants open, with their works, on a signed responsible declaration filed with the city or an authorised collaborating body (ECU); it takes effect when filed. A licence is needed only where safety, public health or the environment justify it. Fee: Varies. https://sede.madrid.es
5. Employer registration with Social Security (contribution account code), Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social. The employer applies for its contribution account code on form TA.6 before the first hire, online with a digital certificate or at a Treasury office. Fee: Varies. https://www.seg-social.es
6. EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), European Union (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), checked by the national food inspectors. Nothing to file: every food business keeps to the hygiene rules and runs food safety procedures based on HACCP principles, which the local food inspectors check. The registration it requires is the country's own food business registration. Fee: Varies. https://food.ec.europa.eu/food-safety/biological-safety/food-hygiene_en

None of them has a fixed government fee and 6 fees are set by the space or the business. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Limited company (SL) deed and commercial register entry, Notary and Registro Mercantil. The company name is reserved with the central commercial register, the capital is deposited, and all partners sign the deed of incorporation before a notary, which is then entered in the provincial commercial register. It can also be started online through CIRCE. Fee: Varies. https://paeelectronico.es/es-es/CreaEmpresaPorTiMismo/Paginas/CIRCE.aspx
2. Company tax number (NIF), Agencia Tributaria. The company asks the tax agency for its NIF before any operation with tax effect, and within a month of its incorporation or establishment in Spain. Fee: Varies. https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
3. Tax census declaration (Modelo 036) for VAT and income tax, Agencia Tributaria. Filed online with the tax agency before the business starts, registering it for VAT and the other taxes it owes. Fee: Varies. https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
4. Activity notice or licence, Ajuntament de Barcelona. Shops and restaurants notify the city of their activity online before opening; some need a licence. Fee: Varies. https://ajuntament.barcelona.cat/comerc/en/do-you-have-establishment/how-open-business-barcelona-step-step
5. Employer registration with Social Security (contribution account code), Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social. The employer applies for its contribution account code on form TA.6 before the first hire, online with a digital certificate or at a Treasury office. Fee: Varies. https://www.seg-social.es
6. EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), European Union (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), checked by the national food inspectors. Nothing to file: every food business keeps to the hygiene rules and runs food safety procedures based on HACCP principles, which the local food inspectors check. The registration it requires is the country's own food business registration. Fee: Varies. https://food.ec.europa.eu/food-safety/biological-safety/food-hygiene_en

### Restaurants in Milan
https://www.placetta.com/guides/milan/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Milan takes 9 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the company registration in the business register (ComUnica) and ending with the Yearly Chamber of Commerce fee. None of them has a fixed government fee and 9 fees are set by the space or the business. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Company registration in the business register (ComUnica), Registro delle imprese, Camera di commercio. Filed online as one Comunicazione Unica, which registers the company with the Chamber of Commerce and, in the same filing, with the tax agency, INAIL and INPS. A company's deed of incorporation is drawn up by a notary. Fee: Varies. Takes: Registration is completed within five days of the application. https://www.registroimprese.it
2. VAT number (partita IVA), Agenzia delle Entrate. Opened through the same Comunicazione Unica, for tax purposes, before trading. Fee: Varies. https://www.agenziaentrate.gov.it
3. Food and drink service notice (SCIA), or an authorisation in protected zones, Comune di Milano, SUAP (Sportello Unico Attività Produttive). Outside Milan's protected zones a bar or restaurant files the SCIA online with the SUAP, with the ATS health fee receipt; inside them it needs an authorisation. Fee: Varies. https://www.impresainungiorno.gov.it
4. Food business health notice for registration, ATS Città Metropolitana di Milano, through the SUAP. Filed with the SCIA through Milan's SUAP, which sends it to the health authority (ATS) to register the food business. Fee: Varies. https://www.impresainungiorno.gov.it
5. Employer registration with INPS and INAIL, INPS and INAIL. Registered through the Comunicazione Unica, for pensions and social security (INPS) and workplace accident insurance (INAIL). Fee: Varies. https://www.inps.it
6. Shop sign notice (SCIA), Comune di Milano, Area Pubblicità e Occupazione Suolo. A shop sign is notified to the city's advertising and public land office with its SCIA form, in three signed copies. Fee: Varies. https://fareimpresa.comune.milano.it/documents/20126/526414/Modulo+SCIA+per+insegne+e+targhe+professionali.pdf/20cf0075-f30e-02af-0f4d-9886b19587b9?t=1637749345425
7. Fire prevention notice, for premises on the fire brigade's list, Vigili del Fuoco (the provincial fire brigade command). Premises whose size or use puts them on the fire prevention list file a fire safety SCIA with the fire brigade, through the SUAP. Fee: Varies. https://www.vigilfuoco.it
8. EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), European Union (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), checked by the national food inspectors. Nothing to file: every food business keeps to the hygiene rules and runs food safety procedures based on HACCP principles, which the local food inspectors check. The registration it requires is the country's own food business registration. Fee: Varies. https://food.ec.europa.eu/food-safety/biological-safety/food-hygiene_en
9. Yearly Chamber of Commerce fee, Camera di commercio. Paid every year by every business entered in the register. Fee: Varies. https://www.registroimprese.it

5. Fire prevention notice, for premises on the fire brigade's list, Vigili del Fuoco (the provincial fire brigade command). Premises whose size or use puts them on the fire prevention list file a fire safety SCIA with the fire brigade, through the SUAP. Fee: Varies. https://www.vigilfuoco.it
6. EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), European Union (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), checked by the national food inspectors. Nothing to file: every food business keeps to the hygiene rules and runs food safety procedures based on HACCP principles, which the local food inspectors check. The registration it requires is the country's own food business registration. Fee: Varies. https://food.ec.europa.eu/food-safety/biological-safety/food-hygiene_en
7. Yearly Chamber of Commerce fee, Camera di commercio. Paid every year by every business entered in the register. Fee: Varies. https://www.registroimprese.it

### Restaurants in Amsterdam
https://www.placetta.com/guides/amsterdam/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Amsterdam takes 10 filings with 6 agencies, starting with the private limited company (BV) through a civil-law notary and ending with the EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004). None of them has a fixed government fee and 10 fees are set by the space or the business. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Private limited company (BV) through a civil-law notary, Civil-law notary (notaris). A BV is incorporated by a civil-law notary's deed, which includes the articles; the notary registers it with KVK and the tax office. Fee: Varies. https://www.kvk.nl
2. Business register entry (KVK), Kamer van Koophandel (KVK). Every new business registers with KVK, with its lease or purchase contract; KVK passes the details to the tax office. A foreign company opening a branch registers it too. Fee: Varies. https://www.kvk.nl
3. VAT numbers from the tax office (Belastingdienst), Belastingdienst. No separate request: after the KVK registration the tax office sends the VAT identification number and the VAT number. Fee: Varies. https://www.belastingdienst.nl
4. Environment and planning permit, where the plans don't fit the environment plan, The gemeente (municipality): Gemeente Amsterdam, Gemeente Rotterdam. Checked first against the municipality's environment plan on the Omgevingsloket; building works or a use the plan doesn't allow need the permit. Fee: Varies. https://omgevingswet.overheid.nl
5. Catering operating permit for the premises (exploitatievergunning), The gemeente (municipality): Gemeente Amsterdam, Gemeente Rotterdam. Where customers eat and drink on the premises, the municipality's operating permit is needed; the municipality may run an integrity (Bibob) check. Fee: Varies. https://www.amsterdam.nl
6. Employer registration for payroll tax, Belastingdienst. Before hiring, the company registers as an employer with the tax office and gets its payroll tax number. Fee: Varies. https://www.belastingdienst.nl
7. Permit for the shop sign, The gemeente (municipality): Gemeente Amsterdam, Gemeente Rotterdam. Advertising on or at the premises often needs an environment and planning permit; the permit check shows which. Fee: Varies. https://omgevingswet.overheid.nl
8. Fire safety measures (checked by the municipality and the fire service), The gemeente (municipality): Gemeente Amsterdam, Gemeente Rotterdam. The premises take fire safety measures, such as non-flammable or flame-retardant materials; larger premises notify the municipality of their fire-safe use. Fee: Varies. https://business.gov.nl/starting-your-business/starting-situations/starting-a-hotel-restaurant-or-cafe-step-by-step-plan/
9. Food business registration with the NVWA, Nederlandse Voedsel- en Warenautoriteit (NVWA). A business that makes, processes or sells food registers with the NVWA, and works to a HACCP food safety plan or an approved hygiene code, which the NVWA inspects. Fee: Varies. https://www.nvwa.nl
10. EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), European Union (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), checked by the national food inspectors. Nothing to file: every food business keeps to the hygiene rules and runs food safety procedures based on HACCP principles, which the local food inspectors check. The registration it requires is the country's own food business registration. Fee: Varies. https://food.ec.europa.eu/food-safety/biological-safety/food-hygiene_en

Checked first against the municipality's environment plan on the Omgevingsloket; building works or a use the plan doesn't allow need the permit. Fee: Varies. https://omgevingswet.overheid.nl
5. Catering operating permit for the premises (exploitatievergunning), The gemeente (municipality): Gemeente Amsterdam, Gemeente Rotterdam. Where customers eat and drink on the premises, the municipality's operating permit is needed; the municipality may run an integrity (Bibob) check. Fee: Varies. https://www.amsterdam.nl
6. Employer registration for payroll tax, Belastingdienst. Before hiring, the company registers as an employer with the tax office and gets its payroll tax number. Fee: Varies. https://www.belastingdienst.nl
7. Permit for the shop sign, The gemeente (municipality): Gemeente Amsterdam, Gemeente Rotterdam. Advertising on or at the premises often needs an environment and planning permit; the permit check shows which. Fee: Varies. https://omgevingswet.overheid.nl
8. Fire safety measures (checked by the municipality and the fire service), The gemeente (municipality): Gemeente Amsterdam, Gemeente Rotterdam. The premises take fire safety measures, such as non-flammable or flame-retardant materials; larger premises notify the municipality of their fire-safe use. Fee: Varies. https://business.gov.nl/starting-your-business/starting-situations/starting-a-hotel-restaurant-or-cafe-step-by-step-plan/
9. Food business registration with the NVWA, Nederlandse Voedsel- en Warenautoriteit (NVWA). A business that makes, processes or sells food registers with the NVWA, and works to a HACCP food safety plan or an approved hygiene code, which the NVWA inspects. Fee: Varies. https://www.nvwa.nl
10. EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), European Union (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), checked by the national food inspectors. Nothing to file: every food business keeps to the hygiene rules and runs food safety procedures based on HACCP principles, which the local food inspectors check. The registration it requires is the country's own food business registration. Fee: Varies. https://food.ec.europa.eu/food-safety/biological-safety/food-hygiene_en

### Restaurants in Dublin
https://www.placetta.com/guides/dublin/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Dublin takes 7 filings with 6 agencies, starting with the company registration with the CRO and ending with the EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004). None of them has a fixed government fee, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Company registration with the CRO, Companies Registration Office. The company is registered online through the CRO's CORE system; a foreign company opening a branch registers the branch. Fee: Varies. https://core.cro.ie
2. Tax registration with Revenue (corporation tax and VAT), Revenue (Office of the Revenue Commissioners). A new company registers online with Revenue through eRegistration, for corporation tax and, as they apply, VAT and employer PAYE. Fee: Varies. https://www.ros.ie
3. Planning permission for a change of use, Dublin City Council, Planning. A significant change of use, such as turning a shop into a restaurant, needs planning permission, applied for online with public notices and the fee in the council's checklist. Fee: Varies. https://www.dublincity.ie/planning-and-land-use/make-planning-application/apply-planning-permission
4. Fire safety certificate for a fit-out or change of use, The council's building control authority (Dublin City Council, Cork City Council fire prevention). A fire safety certificate is applied for through the national Building Control Management System before work starts on a new building, an extension, a material alteration or a change of use. Fee: Varies. https://www.gov.ie/en/dublin-city-council/services/getting-a-fire-safety-certificate/
5. Employer registration with Revenue (PAYE), Revenue (Office of the Revenue Commissioners). Before paying an employee, the company tells Revenue through MyEnquiries in ROS that it will pay staff; a company registers even if its only employees are its directors. Fee: Free. https://www.revenue.ie/en/employing-people/becoming-an-employer-and-ongoing-obligations/registration-of-employers-for-paye-purposes/index.aspx
6. Food business registration, HSE Environmental Health Service (the inspecting official agency). Before starting, a food business registers with the official agency that inspects it, and has food hygiene training, traceability and a food safety management system. Fee: Varies. https://www.fsai.ie/business-advice/starting-a-food-business
7. EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), European Union (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), checked by the national food inspectors. Nothing to file: every food business keeps to the hygiene rules and runs food safety procedures based on HACCP principles, which the local food inspectors check. The registration it requires is the country's own food business registration. Fee: Varies. https://food.ec.europa.eu/food-safety/biological-safety/food-hygiene_en

### Restaurants in Brussels
https://www.placetta.com/guides/brussels/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Brussels takes 8 filings with 8 agencies, starting with the company formation: deed of incorporation filed with the enterprise court and ending with the EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004). The fixed government fees add up to about €150, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 2 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Company formation: deed of incorporation filed with the enterprise court, Greffe du tribunal de l'entreprise (through the notary). The founders sign the deed (an authentic notarial deed for an SRL, SA or SC) with a financial plan, and the deed is filed with the competent enterprise court registry within 30 days of signing. Fee: Varies. Takes: Filed within 30 days of signing the deed. https://business.belgium.be/fr/creer-votre-entreprise/enregistrer-votre-entreprise/creer-votre-societe
2. Crossroads Bank for Enterprises registration, through an enterprise counter, An approved guichet d'entreprises (enterprise counter), for the BCE. Before starting, the business registers with the BCE through an approved enterprise counter, which issues the enterprise number; a company first has its deed and articles filed with the enterprise court registry. Fee: Varies. https://economie.fgov.be
3. VAT activation of the enterprise number, SPF Finances. The enterprise number is activated for VAT online on the SPF Finances site, free, or by the enterprise counter for a fee. Fee: Free. https://finances.belgium.be
4. Planning permit for the use (permis d'urbanisme), City of Brussels, Urbanisme (under the Brussels-Capital Region's planning code). A restaurant, café, snack bar or any shop where food or drink is consumed on site needs a planning permit for that use; the operating licence is refused if the building's planning use doesn't match. Fee: Varies. https://www.bruxelles.be/obtenir-une-autorisation-pour-ouvrir-un-commerce
5. Employer registration with the social security office (ONSS), Office national de sécurité sociale (ONSS). Before the first hire the business identifies itself as an employer with the ONSS through the online service WIDE and receives an ONSS number; each hire is then declared in Dimona. Fee: Free. https://www.socialsecurity.be/site_fr/general/first_visit/access/register-as-employer.htm
6. Food chain registration or authorisation with the AFSCA, Agence fédérale pour la sécurité de la chaîne alimentaire (AFSCA). Every operator in the food chain registers with the AFSCA, and some activities need its authorisation, before starting. Fee: Varies. https://favv-afsca.be
7. Hospitality operating licence (attestation de conformité), City of Brussels, Affaires économiques (Horeca). A restaurant, café or snack bar applies to the city at least 3 months before opening so the file can be finished 20 days before; the licence certifies the premises meet the rules for receiving the public. Fee: €150. Takes: Filed at least 3 months before opening. https://www.bruxelles.be/horeca-autorisation-exploitation
8. EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), European Union (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), checked by the national food inspectors. Nothing to file: every food business keeps to the hygiene rules and runs food safety procedures based on HACCP principles, which the local food inspectors check. The registration it requires is the country's own food business registration. Fee: Varies. https://food.ec.europa.eu/food-safety/biological-safety/food-hygiene_en

### Restaurants in Lisbon
https://www.placetta.com/guides/lisbon/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Lisbon takes 6 filings with 6 agencies, starting with the Company creation (Empresa na Hora) and ending with the EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004). The fixed government fees add up to about €360, 4 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Company creation (Empresa na Hora), Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado (IRN). A limited company (sociedade por quotas or unipessoal) or a public limited company is created at an Empresa na Hora desk, or online. Fee: €360. https://registo.justica.gov.pt/Empresas/Empresa-na-Hora
2. Start-of-activity tax declaration, Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira (Finanças). The company declares the start of its activity to the tax authority, which registers it for VAT and income tax. Fee: Varies. https://www.gov.pt/servicos/abrir-atividade-nas-financas
3. Use permit for the premises (autorização de utilização), Câmara Municipal de Lisboa (Urbanismo). Whatever the premises, a restaurant needs a use authorisation from the city; in a used building the existing one is checked for restaurant use, or a change of use is applied for. Fee: Varies. https://areadocomerciante.dgae.gov.pt/documentacao1/documentos/20250530-guia-da-restauracao_2025-pdf.aspx
4. Employer duties with Social Security: hiring declarations, Instituto da Segurança Social (Segurança Social Direta). The company's registration with Social Security follows from the tax start-of-activity declaration; as an employer it declares every new hire online in Segurança Social Direta within the 24 hours before the contract starts. Fee: Free. Takes: Each hire declared within the 24 hours before the contract starts. https://www.seg-social.pt/admissao-de-trabalhadores
5. Opening notice for a restaurant or bar (mera comunicação prévia), Câmara Municipal de Lisboa, through the gov.pt business counter. Opening a restaurant or bar is, as a rule, a prior notice to the city made on gov.pt, kept on file with proof of the fees paid; where some requirements can't be met, the city's authorisation is needed instead. Fee: Varies. https://www.gov.pt/servicos/abrir-um-estabelecimento-de-restauracao-ou-bebidas
6. EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), European Union (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), checked by the national food inspectors. Nothing to file: every food business keeps to the hygiene rules and runs food safety procedures based on HACCP principles, which the local food inspectors check. The registration it requires is the country's own food business registration. Fee: Varies. https://food.ec.europa.eu/food-safety/biological-safety/food-hygiene_en

Whatever the premises, a restaurant needs a use authorisation from the city; in a used building the existing one is checked for restaurant use, or a change of use is applied for. Fee: Varies. https://areadocomerciante.dgae.gov.pt/documentacao1/documentos/20250530-guia-da-restauracao_2025-pdf.aspx
4. Employer duties with Social Security: hiring declarations, Instituto da Segurança Social (Segurança Social Direta). The company's registration with Social Security follows from the tax start-of-activity declaration; as an employer it declares every new hire online in Segurança Social Direta within the 24 hours before the contract starts. Fee: Free. Takes: Each hire declared within the 24 hours before the contract starts. https://www.seg-social.pt/admissao-de-trabalhadores
5. Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation, European Union (Regulation (EU) 2025/40), with each country's producer register for packaging. Goods imported in packaging meet the regulation's packaging requirements, and the importer registers as the producer of that packaging in each country it sells in (extended producer responsibility). Fee: Varies. https://environment.ec.europa.eu/topics/waste-and-recycling/packaging-waste_en

### Restaurants in Zurich
https://www.placetta.com/guides/zurich/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Zurich takes 7 filings with 6 agencies, starting with the Commercial register entry in the canton of Zurich and ending with the sign permit (Reklamebewilligung). None of them has a fixed government fee and 7 fees are set by the space or the business. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Commercial register entry in the canton of Zurich, Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zürich. After a notary has recorded the founding deed, the GmbH is filed with the Zurich commercial register office with the deed and the office's application form. The company exists from its entry. Fee: Varies. https://www.zh.ch/de/wirtschaft-arbeit/unternehmensportal/opu/firma-gruenden/rechtsform-waehlen/gmbh-gruenden.html
2. VAT registration with the Federal Tax Administration, Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung (ESTV). A business established in Switzerland is in principle liable to VAT and registers online with the ESTV once its turnover reaches the threshold. Fee: Varies. https://www.estv.admin.ch/de/mwst-steuerpflicht
3. Food business project approval, City of Zurich, Umwelt- und Gesundheitsschutz (UGZ). A business that serves food and drink, or a food shop, has its project approved by the city's food inspectorate, usually as a condition of the building permit, and reports readiness for the joint opening inspection. Fee: Varies. https://www.stadt-zuerich.ch/de/planen-und-bauen/bauvorschriften-und-planerische-grundlagen/bauten-anlagen/lebensmittelbetriebe.html
4. Building permit, including a change of use, City of Zurich, Amt für Baubewilligungen. New building, alterations and certain changes of use need a building permit, applied for on the canton's eBaugesucheZH platform; ventilation and air conditioning are permit items too. Fee: Varies. Takes: About 2 months (notice procedure), 3 months (ordinary fast) or 5 months (ordinary long), after a 21-day completeness check. https://www.stadt-zuerich.ch/de/planen-und-bauen/baubewilligungen/bewilligungspflichtige-vorhaben.html
5. Employer affiliation with a compensation fund (AHV), The canton's or trade's Ausgleichskasse (AHV compensation fund). An employer joins a compensation fund for old-age and survivors' insurance contributions before paying wages. Fee: Varies. https://www.kmu.admin.ch
6. Restaurant licence (Gastwirtschaftspatent), City of Zurich, Stadtpolizei, Kommissariat Verwaltungspolizei (Bewilligung Gastro). Filed at least 4 weeks before opening, once the building permit and the food project approval are final; the licence can be granted at the opening inspection. Fee: Varies. Takes: Filed at least 4 weeks before opening. https://www.stadt-zuerich.ch/content/dam/web/de/stadtleben/veranstaltungen-und-bewilligungen/dokumente/gastgewerbe/der-weg-zum-restaurant/gesuch-fuer-ein-patent-zur-fuehrung-einer-gastwirtschaft.pdf
7. Sign permit (Reklamebewilligung), City of Zurich, Amt für Baubewilligungen. A new or changed sign needs a permit first; a pre-enquiry or the application itself is made online. Fee: Varies. https://www.stadt-zuerich.ch/de/planen-und-bauen/baubewilligungen/reklame-aussenwerbung/gesuche.html

### Restaurants in Vienna
https://www.placetta.com/guides/vienna/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Vienna takes 6 filings with 6 agencies, starting with the company register entry (Firmenbuch) and ending with the EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004). None of them has a fixed government fee, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to grocery stores, milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Company register entry (Firmenbuch), Firmenbuchgericht (the regional court). A GmbH is founded by a notarial act and entered in the company register; the business service portal offers a simplified online route for some. Fee: Varies. https://www.usp.gv.at
2. Trade registration (Gewerbeanmeldung), Gewerbebehörde: the Bezirkshauptmannschaft, in a statutory city the Magistrat (in Vienna the Magistratisches Bezirksamt or MA 63). The trade is registered with the trade authority for the location, in person, in writing or online through the business service portal. Fee: Varies. https://www.usp.gv.at
3. Tax registration with the Finanzamt Österreich (tax number), Finanzamt Österreich (Federal Ministry of Finance). The opening of the business is reported to the Finanzamt Österreich within one month, which sends the questionnaire (Verf 15 for a company) and issues the tax number. A one-person GmbH can report it through the USP's eGründung. Fee: Varies. Takes: Within one month of opening. https://www.usp.gv.at/themen/steuern-finanzen/steuerliche-rechte-und-pflichten/pflichten-des-unternehmers.html
4. Premises use permit (Betriebsanlagengenehmigung), City of Vienna, Magistratisches Bezirksamt for the district. A restaurant or shop whose kitchen, machines or customers could affect neighbours, staff or guests needs the district office's approval before it is built or changed. The application is made on the city's form with plans and a description of the premises. Fee: Varies. Takes: The approval must be in hand before the premises are built or changed. https://www.wien.gv.at/pdf/mba/ansuchen-gewerbe.pdf
5. Employer account and staff registration with the health insurance fund (ÖGK), Österreichische Gesundheitskasse (ÖGK). Before the first hire the employer asks the ÖGK, free and online, for an employer account number, then registers every employee through ELDA before they start work. Fee: Free. Takes: Each employee is registered before starting work. https://www.usp.gv.at/themen/mitarbeiter-und-gesundheit/einstellung-mitarbeiter-und-arten-der-beschaeftigung/weitere-informationen-einstellen-von-personal/anmeldung-dienstnehmer.html
6. EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), European Union (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), checked by the national food inspectors. Nothing to file: every food business keeps to the hygiene rules and runs food safety procedures based on HACCP principles, which the local food inspectors check. The registration it requires is the country's own food business registration. Fee: Varies. https://food.ec.europa.eu/food-safety/biological-safety/food-hygiene_en

### Restaurants in Stockholm
https://www.placetta.com/guides/stockholm/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Stockholm takes 7 filings with 5 agencies, starting with the company registration (Verksamt) and ending with the sign permit (bygglov för skylt). The fixed government fees add up to about SEK 2,400, 4 fees are set by the space or the business and 2 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to grocery stores, milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Company registration (Verksamt), Bolagsverket and Skatteverket. Register the company and for tax, VAT and as an employer in one place. Fee: SEK 2,400. https://www.verksamt.se
2. VAT and F-tax registration with Skatteverket, Skatteverket (Swedish Tax Agency). Registered on verksamt.se with the company registration, or on form SKV 4620; a business with taxable sales registers for VAT. Fee: Free. https://www.skatteverket.se/foretag/etjansterochblanketter/blanketterbroschyrer/blanketter/info/4620.4.6efe6285127ab4f1d2580003836.html
3. Building permit or building notice, including a change of use, City of Stockholm, Stadsbyggnadskontoret (building permits). Building, extending or altering premises, including changing their use or façade, often needs a building permit or a notice to the city. Fee: Varies. https://bygglov.stockholm/
4. Employer registration with Skatteverket, Skatteverket (Swedish Tax Agency). A company that pays wages registers as an employer through the e-service on verksamt.se, or on form SKV 4620, and then files a monthly employer return. Fee: Free. https://www.skatteverket.se/foretag/arbetsgivare/arbetsgivarregistrering/registreradig.4.18e1b10334ebe8bc80003496.html
5. Food business registration with the city's food control, City of Stockholm, Miljöförvaltningen (food control). Most businesses that sell, serve or handle food register with the environment department's food control before they start; a few register with Livsmedelsverket instead. Fee: Varies. Takes: Registered before the business starts. https://tillstand.stockholm/tillstand-regler-och-tillsyn/servering-av-mat/anmala-livsmedels--eller-kontaktmaterialverksamhet/
6. EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), European Union (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), checked by the national food inspectors. Nothing to file: every food business keeps to the hygiene rules and runs food safety procedures based on HACCP principles, which the local food inspectors check. The registration it requires is the country's own food business registration. Fee: Varies. https://food.ec.europa.eu/food-safety/biological-safety/food-hygiene_en
7. Sign permit (bygglov för skylt), City of Stockholm, Stadsbyggnadskontoret (building permits). Putting up, moving or changing a sign usually needs a building permit; the rules depend on where it is and how it looks. Fee: Varies. https://tillstand.stockholm/tillstand-regler-och-tillsyn/lokal-och-fastigheter/ansoka-om-bygglov-for-skylt/

### Restaurants in Copenhagen
https://www.placetta.com/guides/copenhagen/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Copenhagen takes 5 filings with 4 agencies, starting with the company registration (Virk) and ending with the EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004). The fixed government fees add up to about DKK 670, 2 fees are set by the space or the business and 2 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to grocery stores, milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Company registration (Virk), Danish Business Authority. Register the company and its CVR number, VAT and employer status online. Fee: DKK 670. https://virk.dk
2. VAT registration with the Danish Tax Agency, Skattestyrelsen (Danish Tax Agency), through virk.dk. Once the company exists it registers on virk.dk for the duties that apply; a company expected to sell more than 50,000 kroner in 12 months registers for VAT. Fee: Free. https://virk.dk/integration/ERST/Startblanketten_momsregistrering_mv
3. Building permit for a restaurant or change of use, City of Copenhagen, Område for Bygninger. Setting up a restaurant needs a building permit, applied for in Byg og Miljø, with the fire safety, escape route and access requirements that go with it. Fee: Varies. https://www.kk.dk/borger/bolig-og-byggeri/byggetilladelse/byggetilladelse-trin-for-trin/restaurant-og-cafe
4. Employer registration (A-tax and labour market contribution), Skattestyrelsen (Danish Tax Agency), through virk.dk. Before paying wages the company registers as an employer on virk.dk, then reports and pays A-tax and labour market contributions every month in eIndkomst. Fee: Free. https://virk.dk/integration/ERST/Startblanketten_momsregistrering_mv
5. EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), European Union (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), checked by the national food inspectors. Nothing to file: every food business keeps to the hygiene rules and runs food safety procedures based on HACCP principles, which the local food inspectors check. The registration it requires is the country's own food business registration. Fee: Varies. https://food.ec.europa.eu/food-safety/biological-safety/food-hygiene_en

### Restaurants in Warsaw
https://www.placetta.com/guides/warsaw/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Warsaw takes 6 filings with 6 agencies, starting with the Company registration in the National Court Register (KRS) and ending with the EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004). None of them has a fixed government fee, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to grocery stores, milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Company registration in the National Court Register (KRS), Sąd rejonowy (the registry court), through the court registers portal (PRS) or S24. Register the company in the court register and for tax and social insurance online. Fee: Varies. https://www.biznes.gov.pl/pl/portal/ou1503
2. VAT registration with the tax office (VAT-R), Urząd skarbowy (tax office), Krajowa Administracja Skarbowa. The VAT-R form goes to the tax office, online through the tax portal with a qualified signature or on paper; registering is required once the year's sales pass 240,000 złoty, and optional before. Fee: Varies. https://www.biznes.gov.pl/pl/portal/ou1609
3. Change-of-use notice for the building (PB-18), Prezydent m.st. Warszawy (the district office's architecture and building department). Changing the use of a building or unit, for example to a restaurant, is notified to the city (a city with county rights) on form PB-18, online through e-Budownictwo or on paper; works needing a building permit are applied for together. Fee: Varies. https://wnioski.gunb.gov.pl/
4. Employer contributions account and staff registration with ZUS, Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych (ZUS). A company in the KRS is registered as a contribution payer from the court register's data; each employee is then registered with ZUS within 7 days of starting work. Fee: Free. Takes: Each employee within 7 days of starting work. https://www.biznes.gov.pl/pl/portal/00275
5. Food premises entry in the sanitary inspection's register (Sanepid), Państwowy Powiatowy Inspektor Sanitarny w m.st. Warszawie (PSSE Warszawa). A restaurant or shop selling food asks the Warsaw sanitary inspector to enter its premises in the register at least 14 days before it starts; some activities need approval instead. Fee: Varies. Takes: Filed at least 14 days before opening. https://www.biznes.gov.pl/pl/portal/ou521
6. EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), European Union (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), checked by the national food inspectors. Nothing to file: every food business keeps to the hygiene rules and runs food safety procedures based on HACCP principles, which the local food inspectors check. The registration it requires is the country's own food business registration. Fee: Varies. https://food.ec.europa.eu/food-safety/biological-safety/food-hygiene_en

4. Employer contributions account and staff registration with ZUS, Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych (ZUS). A company in the KRS is registered as a contribution payer from the court register's data; each employee is then registered with ZUS within 7 days of starting work. Fee: Free. Takes: Each employee within 7 days of starting work. https://www.biznes.gov.pl/pl/portal/00275
5. General Product Safety Regulation: a responsible operator in the EU, European Union (Regulation (EU) 2023/988), enforced by the national market surveillance authority. Nothing to file: a consumer product made outside the EU is sold there only with an economic operator in the EU responsible for it, named with its contact details on the product. Fee: Varies. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32023R0988
6. Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation, European Union (Regulation (EU) 2025/40), with each country's producer register for packaging. Goods imported in packaging meet the regulation's packaging requirements, and the importer registers as the producer of that packaging in each country it sells in (extended producer responsibility). Fee: Varies. https://environment.ec.europa.eu/topics/waste-and-recycling/packaging-waste_en

### Restaurants in Helsinki
https://www.placetta.com/guides/helsinki/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Helsinki takes 6 filings with 5 agencies, starting with the Company registration with the Trade Register (YTJ start-up notification) and ending with the EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004). None of them has a fixed government fee, 4 fees are set by the space or the business and 2 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to grocery stores, milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Company registration with the Trade Register (YTJ start-up notification), Finnish Patent and Registration Office and Tax Administration. One start-up notification registers the company, VAT and employer status. Fee: Varies. https://www.ytj.fi
2. VAT registration with the Finnish Tax Administration, Verohallinto (Finnish Tax Administration). A company is entered in the VAT register with its start-up notification on ytj.fi, or later in MyTax; it must register once turnover passes 20,000 euros in a calendar year. Fee: Free. https://www.ytj.fi
3. Building permit for a change of use (to a restaurant), City of Helsinki, Building Control Services (rakennusvalvonta). Turning a shop, café or other premises into a restaurant, or making permit-level changes to the kitchen, ventilation, exits or fire compartments, needs a building permit, applied for in Lupapiste. Fee: Varies. https://www.hel.fi/static/rakvv/ohjeet/Ravintola_kahvila.pdf
4. Employer registration with the Finnish Tax Administration, Verohallinto (Finnish Tax Administration). A company that pays wages regularly signs up for the employer register and reports every payment of wages to the Incomes Register. Fee: Free. https://www.ytj.fi
5. Food premises notification to the city, City of Helsinki, Environmental Services (food safety unit). A restaurant or shop notifies the city of its food business four weeks before it starts, online, by email or by post, with a floor plan; the city processes it within a week. Fee: Varies. Takes: Filed four weeks before opening; processed within a week. https://www.hel.fi/en/business-and-work/apply-for-permits-and-facilities/food-business/registering-a-food-business
6. EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), European Union (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), checked by the national food inspectors. Nothing to file: every food business keeps to the hygiene rules and runs food safety procedures based on HACCP principles, which the local food inspectors check. The registration it requires is the country's own food business registration. Fee: Varies. https://food.ec.europa.eu/food-safety/biological-safety/food-hygiene_en

### Restaurants in Cork
https://www.placetta.com/guides/cork/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Cork takes 7 filings with 6 agencies, starting with the company registration with the CRO and ending with the EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004). None of them has a fixed government fee, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Company registration with the CRO, Companies Registration Office. The company is registered online through the CRO's CORE system; a foreign company opening a branch registers the branch. Fee: Varies. https://core.cro.ie
2. Tax registration with Revenue (corporation tax and VAT), Revenue (Office of the Revenue Commissioners). A new company registers online with Revenue through eRegistration, for corporation tax and, as they apply, VAT and employer PAYE. Fee: Varies. https://www.ros.ie
3. Planning permission for a change of use, Cork City Council, Planning. Development that isn't exempt, including a material change of use, needs planning permission from Cork City Council. Fee: Varies. https://www.corkcity.ie/en/council-services/services/planning/planning-application-process/
4. Fire safety certificate for a fit-out or change of use, The council's building control authority (Dublin City Council, Cork City Council fire prevention). A fire safety certificate is applied for through the national Building Control Management System before work starts on a new building, an extension, a material alteration or a change of use. Fee: Varies. https://www.gov.ie/en/dublin-city-council/services/getting-a-fire-safety-certificate/
5. Employer registration with Revenue (PAYE), Revenue (Office of the Revenue Commissioners). Before paying an employee, the company tells Revenue through MyEnquiries in ROS that it will pay staff; a company registers even if its only employees are its directors. Fee: Free. https://www.revenue.ie/en/employing-people/becoming-an-employer-and-ongoing-obligations/registration-of-employers-for-paye-purposes/index.aspx
6. Food business registration, HSE Environmental Health Service (the inspecting official agency). Before starting, a food business registers with the official agency that inspects it, and has food hygiene training, traceability and a food safety management system. Fee: Varies. https://www.fsai.ie/business-advice/starting-a-food-business
7. EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), European Union (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), checked by the national food inspectors. Nothing to file: every food business keeps to the hygiene rules and runs food safety procedures based on HACCP principles, which the local food inspectors check. The registration it requires is the country's own food business registration. Fee: Varies. https://food.ec.europa.eu/food-safety/biological-safety/food-hygiene_en

Opening a restaurant in Bern takes 6 filings with 6 agencies, starting with the Commercial register entry in the canton of Bern and ending with the Restaurant operating permit (Betriebsbewilligung Gastgewerbe). None of them has a fixed government fee and 6 fees are set by the space or the business. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Commercial register entry in the canton of Bern, Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Bern. The founding of a GmbH is recorded by a notary, who usually files the documents with the Bern commercial register office. Fee: Varies. https://www.hra.dij.be.ch/de/start/rechtsformen/gmbH.html
2. VAT registration with the Federal Tax Administration, Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung (ESTV). A business established in Switzerland is in principle liable to VAT and registers online with the ESTV once its turnover reaches the threshold. Fee: Varies. https://www.estv.admin.ch/de/mwst-steuerpflicht
3. Building permit, including a change of use, City of Bern, Bauinspektorat. A restaurant's building permit, and one for outdoor seating, is applied for with the city's building inspectorate, which publishes guidance for restaurant applications. Fee: Varies. https://www.bern.ch/themen/planen-und-bauen/baubewilligung/baugesuche-gastgewerbe-und-aussenbewirtungsflaechen
4. Employer affiliation with a compensation fund (AHV), The canton's or trade's Ausgleichskasse (AHV compensation fund). An employer joins a compensation fund for old-age and survivors' insurance contributions before paying wages. Fee: Varies. https://www.kmu.admin.ch
5. Food safety self-check review by the cantonal laboratory, Kantonales Laboratorium Bern. The restaurant's food safety self-check documentation goes to the cantonal laboratory with the operating permit application, which confirms it on the form. Fee: Varies. https://www.rsta.dij.be.ch/de/start/themen/gastgewerbe/betriebsbewilligung-gastgewerbe.html
6. Restaurant operating permit (Betriebsbewilligung Gastgewerbe), Regierungsstatthalteramt Bern-Mittelland (filed through the City of Bern). To open or take over a restaurant in the canton of Bern, the operating permit is applied for once the building permit is in hand; in the city, the form goes to the city's office, which forwards it. Fee: Varies. https://www.rsta.dij.be.ch/content/dam/rsta_dij/dokumente/de/themen/gastgewerbe/RSTA_Gesuch_Betriebsbewilligung_Gastgewerbe_de.pdf

### Restaurants in Graz
https://www.placetta.com/guides/graz/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Graz takes 6 filings with 6 agencies, starting with the company register entry (Firmenbuch) and ending with the EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004). None of them has a fixed government fee, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to grocery stores, milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Company register entry (Firmenbuch), Firmenbuchgericht (the regional court). A GmbH is founded by a notarial act and entered in the company register; the business service portal offers a simplified online route for some. Fee: Varies. https://www.usp.gv.at
2. Trade registration (Gewerbeanmeldung), Gewerbebehörde: the Bezirkshauptmannschaft, in a statutory city the Magistrat (in Vienna the Magistratisches Bezirksamt or MA 63). The trade is registered with the trade authority for the location, in person, in writing or online through the business service portal. Fee: Varies. https://www.usp.gv.at
3. Tax registration with the Finanzamt Österreich (tax number), Finanzamt Österreich (Federal Ministry of Finance). The opening of the business is reported to the Finanzamt Österreich within one month, which sends the questionnaire (Verf 15 for a company) and issues the tax number. A one-person GmbH can report it through the USP's eGründung. Fee: Varies. Takes: Within one month of opening. https://www.usp.gv.at/themen/steuern-finanzen/steuerliche-rechte-und-pflichten/pflichten-des-unternehmers.html
4. Premises use permit (Betriebsanlagengenehmigung), City of Graz, Bau- und Anlagenbehörde (Referat für gastgewerbliche Betriebsanlagen). The signed application goes to the Bau- und Anlagenbehörde on paper with three sets of technical documents and one digital copy; a restaurant is handled by the department for hospitality premises. Fee: Varies. Takes: Decided within 6 months of a complete application. https://www.graz.at/cms/beitrag/10223874/7708483
5. Employer account and staff registration with the health insurance fund (ÖGK), Österreichische Gesundheitskasse (ÖGK). Before the first hire the employer asks the ÖGK, free and online, for an employer account number, then registers every employee through ELDA before they start work. Fee: Free. Takes: Each employee is registered before starting work. https://www.usp.gv.at/themen/mitarbeiter-und-gesundheit/einstellung-mitarbeiter-und-arten-der-beschaeftigung/weitere-informationen-einstellen-von-personal/anmeldung-dienstnehmer.html
6. EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), European Union (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), checked by the national food inspectors. Nothing to file: every food business keeps to the hygiene rules and runs food safety procedures based on HACCP principles, which the local food inspectors check. The registration it requires is the country's own food business registration. Fee: Varies. https://food.ec.europa.eu/food-safety/biological-safety/food-hygiene_en

### Restaurants in Gothenburg
https://www.placetta.com/guides/gothenburg/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Gothenburg takes 6 filings with 5 agencies, starting with the company registration (Verksamt) and ending with the EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004). The fixed government fees add up to about SEK 2,400, 3 fees are set by the space or the business and 2 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to grocery stores, milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Company registration (Verksamt), Bolagsverket and Skatteverket. Register the company and for tax, VAT and as an employer in one place. Fee: SEK 2,400. https://www.verksamt.se
2. VAT and F-tax registration with Skatteverket, Skatteverket (Swedish Tax Agency). Registered on verksamt.se with the company registration, or on form SKV 4620; a business with taxable sales registers for VAT. Fee: Free. https://www.skatteverket.se/foretag/etjansterochblanketter/blanketterbroschyrer/blanketter/info/4620.4.6efe6285127ab4f1d2580003836.html
3. Building permit for a change of use, City of Gothenburg, Stadsbyggnadskontoret. Changing the use of a building, or part of one, substantially needs a building permit from the city. Fee: Varies. https://goteborg.se/wps/portal/start/bygga-bo-och-leva-hallbart/bygga-riva-och-forandra/vad-ska-du-bygga/andra-inomhus/andra-anvandning
4. Employer registration with Skatteverket, Skatteverket (Swedish Tax Agency). A company that pays wages registers as an employer through the e-service on verksamt.se, or on form SKV 4620, and then files a monthly employer return. Fee: Free. https://www.skatteverket.se/foretag/arbetsgivare/arbetsgivarregistrering/registreradig.4.18e1b10334ebe8bc80003496.html
5. Food business registration with the city, City of Gothenburg, Miljöförvaltningen. A food business is registered with the environment department before it starts or is taken over, online or on paper; a move or a new company number needs a new registration. Fee: Varies. https://goteborg.se/wps/portal/start/foretag-och-organisationer/tillstand-och-regler/salja-och-servera/livsmedel/registrera-livsmedelsverksamhet
6. EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), European Union (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), checked by the national food inspectors. Nothing to file: every food business keeps to the hygiene rules and runs food safety procedures based on HACCP principles, which the local food inspectors check. The registration it requires is the country's own food business registration. Fee: Varies. https://food.ec.europa.eu/food-safety/biological-safety/food-hygiene_en

Fee: Varies. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32023R0988
4. Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation, European Union (Regulation (EU) 2025/40), with each country's producer register for packaging. Goods imported in packaging meet the regulation's packaging requirements, and the importer registers as the producer of that packaging in each country it sells in (extended producer responsibility). Fee: Varies. https://environment.ec.europa.eu/topics/waste-and-recycling/packaging-waste_en

### Warehouses and 3PLs in Gothenburg
https://www.placetta.com/guides/gothenburg/warehouse-3pl.html
Opening a warehouse or 3PL in Gothenburg takes 5 filings with 4 agencies, starting with the company registration (Verksamt) and ending with the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation. The fixed government fees add up to about SEK 2,400, 2 fees are set by the space or the business and 2 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Company registration (Verksamt), Bolagsverket and Skatteverket. Register the company and for tax, VAT and as an employer in one place. Fee: SEK 2,400. https://www.verksamt.se
2. VAT and F-tax registration with Skatteverket, Skatteverket (Swedish Tax Agency). Registered on verksamt.se with the company registration, or on form SKV 4620; a business with taxable sales registers for VAT. Fee: Free. https://www.skatteverket.se/foretag/etjansterochblanketter/blanketterbroschyrer/blanketter/info/4620.4.6efe6285127ab4f1d2580003836.html
3. Building permit for a change of use, City of Gothenburg, Stadsbyggnadskontoret. Changing the use of a building, or part of one, substantially needs a building permit from the city. Fee: Varies. https://goteborg.se/wps/portal/start/bygga-bo-och-leva-hallbart/bygga-riva-och-forandra/vad-ska-du-bygga/andra-inomhus/andra-anvandning
4. Employer registration with Skatteverket, Skatteverket (Swedish Tax Agency). A company that pays wages registers as an employer through the e-service on verksamt.se, or on form SKV 4620, and then files a monthly employer return. Fee: Free. https://www.skatteverket.se/foretag/arbetsgivare/arbetsgivarregistrering/registreradig.4.18e1b10334ebe8bc80003496.html
5. Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation, European Union (Regulation (EU) 2025/40), with each country's producer register for packaging. Goods imported in packaging meet the regulation's packaging requirements, and the importer registers as the producer of that packaging in each country it sells in (extended producer responsibility). Fee: Varies. https://environment.ec.europa.eu/topics/waste-and-recycling/packaging-waste_en

### Restaurants in Aarhus
https://www.placetta.com/guides/aarhus/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Aarhus takes 5 filings with 4 agencies, starting with the company registration (Virk) and ending with the EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004). The fixed government fees add up to about DKK 670, 2 fees are set by the space or the business and 2 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to grocery stores, milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Company registration (Virk), Danish Business Authority. Register the company and its CVR number, VAT and employer status online. Fee: DKK 670. https://virk.dk
2. VAT registration with the Danish Tax Agency, Skattestyrelsen (Danish Tax Agency), through virk.dk. Once the company exists it registers on virk.dk for the duties that apply; a company expected to sell more than 50,000 kroner in 12 months registers for VAT. Fee: Free. https://virk.dk/integration/ERST/Startblanketten_momsregistrering_mv
3. Building permit, including a change of use, Aarhus Municipality, Byggeri. Building work or a new use of premises needs a building permit from the municipality before work starts or the use changes. Fee: Varies. https://aarhus.dk/borger/bolig-byggeri-og-miljoe/byggeri/vil-du-aendre-brugen-af-din-bygning
4. Employer registration (A-tax and labour market contribution), Skattestyrelsen (Danish Tax Agency), through virk.dk. Before paying wages the company registers as an employer on virk.dk, then reports and pays A-tax and labour market contributions every month in eIndkomst. Fee: Free. https://virk.dk/integration/ERST/Startblanketten_momsregistrering_mv
5. EU food hygiene rules (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), European Union (Regulation (EC) 852/2004), checked by the national food inspectors. Nothing to file: every food business keeps to the hygiene rules and runs food safety procedures based on HACCP principles, which the local food inspectors check. The registration it requires is the country's own food business registration. Fee: Varies. https://food.ec.europa.eu/food-safety/biological-safety/food-hygiene_en

### Restaurants in Dubai
https://www.placetta.com/guides/dubai/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Dubai takes 6 filings with 6 agencies, starting with the company formation on the mainland: trade name, initial approval and memorandum of association and ending with the food establishment approval. None of them has a fixed government fee, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to grocery stores, milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Company formation on the mainland: trade name, initial approval and memorandum of association, The emirate's economic department, under the federal Commercial Companies Law. A mainland company reserves its trade name and gets initial approval from the emirate's economic department, then signs an attested memorandum of association before the licence is issued; a free zone company forms with its free zone authority instead. Fee: Varies. https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/business/Doing-business/doing-business-on-the-mainland/steps-to-start-a-business-on-the-mainland
2. Dubai trade licence, Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism. Reserve the trade name, get initial approval, then issue the licence online through Invest in Dubai. Free zones license through their own authority instead. Fee: Varies. https://invest.dubai.ae
3. Corporate tax and VAT registration, Federal Tax Authority. Every company registers for corporate tax on EmaraTax. VAT registration is required once taxable supplies pass AED 375,000 a year. Fee: Free. https://eservices.tax.gov.ae
4. Employer registration and work permits, Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. Register the establishment, then apply for each employee's work permit. Fee: Varies. https://www.mohre.gov.ae
5. Premises zoning and lease for the licence (Dubai), Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism; Dubai Land Department (Ejari); Dubai Municipality. The premises' location must meet Dubai's economic department requirements and the municipality's land planning rules; the attested lease goes with the licence application. Fee: Varies. https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/business/Doing-business/doing-business-on-the-mainland/steps-to-start-a-business-on-the-mainland
6. Food establishment approval, Dubai Municipality, Food Safety. Food businesses get the municipality's layout approval and inspection before the licence is activated. Fee: Varies. https://www.dm.gov.ae

The premises' location must meet Sharjah's economic department requirements and the municipality's land planning rules; the attested lease goes with the licence application. Fee: Varies. https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/business/Doing-business/doing-business-on-the-mainland/steps-to-start-a-business-on-the-mainland
6. Food establishment approval before trading food, The emirate's food authority (Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority; Sharjah Municipality, Public Health). A business that trades in food needs the competent authority's prior consent before it starts; the emirate's food authority approves the premises and inspects it. Fee: Varies. https://moccae.gov.ae/assets/download/3d703379/L10-15%20Eng.pdf.aspx

### Retail stores in Sharjah
https://www.placetta.com/guides/sharjah/retail-store.html
Opening a retail store in Sharjah takes 5 filings with 5 agencies, starting with the company formation on the mainland: trade name, initial approval and memorandum of association and ending with the premises zoning and lease for the licence (Sharjah). None of them has a fixed government fee, 4 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to warehouses and 3pls, cosmetics stores and toy stores.
1. Company formation on the mainland: trade name, initial approval and memorandum of association, The emirate's economic department, under the federal Commercial Companies Law. A mainland company reserves its trade name and gets initial approval from the emirate's economic department, then signs an attested memorandum of association before the licence is issued; a free zone company forms with its free zone authority instead. Fee: Varies. https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/business/Doing-business/doing-business-on-the-mainland/steps-to-start-a-business-on-the-mainland
2. Sharjah trade licence, Sharjah Economic Development Department. Applied for online with the Sharjah economic department. Fee: Varies. https://www.sedd.ae
3. Corporate tax and VAT registration, Federal Tax Authority. Every company registers for corporate tax on EmaraTax. VAT registration is required once taxable supplies pass AED 375,000 a year. Fee: Free. https://eservices.tax.gov.ae
4. Employer registration and work permits, Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. Register the establishment, then apply for each employee's work permit. Fee: Varies. https://www.mohre.gov.ae
5. Premises zoning and lease for the licence (Sharjah), Sharjah Economic Development Department; Sharjah Municipality. The premises' location must meet Sharjah's economic department requirements and the municipality's land planning rules; the attested lease goes with the licence application. Fee: Varies. https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/business/Doing-business/doing-business-on-the-mainland/steps-to-start-a-business-on-the-mainland

### Restaurants in Riyadh
https://www.placetta.com/guides/riyadh/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Riyadh takes 6 filings with 6 agencies, starting with the foreign investment license and ending with the Civil Defense safety license. None of them has a fixed government fee, 4 fees are set by the space or the business and 2 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to retail stores, grocery stores, warehouses and 3pls, cosmetics stores, toy stores, milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Foreign investment license, Ministry of Investment (MISA). A foreign-owned business gets the investment license before the commercial registration. Fee: Varies. https://misa.gov.sa
2. Commercial registration, Ministry of Commerce, Saudi Business Center. Registered online through the Saudi Business Center. Fee: Varies. https://business.sa
3. Tax, VAT and zakat registration, Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA). Register for zakat or income tax, and for VAT once taxable supplies pass SAR 375,000 a year. E-invoicing applies. Fee: Free. https://zatca.gov.sa
4. Social insurance employer registration, General Organization for Social Insurance. Register as an employer and enroll each employee. Fee: Free. https://www.gosi.gov.sa
5. Municipal license, Ministry of Municipal and Rural Affairs and Housing (Balady). Every shop, restaurant and warehouse gets the municipal license for its premises online. Fee: Varies. https://balady.gov.sa
6. Civil Defense safety license, General Directorate of Civil Defense. Premises open to the public and warehouses get the safety license online. Fee: Varies. https://998.gov.sa

### Restaurants in Istanbul
https://www.placetta.com/guides/istanbul/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Istanbul takes 6 filings with 6 agencies, starting with the company registration (MERSİS and the trade registry) and ending with the Food business registration certificate (İşletme Kayıt Belgesi). None of them has a fixed government fee, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to grocery stores, milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Company registration (MERSİS and the trade registry), Ministry of Trade, Central Registry. Prepare the articles in MERSIS, then register with the trade registry. Fee: Varies. https://mersis.gtb.gov.tr
2. Tax registration, Revenue Administration (GİB). The tax office records the company and issues the tax number. Fee: Varies. https://www.gib.gov.tr
3. Zoning and fire compliance opinions for the premises, The district municipality's zoning department and the Istanbul Metropolitan Fire Department. With the opening licence application, the district's licensing department asks the metropolitan fire department (fire and explosion) and the municipality's zoning department (land use) for compliance opinions before the on-site inspection. Fee: Varies. https://beyoglu.bel.tr/hizmetlerimiz/basvuru-kaynaklari/isyeri-acma-ve-calisma-ruhsatlari/sihhi-muesseseler-ve-aranacak-sartlar/
4. Business opening and operating license, Istanbul district municipality. Shops and restaurants get the opening license from their district municipality, many through e-Devlet. Fee: Varies. https://beyoglu.bel.tr/hizmetlerimiz/basvuru-kaynaklari/isyeri-acma-ve-calisma-ruhsatlari/
5. Employer workplace registration with social security (SGK), Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu (SGK). An employer files the workplace registration with SGK electronically by the day it first employs an insured worker, and registers each employee's start. Fee: Free. Takes: By the day the first employee starts. https://www.sgk.gov.tr/Content/Post/3affeaef-df73-4c5b-926f-86376b4e07bf/Isyeri-Isveren-ve-Isyerinin-Bildirimi-2022-05-15-06-04-21
6. Food business registration certificate (İşletme Kayıt Belgesi), Istanbul Provincial Directorate of Agriculture and Forestry (the district directorate for the address). Shops, restaurants and stores that handle food apply to the district directorate with the registration application and declaration, and get the business registration certificate. Fee: Varies. https://istanbul.tarimorman.gov.tr/Belgeler/DepoPerakende%20ve%20Toplu%20T%C3%BCketim%20Yerleri%20Kay%C4%B1t%20%C4%B0%C5%9Flemleri%20(04.01.2023).pdf
