### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in San Francisco
https://www.placetta.com/guides/san-francisco/milk-tea-shop.html
Opening a milk tea shop in San Francisco takes 16 filings with 12 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the LLC annual tax ($800). The fixed government fees add up to about $4,068, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to coffee shops.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113947.1
6. Food handler cards for staff, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. Every employee who prepares, stores or handles food gets a California Food Handler Card from an accredited course within 30 days of hire; the card is good for 3 years. Anyone holding a valid food manager certificate is exempt. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113948
7. San Francisco Business Registration Certificate, San Francisco Office of the Treasurer and Tax Collector. Apply online, sign the DocuSign email within 15 days, then pay the fee when asked. Fee: $55. Takes: The certificate is mailed within 10 to 15 business days after payment. https://etaxstatement.sfgov.org/NewBusinessRegistration/application
8. Formula retail (chain store) affidavit, San Francisco Planning Department. A chain with 11 or more other locations worldwide files this with the building permit. Many neighborhood districts then require a Conditional Use hearing, and a few ban chains. Fee: Varies. Takes: The affidavit itself isn't reviewed separately, but where neighborhood notification is required, neighbors get 30 days to respond, and districts that need Conditional Use go to a Planning Commission hearing. https://sfplanning.org/resource/formula-retail-establishments
9. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
10. Food facility plan check, San Francisco Department of Public Health. Filed with the building permit at the Permit Center, with health as a review station: the application, plans and the review fee. Fee: $2,207. Takes: DPH doesn't publish a plan review time, but asks you to contact your plan reviewer at least 2 weeks ahead to book the pre-final and final site inspections. https://sf.gov/sites/default/files/2023-07/PlanCheckApplication.pdf
11. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
12. Building permit for a tenant improvement, San Francisco Department of Building Inspection. Submit plans and the application at the Permit Center, which routes it to Planning, Fire and Health. Fee: Varies. Takes: Eligible small businesses opening a new business can get a 30-day review once the application is complete. https://www.sf.gov/step-by-step--get-otc-permit-your-commercial-project/
13. Health permit to operate a food facility, San Francisco Department of Public Health. Apply online at least six weeks before opening, with your business account, location ID and federal tax ID, once a certified food safety manager is on staff. Fee: $470. Takes: Apply for the health permit at least 1 month before you open. https://sf.gov/get-health-permit-open-restaurant-bar-or-other-retail-food-location
14. Sign and awning permit, San Francisco Department of Building Inspection. Online only through PermitSF since June 29, 2026 (Forms 4 and 7 retired): submit drawings, answer plan review, pay, then book the final inspection. Lit signs also need an electrical permit. Fee: Varies. Takes: DBI doesn't publish a review time for sign or awning permits; you apply online with construction drawings, and the sign must meet the zoning rules for your district. https://sf.gov/step-by-step/get-permit-install-sign-or-awning
15. Fire Department place of assembly permit, San Francisco Fire Department. For dining rooms above the assembly occupant load: file with the Fire Prevention permits section, which inspects before issuing. Fee: $446. Takes: Fire permit applications must be submitted at least 5 working days before the activity or operation starts. https://sf-fire.org/permits
16. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
What's different for a milk tea shop in San Francisco:
- Under California's food code, a food facility in a building built after January 1, 2004 that gives customers space to eat or drink on the premises must provide clean restrooms for them. The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-22)

A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113947.1
6. Food handler cards for staff, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. Every employee who prepares, stores or handles food gets a California Food Handler Card from an accredited course within 30 days of hire; the card is good for 3 years. Anyone holding a valid food manager certificate is exempt. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113948
7. San Francisco Business Registration Certificate, San Francisco Office of the Treasurer and Tax Collector. Apply online, sign the DocuSign email within 15 days, then pay the fee when asked. Fee: $55. Takes: The certificate is mailed within 10 to 15 business days after payment. https://etaxstatement.sfgov.org/NewBusinessRegistration/application
8. Formula retail (chain store) affidavit, San Francisco Planning Department. A chain with 11 or more other locations worldwide files this with the building permit. Many neighborhood districts then require a Conditional Use hearing, and a few ban chains. Fee: Varies. Takes: The affidavit itself isn't reviewed separately, but where neighborhood notification is required, neighbors get 30 days to respond, and districts that need Conditional Use go to a Planning Commission hearing. https://sfplanning.org/resource/formula-retail-establishments
9. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
10. Food facility plan check, San Francisco Department of Public Health. Filed with the building permit at the Permit Center, with health as a review station: the application, plans and the review fee. Fee: $2,207. Takes: DPH doesn't publish a plan review time, but asks you to contact your plan reviewer at least 2 weeks ahead to book the pre-final and final site inspections. https://sf.gov/sites/default/files/2023-07/PlanCheckApplication.pdf
11. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
12. Building permit for a tenant improvement, San Francisco Department of Building Inspection. Submit plans and the application at the Permit Center, which routes it to Planning, Fire and Health. Fee: Varies. Takes: Eligible small businesses opening a new business can get a 30-day review once the application is complete. https://www.sf.gov/step-by-step--get-otc-permit-your-commercial-project/
13. Health permit to operate a food facility, San Francisco Department of Public Health. Apply online at least six weeks before opening, with your business account, location ID and federal tax ID, once a certified food safety manager is on staff. Fee: $470. Takes: Apply for the health permit at least 1 month before you open. https://sf.gov/get-health-permit-open-restaurant-bar-or-other-retail-food-location
14. Sign and awning permit, San Francisco Department of Building Inspection. Online only through PermitSF since June 29, 2026 (Forms 4 and 7 retired): submit drawings, answer plan review, pay, then book the final inspection. Lit signs also need an electrical permit. Fee: Varies. Takes: DBI doesn't publish a review time for sign or awning permits; you apply online with construction drawings, and the sign must meet the zoning rules for your district. https://sf.gov/step-by-step/get-permit-install-sign-or-awning
15. Fire Department place of assembly permit, San Francisco Fire Department. For dining rooms above the assembly occupant load: file with the Fire Prevention permits section, which inspects before issuing. Fee: $446. Takes: Fire permit applications must be submitted at least 5 working days before the activity or operation starts. https://sf-fire.org/permits
16. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/

### Bakeries in San Francisco

3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf

What's different for a bakery in San Francisco:
- Under California's food code, a food facility in a building built after January 1, 2004 that gives customers space to eat or drink on the premises must provide clean restrooms for them. The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-22)
- California's Processed Food Registration, from the Department of Public Health, covers bakery products. A retail food facility that sells directly to consumers under a county health permit is exempt, so a bakery selling only over its own counter doesn't need it; making goods for other stores or cafes falls outside that exemption. California Department of Public Health: "General foods such as bakery products, noodles, seafood (except molluscan shellfish)" https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CEH/DFDCS/Pages/FDBPrograms/FoodSafetyProgram/PFRFAQs.aspx (read 2026-10-21)

### Cosmetics stores in San Francisco
https://www.placetta.com/guides/san-francisco/cosmetics-store.html
Opening a cosmetics store in San Francisco takes 17 filings with 14 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the proposition 65 warning labels. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf

9. Packaging producer registration (EPR), CalRecycle, through Circular Action Alliance. A producer of packaged goods sold in California applies to participate in Circular Action Alliance's plan, submits an independent producer application, or obtains a small producer exemption; CalRecycle's PEPRS portal or the PRO takes the registration and the reports. Fee: Varies. https://calrecycle.ca.gov/packaging/packaging-epr/producerguidance/
10. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling

7. Children's Product Certificate, from a CPSC-accepted lab's tests, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). Children's furniture is tested by a third-party, CPSC-accepted laboratory to the children's product safety rules that apply, and the importer issues the certificate, with its test reports, in English, citing each rule. Since July 8, 2026 most certificates are eFiled with CBP at entry, so it is ready before the goods ship. There is no government form. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Testing-Certification/Childrens-Product-Certificate-CPC
8. Packaging producer registration (EPR), CalRecycle, through Circular Action Alliance. A producer of packaged goods sold in California applies to participate in Circular Action Alliance's plan, submits an independent producer application, or obtains a small producer exemption; CalRecycle's PEPRS portal or the PRO takes the registration and the reports. Fee: Varies. https://calrecycle.ca.gov/packaging/packaging-epr/producerguidance/
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. San Francisco Business Registration Certificate, San Francisco Office of the Treasurer and Tax Collector. Apply online, sign the DocuSign email within 15 days, then pay the fee when asked. Fee: $55. Takes: The certificate is mailed within 10 to 15 business days after payment. https://etaxstatement.sfgov.org/NewBusinessRegistration/application
11. Formula retail (chain store) affidavit, San Francisco Planning Department. A chain with 11 or more other locations worldwide files this with the building permit. Many neighborhood districts then require a Conditional Use hearing, and a few ban chains. Fee: Varies. Takes: The affidavit itself isn't reviewed separately, but where neighborhood notification is required, neighbors get 30 days to respond, and districts that need Conditional Use go to a Planning Commission hearing. https://sfplanning.org/resource/formula-retail-establishments
12. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
13. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
14. Sign and awning permit, San Francisco Department of Building Inspection. Online only through PermitSF since June 29, 2026 (Forms 4 and 7 retired): submit drawings, answer plan review, pay, then book the final inspection. Lit signs also need an electrical permit. Fee: Varies. Takes: DBI doesn't publish a review time for sign or awning permits; you apply online with construction drawings, and the sign must meet the zoning rules for your district. https://sf.gov/step-by-step/get-permit-install-sign-or-awning
15. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
16. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. Takes: Nothing is filed with or approved by OEHHA, so there's no processing time; the business decides whether a warning is needed and must have it in place itself. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses

### Importers and online sellers in San Francisco
https://www.placetta.com/guides/san-francisco/importer-ecommerce.html
Opening an importer or e-commerce seller in San Francisco takes 12 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the proposition 65 warning labels. The fixed government fees add up to about $945, 2 fees are set by the space or the business and 6 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
8. Packaging producer registration (EPR), CalRecycle, through Circular Action Alliance. A producer of packaged goods sold in California applies to participate in Circular Action Alliance's plan, submits an independent producer application, or obtains a small producer exemption; CalRecycle's PEPRS portal or the PRO takes the registration and the reports. Fee: Varies. https://calrecycle.ca.gov/packaging/packaging-epr/producerguidance/
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. San Francisco Business Registration Certificate, San Francisco Office of the Treasurer and Tax Collector. Apply online, sign the DocuSign email within 15 days, then pay the fee when asked. Fee: $55. Takes: The certificate is mailed within 10 to 15 business days after payment. https://etaxstatement.sfgov.org/NewBusinessRegistration/application
11. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
12. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. Takes: Nothing is filed with or approved by OEHHA, so there's no processing time; the business decides whether a warning is needed and must have it in place itself. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in San Jose
https://www.placetta.com/guides/san-jose/milk-tea-shop.html
Opening a milk tea shop in San Jose takes 16 filings with 12 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the LLC annual tax ($800). The fixed government fees add up to about $1,335, 9 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to coffee shops.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113947.1
6. Food handler cards for staff, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. Every employee who prepares, stores or handles food gets a California Food Handler Card from an accredited course within 30 days of hire; the card is good for 3 years. Anyone holding a valid food manager certificate is exempt. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113948
7. City of San José Business Tax Certificate, City of San José Finance Department. Register online within 90 days of starting business in San José, with the owner, tax ID, location and, if you have them, the seller's permit and county health permit numbers. Fee: Varies. Takes: If you pay during registration, the account activates in 2 to 3 business days; otherwise the invoice is mailed within 5 to 10 business days. https://www.sanjoseca.gov/your-government/departments-offices/finance/business-tax-registration/register-for-a-business-tax-certificate
8. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
9. Food facility plan check, County of Santa Clara Department of Environmental Health. Email the application, scaled plans, menu and equipment sheets to dehplancheck@deh.sccgov.org, then pay the invoiced review fee. The city needs the county's stamped plans before its own plan check. Fee: Varies. Takes: After payment, inspector review may take up to 20 business days. https://deh.santaclaracounty.gov/food-and-retail/compliance-retail-food-operations/submit-plan-review-restaurants-grocery-stores-and
10. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
11. Building permit for a tenant improvement, City of San José Building Division. Apply on SJPermits.org, upload plans through SJePlans and pay the plan review fee before review starts. Restaurants can use the city's Streamlined Restaurant Program. Fee: Varies. Takes: San José's standard plan review for a commercial tenant improvement takes about 10 working days for the first round and 5 working days for each recheck. https://www.sjpermits.org
12. Fire protection system permit, San José Fire Department, Bureau of Fire Prevention. When plan check calls for it, apply on SJPermits.org under Fire Prevention, pay, then upload documents in SJePlans. Fee: Varies. Takes: Fire Department review of fire protection system plans takes about 10 working days for the first round and 5 working days for each recheck on a commercial project. https://www.sjpermits.org
13. Building final inspection, City of San José Building Division. Schedule the final on SJPermits.org once every other inspection on the permit has passed. Fee: Varies. Takes: San José doesn't publish a wait time for the final inspection; you request it on SJPermits.org, and it's approved only after every other inspection on the permit has passed. https://www.sjpermits.org
14. Health permit to operate a food facility, County of Santa Clara Department of Environmental Health. Submit the permit application by email or in person at or before the final inspection; the operating fee is invoiced after the final. Fee: Varies. Takes: The county's plan review can take up to 20 business days, and the invoice for the operating permit is sent after the final inspection passes. https://deh.santaclaracounty.gov/food-and-retail/compliance-retail-food-operations/submit-plan-review-restaurants-grocery-stores-and
15. Sign permit, City of San José Planning Division. Upload the signed application to SJPermits.org, then pay the invoice. Fee: $445. Takes: Average: 2 weeks. https://www.sanjoseca.gov/business/development-services-permit-center/online-permits-at-sjpermits-org/planning-online-permits
16. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
What's different for a milk tea shop in San Jose:
- Under California's food code, a food facility in a building built after January 1, 2004 that gives customers space to eat or drink on the premises must provide clean restrooms for them. The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-22)

Submit the permit application by email or in person at or before the final inspection; the operating fee is invoiced after the final. Fee: Varies. Takes: The county's plan review can take up to 20 business days, and the invoice for the operating permit is sent after the final inspection passes. https://deh.santaclaracounty.gov/food-and-retail/compliance-retail-food-operations/submit-plan-review-restaurants-grocery-stores-and
15. Sign permit, City of San José Planning Division. Upload the signed application to SJPermits.org, then pay the invoice. Fee: $445. Takes: Average: 2 weeks. https://www.sanjoseca.gov/business/development-services-permit-center/online-permits-at-sjpermits-org/planning-online-permits
16. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
What's different for a bakery in San Jose:
- Under California's food code, a food facility in a building built after January 1, 2004 that gives customers space to eat or drink on the premises must provide clean restrooms for them. The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-22)
- California's Processed Food Registration, from the Department of Public Health, covers bakery products. A retail food facility that sells directly to consumers under a county health permit is exempt, so a bakery selling only over its own counter doesn't need it; making goods for other stores or cafes falls outside that exemption. California Department of Public Health: "General foods such as bakery products, noodles, seafood (except molluscan shellfish)" https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CEH/DFDCS/Pages/FDBPrograms/FoodSafetyProgram/PFRFAQs.aspx (read 2026-10-21)

### Grocery stores in San Jose
https://www.placetta.com/guides/san-jose/grocery-store.html
Opening a grocery store in San Jose takes 11 filings with 10 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the proposition 65 warning labels. The fixed government fees add up to about $1,335, 3 fees are set by the space or the business and 4 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. City of San José Business Tax Certificate, City of San José Finance Department. Register online within 90 days of starting business in San José, with the owner, tax ID, location and, if you have them, the seller's permit and county health permit numbers. Fee: Varies. Takes: If you pay during registration, the account activates in 2 to 3 business days; otherwise the invoice is mailed within 5 to 10 business days. https://www.sanjoseca.gov/your-government/departments-offices/finance/business-tax-registration/register-for-a-business-tax-certificate
6. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
7. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
8. Health permit to operate a food facility, County of Santa Clara Department of Environmental Health. Submit the permit application by email or in person at or before the final inspection; the operating fee is invoiced after the final. Fee: Varies. Takes: The county's plan review can take up to 20 business days, and the invoice for the operating permit is sent after the final inspection passes. https://deh.santaclaracounty.gov/food-and-retail/compliance-retail-food-operations/submit-plan-review-restaurants-grocery-stores-and
9. Sign permit, City of San José Planning Division. Upload the signed application to SJPermits.org, then pay the invoice. Fee: $445. Takes: Average: 2 weeks. https://www.sanjoseca.gov/business/development-services-permit-center/online-permits-at-sjpermits-org/planning-online-permits
10. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
11. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. Takes: Nothing is filed with or approved by OEHHA, so there's no processing time; the business decides whether a warning is needed and must have it in place itself. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses

Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
12. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/

### Restaurants in Chicago
https://www.placetta.com/guides/chicago/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Chicago takes 9 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the chicago retail food establishment license. None of them has a fixed government fee, 8 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants and dessert shops.
1. LLC formation, Illinois Secretary of State. Form the LLC online, or register a company formed in another state to do business in Illinois. Fee: Varies. https://www.ilsos.gov
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Illinois business registration (sales tax), Illinois Department of Revenue. Register before your first purchase, sale or hire: online in MyTax Illinois (Register a New Business, Form REG-1), by mail or at an IDOR office. You get a certificate of registration and a taxpayer ID; Chicago's food license application asks for the Illinois Business Tax number. Fee: Varies. Takes: About 1 to 2 business days online; 4 to 6 weeks on paper. https://mytax.illinois.gov/
4. Chicago food service sanitation certificate, Chicago Department of Public Health, Food Protection Program. A person in charge holding this Public Health certificate must be on site whenever food that needs temperature control is prepared, held or served. Pass an approved course, or apply for reciprocity with a valid ANSI-accredited food protection manager certificate. A place selling only prepackaged food doesn't need one. Fee: Varies. https://chicago.gov/city/en/depts/cdph/provdrs/food_safety/svcs/enroll_in_a_foodsanitationcertificationcourse.html
5. Building permit for the interior alteration, Chicago Department of Buildings. Nonstructural interior alterations up to 2,000 square feet can use the Express Permit Program. Fee: Varies. https://chicago.gov/city/en/sites/guide-to-building-permits/home/instructions/EPP/INTWK-alteration.html
6. Unemployment insurance employer registration, Illinois Department of Employment Security. A new business registers with IDES within 30 days of starting, online through MyTax Illinois or on the paper REG-UI-1 form. Fee: Varies. https://mytax.illinois.gov/
7. Food establishment plan review, Chicago Department of Public Health, with the Department of Buildings. For new construction or a rehab, a city health sanitarian reviews the plans as part of the building permit application, coordinated between Public Health and Buildings. Public Health isn't on E-Plan and doesn't review plans filed under the self-certification program. Fee: Varies. https://www.chicago.gov/content/dam/city/depts/bacp/general/Retail%20Food%20Guide.pdf
8. Workers' compensation insurance, Illinois Workers' Compensation Commission. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://iwcc.illinois.gov/about/insurance.html
9. Chicago retail food establishment license, City of Chicago, Business Affairs and Consumer Protection, with the Department of Public Health. Chicago's business license for any fixed place that serves, stores or sells perishable food, at a properly zoned, non-residential address. Apply online or at the Small Business Center, City Hall, 121 N. LaSalle St., Room 800, with the lease, Illinois Business Tax number, FEIN, ownership details and photo ID; the place must pass a public health inspection before the license is issued. Fee: Varies. Takes: Chicago doesn't publish a standard processing time; the license is issued after zoning approval, payment and any required inspections, then mailed to your business. https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/bacp/supp_info/retailfoodestablishment0.html

https://www.placetta.com/guides/chicago/cosmetics-store.html
Opening a cosmetics store in Chicago takes 11 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the workers' compensation insurance. The fixed government fees add up to about $250, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 5 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation, Illinois Secretary of State. Form the LLC online, or register a company formed in another state to do business in Illinois. Fee: Varies. https://www.ilsos.gov
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Takes: About 1 to 2 business days online; 4 to 6 weeks on paper. https://mytax.illinois.gov/
4. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Chicago limited business license, City of Chicago, Business Affairs and Consumer Protection. The license for general retail sales and services in Chicago, at a properly zoned address; apply online or at the Small Business Center in City Hall. Fee: $250. https://chicago.gov/city/en/sites/chicago-business-licensing/home/business-licensing.html

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Seattle
https://www.placetta.com/guides/seattle/milk-tea-shop.html
Opening a milk tea shop in Seattle takes 8 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the food service business permit. The fixed government fees add up to about $83, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation, Washington Secretary of State, Corporations. Form the company or register a foreign company online. Fee: Varies. https://ccfs.sos.wa.gov
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Washington business license (state tax registration), Washington Department of Revenue, Business Licensing Service. File online in My DOR, or by mail. It gives the business its UBI number and tax registration, registers trade names and city and state endorsements, and passes your details to Employment Security and Labor and Industries, which open the unemployment insurance and workers' comp accounts. Fee: Varies. Takes: About 10 business days; city or state endorsements can add another 2 to 3 weeks. https://secure.dor.wa.gov/home
4. Food worker cards for staff, Washington State Department of Health, with local health departments. Everyone who works with unpackaged food, food equipment or utensils takes the state training and exam, online only at foodworkercard.wa.gov or through a local health department. A new worker may start before getting the card, for up to 14 days, if the employer gives food safety training. Fee: $10. https://www.foodworkercard.wa.gov
5. Seattle business license tax certificate, City of Seattle Finance, License and Tax Administration. Apply online through FileLocal once the business has its Washington UBI number, or mail the paper application with payment. A physical business location is required; a P.O. box doesn't count. Fee: $73. Takes: Online, the license can usually be printed 2 to 3 business days after payment; by mail it takes one to six weeks. https://www.filelocal-wa.gov/Default_FileLocal.aspx
6. Food establishment plan review, Public Health, Seattle and King County. Plans are reviewed before construction, remodeling or a change of owner. Apply and pay in the Public Health Permit Center with the site plan, menu, floor plan, equipment list with make and model, the plan review questionnaire, the finish schedule and the seating layout. Fee: Varies. Takes: An initial review may take up to 8 to 10 weeks at current volumes. https://kingcounty.gov/en/dept/dph/certificates-permits-licenses/food-business-permits/permanent-food-plan-review
7. Construction permit for the tenant improvement, Seattle Department of Construction and Inspections. Land use, construction and trade permits for the space come from SDCI; final inspections are scheduled once every permit is approved and the work is done. Fee: Varies. https://www.seattle.gov/sdci
8. Food service business permit, Public Health, Seattle and King County. Once plan review is approved, submit the application to operate in the Public Health Permit Center, pay the operating fee and book the pre-operational inspection at least a week before opening. Opening without that inspection can mean closure and a fee of half the yearly permit. Every employee needs a Washington food worker card. Fee: Varies. Takes: Book the pre-operational inspection at least 1 week before opening. https://kingcounty.gov/en/dept/dph/certificates-permits-licenses/food-business-permits/permanent-food-business-permit
What's different for a milk tea shop in Seattle:
- King County sets the risk category by the menu: drinks made only from commercially packaged products are Category 1 (low), but using Time as a Public Health Control, holding a food out of temperature control for a set time, makes it Category 3 (high), with two routine inspections a year. Public Health – Seattle & King County: "Using Time as a Public Health Control" https://cdn.kingcounty.gov/-/media/king-county/depts/dph/documents/certificates-permits-licenses/food-worker-business-permits/permanent-businesses/food-establishment-risk-levels.pdf?rev=fa5058bfe2344c0da374012f74cac082&hash=6343EB80E0FD05EB643F9899D4DA212D (read 2026-10-22)

### Coffee shops in Seattle
https://www.placetta.com/guides/seattle/coffee-shop.html
Opening a coffee shop in Seattle takes 8 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the food service business permit. The fixed government fees add up to about $83, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation, Washington Secretary of State, Corporations. Form the company or register a foreign company online. Fee: Varies. https://ccfs.sos.wa.gov
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Washington business license (state tax registration), Washington Department of Revenue, Business Licensing Service. File online in My DOR, or by mail. It gives the business its UBI number and tax registration, registers trade names and city and state endorsements, and passes your details to Employment Security and Labor and Industries, which open the unemployment insurance and workers' comp accounts. Fee: Varies. Takes: About 10 business days; city or state endorsements can add another 2 to 3 weeks. https://secure.dor.wa.gov/home
4. Food worker cards for staff, Washington State Department of Health, with local health departments. Everyone who works with unpackaged food, food equipment or utensils takes the state training and exam, online only at foodworkercard.wa.gov or through a local health department. A new worker may start before getting the card, for up to 14 days, if the employer gives food safety training. Fee: $10. https://www.foodworkercard.wa.gov
5. Seattle business license tax certificate, City of Seattle Finance, License and Tax Administration. Apply online through FileLocal once the business has its Washington UBI number, or mail the paper application with payment. A physical business location is required; a P.O. box doesn't count. Fee: $73. Takes: Online, the license can usually be printed 2 to 3 business days after payment; by mail it takes one to six weeks. https://www.filelocal-wa.gov/Default_FileLocal.aspx
6. Food establishment plan review, Public Health, Seattle and King County. Plans are reviewed before construction, remodeling or a change of owner. Apply and pay in the Public Health Permit Center with the site plan, menu, floor plan, equipment list with make and model, the plan review questionnaire, the finish schedule and the seating layout. Fee: Varies. Takes: An initial review may take up to 8 to 10 weeks at current volumes. https://kingcounty.gov/en/dept/dph/certificates-permits-licenses/food-business-permits/permanent-food-plan-review
7. Construction permit for the tenant improvement, Seattle Department of Construction and Inspections. Land use, construction and trade permits for the space come from SDCI; final inspections are scheduled once every permit is approved and the work is done. Fee: Varies. https://www.seattle.gov/sdci
8. Food service business permit, Public Health, Seattle and King County. Once plan review is approved, submit the application to operate in the Public Health Permit Center, pay the operating fee and book the pre-operational inspection at least a week before opening. Opening without that inspection can mean closure and a fee of half the yearly permit. Every employee needs a Washington food worker card. Fee: Varies. Takes: Book the pre-operational inspection at least 1 week before opening. https://kingcounty.gov/en/dept/dph/certificates-permits-licenses/food-business-permits/permanent-food-business-permit
What's different for a coffee shop in Seattle:
- King County puts a coffee shop in risk Category 1 (low), with one routine inspection a year, when it prepares espresso and blended drinks from commercially packaged products. Cooking or baking on site moves it up a category. Public Health – Seattle & King County: "Scooping ice cream, preparing espresso and/or blended drinks with commercially packaged products." https://cdn.kingcounty.gov/-/media/king-county/depts/dph/documents/certificates-permits-licenses/food-worker-business-permits/permanent-businesses/food-establishment-risk-levels.pdf?rev=fa5058bfe2344c0da374012f74cac082&hash=6343EB80E0FD05EB643F9899D4DA212D (read 2026-10-22)

Opening a cosmetics store in Seattle takes 9 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the seattle business license tax certificate. The fixed government fees add up to about $73, 3 fees are set by the space or the business and 5 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation, Washington Secretary of State, Corporations. Form the company or register a foreign company online. Fee: Varies. https://ccfs.sos.wa.gov
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf

Fee: Varies. Takes: About 10 business days; city or state endorsements can add another 2 to 3 weeks. https://secure.dor.wa.gov/home
4. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Seattle business license tax certificate, City of Seattle Finance, License and Tax Administration. Apply online through FileLocal once the business has its Washington UBI number, or mail the paper application with payment. A physical business location is required; a P.O. box doesn't count. Fee: $73. Takes: Online, the license can usually be printed 2 to 3 business days after payment; by mail it takes one to six weeks. https://www.filelocal-wa.gov/Default_FileLocal.aspx

Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
7. Seattle business license tax certificate, City of Seattle Finance, License and Tax Administration. Apply online through FileLocal once the business has its Washington UBI number, or mail the paper application with payment. A physical business location is required; a P.O. box doesn't count. Fee: $73. Takes: Online, the license can usually be printed 2 to 3 business days after payment; by mail it takes one to six weeks. https://www.filelocal-wa.gov/Default_FileLocal.aspx
8. Hazardous materials registration, Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (DOT). Filed online when you ship or offer certain hazardous materials in bulk, such as large lithium battery shipments. Fee: Varies. https://hazmatonline.phmsa.dot.gov/services/

### Restaurants in Boston
https://www.placetta.com/guides/boston/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Boston takes 14 filings with 10 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the food service permit. The fixed government fees add up to about $565, 9 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. LLC formation, Secretary of the Commonwealth, Corporations Division. Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: $500. https://www.sec.state.ma.us
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Sales tax registration, Massachusetts Department of Revenue. Register for sales tax and withholding before trading. Fee: Free. Takes: DOR doesn't publish how long registration takes; once approved, it mails a registration certificate for each location. https://mtc.dor.state.ma.us
4. Certified food protection manager, Massachusetts Department of Public Health, Food Protection Program. At least one manager on staff passes a food protection manager exam from a nationally accredited provider that Massachusetts accepts; a backup person in charge covers when they're away. Boston asks for the certificate with the food service permit application. Fee: Varies. https://www.mass.gov/doc/massachusetts-food-protection-manager-certification-exam-and-trainer-directory-1/download
5. Allergen awareness certificate, Massachusetts Department of Public Health, Food Protection Program. The person in charge, who must be on site whenever the place is open, and the backup who covers for them take an allergen awareness course and train the staff. Places that cook, prepare or serve food to eat right away need it; Boston asks for the certificate before the opening inspection. Fee: Varies. https://www.mass.gov/lists/food-allergen-awareness-guidance
6. Boston business certificate (DBA), City of Boston, City Clerk. Needed when the business trades under a name other than its legal name. Bring the notarized form, the signed lease and photo ID to City Hall, Room 601 (the clerk notarizes free), or mail them with a check; there is no online filing. An LLC or corporation registers with the Secretary of the Commonwealth first. Fee: $65. Takes: Issued while you wait in person; 2 to 3 business days by mail. https://www.boston.gov/sites/default/files/file/2025/03/2025-New-Business-Certificate-Form_0.pdf
7. Employer registration for unemployment insurance, Massachusetts Department of Unemployment Assistance. Employers who pay wages for work done in Massachusetts register with DUA online: open Unemployment Services for Employers without logging in and choose Register your Business. Fee: Free. https://www.mass.gov/how-to/register-a-business-with-the-department-of-unemployment-assistance
8. Food establishment plan review, City of Boston Inspectional Services, Health Division. Needed to build a new place, renovate, change the layout, or add equipment or processes the menu calls for. Book the in-person review with ISD Health (617-635-5326, ISDHealth@boston.gov) and bring the worksheet, two scaled floor plans, NSF or UL equipment specs and the menu; then take the stamped plans to ISD's Building Division for the building permits. Fee: Varies. https://www.boston.gov/sites/default/files/file/2021/05/FSPLAN%20REVIEW%20fillable%205%2013%20FINAL.pdf
9. Workers' compensation insurance, Massachusetts Department of Industrial Accidents. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://www.mass.gov/info-details/workers-compensation-insurance-requirements
10. Building permit for the build-out, City of Boston Inspectional Services. A Long Form permit for major construction or structural change, a Short Form for minor work; only licensed contractors apply. The health plan review comes first, and the building, plumbing, gas, electrical and mechanical permits follow it. Fee: Varies. https://www.boston.gov/departments/inspectional-services
11. Common Victualler License, City of Boston Licensing Board. Needed to sell food made to order at a fixed place, seated or takeout. File on the Licensing Board's online form with the lease, a floor plan, each owner's personal information form and the wage theft form, once the Certificate of Occupancy is in hand. A new address, or hours outside 6 a.m. to 11 p.m., goes to a public hearing after the neighborhood process. ISD issues the food service permit only after this license. Fee: Varies. Takes: About 2 to 3 weeks; when a public hearing is needed, several weeks from filing to the hearing. https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScp721MuqsSIAPeryi7VN7cdMEH4cXgnY2MAze5iM3LSrDCcw/viewform?usp=sf_link
12. Site cleanliness license, City of Boston Inspectional Services. Listed with the Common Victualler License among the approvals Boston's restaurant guide asks for before the food service permit; it covers how the place keeps its trash and dumpsters. Fee: Varies. https://www.boston.gov/departments/inspectional-services
13. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Boston Inspectional Services. Required before opening; Boston's guide accepts a Certificate of Inspection (with the Fire Department's capacity approval) in its place. Either one must be in hand before the health inspection. Fee: Varies. https://www.boston.gov/departments/inspectional-services
14. Food service permit, City of Boston Inspectional Services, Health Division. Email the application (with its workers' comp affidavit), the EIN and the food protection manager certificate to ISDHealth@boston.gov, or bring them to 1010 Massachusetts Ave, 4th floor. Before the opening inspection, which you book a few days ahead, have the allergen certificate, Certificate of Occupancy, Common Victualler License and paid fees ready. Fee: Varies. Takes: 1 to 2 business days when the space isn't changing; after a build-out, the inspection is usually done within 1 business day of proof of every other approval. https://www.boston.gov/sites/default/files/file/2026/07/%28English%29%20Food%20Establishment%20Permit%20Application%20updated-combined.pdf

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Miami
https://www.placetta.com/guides/miami/milk-tea-shop.html
Opening a milk tea shop in Miami takes 12 filings with 10 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the Miami-Dade County local business tax receipt. The fixed government fees add up to about $175, 8 fees are set by the space or the business and 2 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation, Florida Division of Corporations (Sunbiz). Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: $125. https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Florida sales tax and reemployment tax registration, Florida Department of Revenue. Register online before you start doing business. The same application covers sales and use tax and reemployment tax, Florida's unemployment tax for employers. Fee: Varies. Takes: After registering online, the certificate number is available on the website after three business days. https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/registration
4. Registration of a fictitious name (DBA), Florida Department of State, Division of Corporations. Needed before doing business under any name other than the legal name. Advertise the name once in a newspaper in the county, then register online at Sunbiz or mail the form with the fee. Fee: $50. https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/start-business/efile/fl-fictitious-name-registration/
5. Certified food protection manager, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Food managers complete training and pass a certification exam from an accredited program within 30 days of starting the job, and the restaurant shows proof whenever an inspector asks. Fee: Varies. https://www2.myfloridalicense.com/hotels-restaurants/food-lodging/food-manager/
6. Food service plan review, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Required for a space that is newly built, remodeled, converted from another use or reopening after 18 months closed; the state recommends approval before construction. Submit the plan with labeled equipment and a sample menu together with the new license application on DBPR Online. Fee: Free. https://www.myfloridalicense.com/intentions2.asp?chBoard=true&SID=&boardid=200&professionid=2010
7. Workers' compensation insurance, Florida Department of Financial Services, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://www.myfloridacfo.com/division/wc/employer/coverage-requirements
8. Certificate of Occupancy or Completion after the build-out, City of Miami Building Department. A new building, or one that has undergone construction, shows its CO or CC to get the Certificate of Use. Fee: Varies. https://www.miami.gov/Business/New-Business-Guide
9. City of Miami CU (use approval), City of Miami, Office of Zoning. For a business opening or moving in the city, applied for online only through MiamiBiz once construction is done (with the certificate of occupancy or completion for new or renovated space). After the $50 fee, pass the DERM, fire and code inspections, plus Health or DBPR for food, within 90 working days of starting the application. Fee: Varies. Takes: The city contacts you within five business days of applying and paying. https://apps.miami.gov/MiamiBizIntake
10. Florida public food service license, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Apply and pay on DBPR Online, one license for each operation. Once the plan review requirements are met, call 850-487-1395 several business days before opening to book the opening inspection; serve nobody until it passes and a temporary paper license is issued on the spot. Fee: Varies. Takes: Most applications are processed within a few business days; mailed ones take longer. https://www.myfloridalicense.com/intentions2.asp?chBoard=true&SID=&boardid=200&professionid=2010
11. City of Miami business tax receipt, City of Miami. Every business operating in the city needs one, after its Certificate of Use. Apply online with the EIN and, for a restaurant, the state food service license; the city emails an invoice, and the interim receipt comes by email once it's paid. A Miami-Dade County receipt is needed as well. Fee: Varies. Takes: The city doesn't publish how long approval takes; the interim receipt is emailed after payment. https://us.openforms.com/Form/98a6acf3-a616-4139-857d-68f4d9a4e51e
12. Miami-Dade County local business tax receipt, Miami-Dade County Tax Collector. Needed for each place of business in the county, and inside a city on top of the city's receipt. Apply online in BTExpress after completing the attestation that the business doesn't trade with Cuba in violation of federal law. Fee: Varies. Takes: Allow up to three business days after the attestation for the receipt to be ready to print. https://county-taxes.net/fl-miamidade/btexpress
What's different for a milk tea shop in Miami:
- Florida's Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS) permits coffee shops and juice and smoothie bars, and DBPR licenses restaurants and fast food. Neither names tea shops, so Odelia confirms which one licenses yours before anything is filed. Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services: "These food establishments may include supermarkets, grocery stores, convenience stores, coffee shops, bakeries, retail meat markets, retail seafood markets, juice and smoothie bars," https://www.fdacs.gov/Business-Services/Food/Food-Establishments/Retail-Food-Establishment-Permit (read 2026-10-22)

### Cosmetics stores in Miami
https://www.placetta.com/guides/miami/cosmetics-store.html
Opening a cosmetics store in Miami takes 13 filings with 11 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the Miami-Dade County local business tax receipt. The fixed government fees add up to about $175, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 5 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation, Florida Division of Corporations (Sunbiz). Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: $125. https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Florida sales tax and reemployment tax registration, Florida Department of Revenue. Register online before you start doing business. The same application covers sales and use tax and reemployment tax, Florida's unemployment tax for employers. Fee: Varies. 4. Registration of a fictitious name (DBA), Florida Department of State, Division of Corporations. Needed before doing business under any name other than the legal name. Advertise the name once in a newspaper in the county, then register online at Sunbiz or mail the form with the fee. Fee: $50. https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/start-business/efile/fl-fictitious-name-registration/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. Workers' compensation insurance, Florida Department of Financial Services, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://www.myfloridacfo.com/division/wc/employer/coverage-requirements
11. City of Miami CU (use approval), City of Miami, Office of Zoning. For a business opening or moving in the city, applied for online only through MiamiBiz once construction is done (with the certificate of occupancy or completion for new or renovated space). After the $50 fee, pass the DERM, fire and code inspections, plus Health or DBPR for food, within 90 working days of starting the application. Fee: Varies. Takes: The city contacts you within five business days of applying and paying. https://apps.miami.gov/MiamiBizIntake
12. City of Miami business tax receipt, City of Miami. Every business operating in the city needs one, after its Certificate of Use. Apply online with the EIN and, for a restaurant, the state food service license; the city emails an invoice, and the interim receipt comes by email once it's paid. A Miami-Dade County receipt is needed as well. Fee: Varies. Takes: The city doesn't publish how long approval takes; the interim receipt is emailed after payment. https://us.openforms.com/Form/98a6acf3-a616-4139-857d-68f4d9a4e51e
13. Miami-Dade County local business tax receipt, Miami-Dade County Tax Collector. Needed for each place of business in the county, and inside a city on top of the city's receipt. Apply online in BTExpress after completing the attestation that the business doesn't trade with Cuba in violation of federal law. Fee: Varies. Takes: Allow up to three business days after the attestation for the receipt to be ready to print. https://county-taxes.net/fl-miamidade/btexpress

### Toy stores in Miami
https://www.placetta.com/guides/miami/toy-store.html

The fixed government fees add up to about $175, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 4 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
