A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Florida sales tax and reemployment tax registration, Florida Department of Revenue. Register online before you start doing business. The same application covers sales and use tax and reemployment tax, Florida's unemployment tax for employers. Fee: Varies. Takes: After registering online, the certificate number is available on the website after three business days. https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/registration
4. Registration of a fictitious name (DBA), Florida Department of State, Division of Corporations. Needed before doing business under any name other than the legal name. Advertise the name once in a newspaper in the county, then register online at Sunbiz or mail the form with the fee. Fee: $50. https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/start-business/efile/fl-fictitious-name-registration/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Children's Product Certificate, from a CPSC-accepted lab's tests, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). Children's furniture is tested by a third-party, CPSC-accepted laboratory to the children's product safety rules that apply, and the importer issues the certificate, with its test reports, in English, citing each rule. Since July 8, 2026 most certificates are eFiled with CBP at entry, so it is ready before the goods ship. There is no government form. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Testing-Certification/Childrens-Product-Certificate-CPC
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Workers' compensation insurance, Florida Department of Financial Services, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://www.myfloridacfo.com/division/wc/employer/coverage-requirements
10. City of Miami CU (use approval), City of Miami, Office of Zoning. For a business opening or moving in the city, applied for online only through MiamiBiz once construction is done (with the certificate of occupancy or completion for new or renovated space). After the $50 fee, pass the DERM, fire and code inspections, plus Health or DBPR for food, within 90 working days of starting the application. Fee: Varies. Takes: The city contacts you within five business days of applying and paying. https://apps.miami.gov/MiamiBizIntake
11. City of Miami business tax receipt, City of Miami. Every business operating in the city needs one, after its Certificate of Use. Apply online with the EIN and, for a restaurant, the state food service license; the city emails an invoice, and the interim receipt comes by email once it's paid. A Miami-Dade County receipt is needed as well. Fee: Varies. Takes: The city doesn't publish how long approval takes; the interim receipt is emailed after payment. https://us.openforms.com/Form/98a6acf3-a616-4139-857d-68f4d9a4e51e
12. Miami-Dade County local business tax receipt, Miami-Dade County Tax Collector. Needed for each place of business in the county, and inside a city on top of the city's receipt. ### Restaurants in Dallas
https://www.placetta.com/guides/dallas/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Dallas takes 15 filings with 10 agencies, starting with the Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC) and ending with the franchise tax annual report. The fixed government fees add up to about $1,552, 4 fees are set by the space or the business and 4 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants and dessert shops.
1. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Permit arrives in about 2 to 3 weeks. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Certified food manager, Texas Department of State Health Services. At least one manager passes an exam from a DSHS-licensed certified food manager program. Local health departments require a certified food manager on site whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. Takes: DSHS doesn't issue the certificate itself; the accredited exam provider issues it as soon as you pass the exam. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-managers
6. Food handler certificates for staff, Texas Department of State Health Services. Every employee who works with unpackaged food, equipment or food-contact surfaces finishes an accredited food handler course within 30 days of hire. Certified food managers are exempt. Fee: Varies. Takes: Each food employee must complete an accredited food handler course within 30 days of being hired; the training provider issues the card. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-handlers
7. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. Takes: Account number issued instantly online. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
8. Workers' compensation, or the yearly non-subscriber notice, Texas Department of Insurance, Division of Workers' Compensation. Texas doesn't require private employers to carry workers' compensation. An employer with one or more employees who doesn't carry it is a non-subscriber: it files DWC Form-005 every year between February 1 and April 30, and tells its employees. Fee: Varies. https://Www.Tdi.Texas.Gov/forms/dwc/dwc005nocovst.pdf
9. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Dallas Planning and Development. Apply on DallasNow with the land use questionnaire, plus site and floor plans if the use is changing. Needed for a new tenant or a change of use. Fee: $375. Takes: Dallas's goal is to review a CO application within 15 business days on average, though its CO page notes processing times differ based on demand. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/Pages/certificate_occupancy.aspx
10. Building permit for tenant finish-out, City of Dallas Planning and Development. Apply on DallasNow under Commercial Permits, upload the plans and checklists, and pay online. Fee: Varies. Takes: Dallas's goal for a commercial alteration/addition is an initial plan review within 15 business days and a resubmittal review within 7. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/pages/fees.aspx
11. Food establishment plan review, City of Dallas Planning and Development, Health Plan Review. Submit two sets of plans, equipment sheets, finishes and the menu at 320 E. Jefferson Blvd., where the plans are reviewed and stamped. Fee: $200. Takes: Dallas's goal for the Health team's initial plan review is 15 business days. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/Pages/Health-Inspections.aspx
12. Food establishment permit, City of Dallas Code Compliance, Consumer Health. File CCS-FRM-424 with photo ID, the Texas sales tax permit and the fee, then book the health inspection. A registered food manager must be on site. Fee: $121. Takes: Consumer Health doesn't publish a processing time; after you apply, you schedule and coordinate the required health inspections with your permitting inspector. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/codecompliance/consumer-health/Pages/food-establishment.aspx
13. Sign permit, City of Dallas Planning and Development. A registered sign contractor applies on DallasNow once the Certificate of Occupancy is approved. Fee: $281. Takes: Typically about two business days if everything required is submitted. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/Pages/Signs.aspx
14. Kitchen hood fire-extinguishing system permit, Dallas Fire-Rescue. Get the application from Dallas Fire-Rescue, 1551 Baylor St., Suite 400. Fee: $250. Takes: Dallas doesn't publish a review time for kitchen hood fire-extinguishing system permits; its published goals cover only fire alarm, sprinkler and flammable-liquid reviews. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/fire-rescue/Pages/Prevention-and-Investigation-Bureau.aspx
15. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. Takes: The Comptroller doesn't publish a processing time for the report; the annual franchise tax report is due May 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

- Texas requires a Food Manufacturer license from the Department of State Health Services (DSHS) of a business that packages food for wholesale or for a self-service display, and lists bakeries among its examples. Texas Department of State Health Services: "Processing and/or packaging any food product, including dietary supplements, ice, and water, for wholesale distribution or for sale via retail customer self-service." https://dshs.texas.gov/foods/manufacturers.aspx (read 2026-10-22)

8. Sign permit, City of Dallas Planning and Development. A registered sign contractor applies on DallasNow once the Certificate of Occupancy is approved. Fee: $281. Takes: Typically about two business days if everything required is submitted. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/Pages/Signs.aspx
9. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. Takes: The Comptroller doesn't publish a processing time for the report; the annual franchise tax report is due May 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

### Cosmetics stores in Dallas
https://www.placetta.com/guides/dallas/cosmetics-store.html
Opening a cosmetics store in Dallas takes 14 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC) and ending with the franchise tax annual report. The fixed government fees add up to about $981, 2 fees are set by the space or the business and 8 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Permit arrives in about 2 to 3 weeks. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. Takes: Account number issued instantly online. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
11. Workers' compensation, or the yearly non-subscriber notice, Texas Department of Insurance, Division of Workers' Compensation. Texas doesn't require private employers to carry workers' compensation. An employer with one or more employees who doesn't carry it is a non-subscriber: it files DWC Form-005 every year between February 1 and April 30, and tells its employees. Fee: Varies. https://Www.Tdi.Texas.Gov/forms/dwc/dwc005nocovst.pdf
12. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Dallas Planning and Development. Apply on DallasNow with the land use questionnaire, plus site and floor plans if the use is changing. Needed for a new tenant or a change of use. Fee: $375. Takes: Dallas's goal is to review a CO application within 15 business days on average, though its CO page notes processing times differ based on demand. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/Pages/certificate_occupancy.aspx
13. Sign permit, City of Dallas Planning and Development. A registered sign contractor applies on DallasNow once the Certificate of Occupancy is approved. Fee: $281. Takes: Typically about two business days if everything required is submitted. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/Pages/Signs.aspx
14. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. Takes: The Comptroller doesn't publish a processing time for the report; the annual franchise tax report is due May 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

### Restaurants in Austin
https://www.placetta.com/guides/austin/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Austin takes 15 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC) and ending with the franchise tax annual report. The fixed government fees add up to about $815, 7 fees are set by the space or the business and 4 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants and dessert shops.
1. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Permit arrives in about 2 to 3 weeks. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Certified food manager, Texas Department of State Health Services. At least one manager passes an exam from a DSHS-licensed certified food manager program. Local health departments require a certified food manager on site whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. Takes: DSHS doesn't issue the certificate itself; the accredited exam provider issues it as soon as you pass the exam. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-managers
6. Food handler certificates for staff, Texas Department of State Health Services. Every employee who works with unpackaged food, equipment or food-contact surfaces finishes an accredited food handler course within 30 days of hire. Certified food managers are exempt. Fee: Varies. Takes: Each food employee must complete an accredited food handler course within 30 days of being hired; the training provider issues the card. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-handlers
7. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. Takes: Account number issued instantly online. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
8. Workers' compensation, or the yearly non-subscriber notice, Texas Department of Insurance, Division of Workers' Compensation. Texas doesn't require private employers to carry workers' compensation. An employer with one or more employees who doesn't carry it is a non-subscriber: it files DWC Form-005 every year between February 1 and April 30, and tells its employees. Fee: Varies. https://Www.Tdi.Texas.Gov/forms/dwc/dwc005nocovst.pdf
9. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Austin Development Services. Needed when the space's use changes or after construction; it may include a site plan exemption and building plan review. For a food business it comes through Austin Public Health's pre-opening inspection. Fee: Varies. Takes: Change-of-use reviews now take about two weeks (three review disciplines since October 2025). https://www.austintexas.gov/development-services/small-business-permitting
10. Building permit for a tenant finish-out, City of Austin Development Services. Apply with the city's commercial building permit web form (not AB+C) to build, alter or convert the space, with plans for commercial plan review. Fee: Varies. Takes: Commercial plan review for a remodel up to 25,000 sq ft takes 10 business days; small projects, such as a finish-out under 10,000 sq ft, take 5 business days. https://austintexas.jotform.com/austin-dsd/commercial-building-permit-web-form
11. Food establishment plan review, City of Austin Development Services, with Austin Public Health. For new construction or a remodel: inside the City of Austin, apply online through Development Services; in unincorporated Travis County, through Austin Public Health's My Health Department portal. Fee: $312. Takes: Inside the City of Austin, the food plan review is submitted with the commercial building application, whose review takes 10 business days for a remodel up to 25,000 sq ft (5 for small projects). https://www.austintexas.gov/health/programs/fixed-food-establishments
12. Pre-opening health inspection, Austin Public Health, Environmental Health Services. Apply on the My Health Department portal (Retail and Wholesale Food Applications, Pre-Opening Inspection), in person at 1520 Rutherford Ln, or by mail. Needed for a new place, a remodel or a change of owner; the place must pass before the permit is issued. Fee: $178. Takes: Austin Public Health doesn't publish how soon a pre-opening inspection happens; you apply once the space is built, and you must pass before the permit is issued. https://www.austintexas.gov/health/programs/fixed-food-establishments
13. Food enterprise permit (fixed food establishment), Austin Public Health, Environmental Health Services. Issued after the pre-opening inspection passes. Apply on the My Health Department portal (Food Enterprise, Operational Permit Application) or in person at 1520 Rutherford Ln; the form says mailed applications are not accepted. A certified food manager must be on site whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. Takes: Austin Public Health doesn't publish a processing time; the operating permit is issued after the pre-opening inspection is approved. https://www.austintexas.gov/health/programs/fixed-food-establishments
14. Sign permit, City of Austin Development Services. Any outdoor sign (wall, awning, projecting, freestanding, roof) needs a permit, applied for on the AB+C portal. Fee: Varies. Takes: Austin doesn't publish a review time for sign permits; staff review the application once the review fee is paid and email you the decision. https://abc.austintexas.gov
15. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. Takes: The Comptroller doesn't publish a processing time for the report; the annual franchise tax report is due May 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

Apply on the My Health Department portal (Food Enterprise, Operational Permit Application) or in person at 1520 Rutherford Ln; the form says mailed applications are not accepted. A certified food manager must be on site whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. Takes: Austin Public Health doesn't publish a processing time; the operating permit is issued after the pre-opening inspection is approved. https://www.austintexas.gov/health/programs/fixed-food-establishments
14. Sign permit, City of Austin Development Services. Any outdoor sign (wall, awning, projecting, freestanding, roof) needs a permit, applied for on the AB+C portal. Fee: Varies. Takes: Austin doesn't publish a review time for sign permits; staff review the application once the review fee is paid and email you the decision. https://abc.austintexas.gov
15. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. Takes: The Comptroller doesn't publish a processing time for the report; the annual franchise tax report is due May 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/
What's different for a bakery in Austin:
- Texas requires a Food Manufacturer license from the Department of State Health Services (DSHS) of a business that packages food for wholesale or for a self-service display, and lists bakeries among its examples. It applies if the bakery packages its goods that way. Texas Department of State Health Services: "Processing and/or packaging any food product, including dietary supplements, ice, and water, for wholesale distribution or for sale via retail customer self-service." https://dshs.texas.gov/foods/manufacturers.aspx (read 2026-10-22)

### Retail stores in Austin
https://www.placetta.com/guides/austin/retail-store.html
Opening a retail store in Austin takes 9 filings with 6 agencies, starting with the Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC) and ending with the franchise tax annual report. The fixed government fees add up to about $325, 3 fees are set by the space or the business and 4 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to grocery stores.
1. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Permit arrives in about 2 to 3 weeks. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. Takes: Account number issued instantly online. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
6. Workers' compensation, or the yearly non-subscriber notice, Texas Department of Insurance, Division of Workers' Compensation. Texas doesn't require private employers to carry workers' compensation. An employer with one or more employees who doesn't carry it is a non-subscriber: it files DWC Form-005 every year between February 1 and April 30, and tells its employees. Fee: Varies. https://Www.Tdi.Texas.Gov/forms/dwc/dwc005nocovst.pdf
7. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Austin Development Services. Needed when the space's use changes or after construction; it may include a site plan exemption and building plan review. For a food business it comes through Austin Public Health's pre-opening inspection. Fee: Varies. Takes: Change-of-use reviews now take about two weeks (three review disciplines since October 2025). https://www.austintexas.gov/development-services/small-business-permitting
8. Sign permit, City of Austin Development Services. Any outdoor sign (wall, awning, projecting, freestanding, roof) needs a permit, applied for on the AB+C portal. Fee: Varies. Takes: Austin doesn't publish a review time for sign permits; staff review the application once the review fee is paid and email you the decision. https://abc.austintexas.gov
9. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. Takes: The Comptroller doesn't publish a processing time for the report; the annual franchise tax report is due May 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. Takes: Account number issued instantly online. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax

### Restaurants in Washington, DC
https://www.placetta.com/guides/washington-dc/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Washington, DC takes 10 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the LLC formation (Articles of Organization) and ending with the food services business license. The fixed government fees add up to about $99, 8 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. LLC formation (Articles of Organization), DC Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection, Corporations Division. Form DLC-1 goes to the Superintendent of Corporations online, by mail or at the counter. Fee: Varies. https://dlcp.dc.gov/node/1616716
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. DC tax registration, DC Office of Tax and Revenue. Register with the Office of Tax and Revenue on the FR-500. Every basic business license applicant must be registered and in good standing, and the license application checks the tax number for Clean Hands. Fee: Varies. Takes: The Office of Tax and Revenue may take up to 10 business days to process a new registration. https://mytax.dc.gov
4. DC certified food protection manager card, DC Health. A manager who passed a nationally recognized food safety exam applies for DC Health's ID card with a copy of the certificate, in person at 899 North Capitol Street NE or by mail. DLCP asks for the DC Health food manager's certificate with the food license, and a certified manager has to be on duty whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. https://doh.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/doh/publication/attachments/Application%20for%20ID%20Cards.pdf
5. Building permit, DC Department of Buildings. A change of use takes building permits and final inspections before the new Certificate of Occupancy. Fee: Varies. https://dob.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/dob/Certificate%20of%20Occupancy--A%20Quick%20Guide.pdf
6. Unemployment insurance employer registration, DC Department of Employment Services, UI Tax Division. Any business with employees working in DC registers online in the Employer Self-Service Portal, which also takes the wage reports and tax payments. Fee: Varies. https://essp.does.dc.gov
7. Food establishment plan review, DC Health, Food Safety and Hygiene Inspection Services Division. Needed before building, converting or remodeling a food establishment, or changing its type of food operation. Plans, specifications and the menu go to DC Health through ProjectDox with the building permit application. Fee: Varies. https://dchealth.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/doh/publication/attachments/FS%28redtop%29%20-%20Plan%20review%202018%20v2.pdf
8. Workers' compensation insurance, DC Department of Employment Services, Office of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://does.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/does/page_content/attachments/OWC%20Employer%20brochure.pdf
9. Certificate of Occupancy, DC Department of Buildings. Needed when a new owner or tenant takes over a space, even with the same use, and when the space is used for something new; a new use also needs building permits and final inspections. Applied for online in Certifi. Fee: Varies. https://dob.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/dob/Certificate%20of%20Occupancy--A%20Quick%20Guide.pdf
10. Food services business license, DC Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection, with DC Health. The basic business license for restaurants, delis, caterers and other food businesses. Apply online in BOSS with the Certificate of Occupancy, the DC Health food manager's certificate, the approved DC Health inspection report, tax registration and Clean Hands, and corporate registration if you have one; pick only the category the business was approved for. Fee: $99. Takes: DLCP doesn't publish a processing time; apply once DC Health has approved the inspection. https://boss.dc.gov

Fee: Varies. https://does.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/does/page_content/attachments/OWC%20Employer%20brochure.pdf
8. Certificate of Occupancy, DC Department of Buildings. Needed when a new owner or tenant takes over a space, even with the same use, and when the space is used for something new; a new use also needs building permits and final inspections. Applied for online in Certifi. Fee: Varies. https://dob.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/dob/Certificate%20of%20Occupancy--A%20Quick%20Guide.pdf
9. Food services business license, DC Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection, with DC Health. The basic business license for restaurants, delis, caterers and other food businesses. Apply online in BOSS with the Certificate of Occupancy, the DC Health food manager's certificate, the approved DC Health inspection report, tax registration and Clean Hands, and corporate registration if you have one; pick only the category the business was approved for. Fee: $99. Takes: DLCP doesn't publish a processing time; apply once DC Health has approved the inspection. https://boss.dc.gov

### Retail stores in Washington, DC
https://www.placetta.com/guides/washington-dc/retail-store.html
Opening a retail store in Washington, DC takes 7 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the LLC formation (Articles of Organization) and ending with the Certificate of Occupancy. None of them has a fixed government fee, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation (Articles of Organization), DC Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection, Corporations Division. Form DLC-1 goes to the Superintendent of Corporations online, by mail or at the counter. Fee: Varies. https://dlcp.dc.gov/node/1616716
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Corporate registration and basic business license, DC Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection. Register the company, then get the basic business license for the activity. Fee: Varies. Takes: DLCP doesn't publish how long a Basic Business License takes; you need a processed FR-500 tax registration and a Clean Hands check before you can apply. https://dlcp.dc.gov
4. DC tax registration, DC Office of Tax and Revenue. Register with the Office of Tax and Revenue on the FR-500. Every basic business license applicant must be registered and in good standing, and the license application checks the tax number for Clean Hands. Fee: Varies. Takes: The Office of Tax and Revenue may take up to 10 business days to process a new registration. https://mytax.dc.gov
5. Unemployment insurance employer registration, DC Department of Employment Services, UI Tax Division. Any business with employees working in DC registers online in the Employer Self-Service Portal, which also takes the wage reports and tax payments. Fee: Varies. https://essp.does.dc.gov
6. Workers' compensation insurance, DC Department of Employment Services, Office of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://does.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/does/page_content/attachments/OWC%20Employer%20brochure.pdf
7. Certificate of Occupancy, DC Department of Buildings. Needed when a new owner or tenant takes over a space, even with the same use, and when the space is used for something new; a new use also needs building permits and final inspections. Applied for online in Certifi. Fee: Varies. https://dob.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/dob/Certificate%20of%20Occupancy--A%20Quick%20Guide.pdf

### Cosmetics stores in Washington, DC
https://www.placetta.com/guides/washington-dc/cosmetics-store.html
Opening a cosmetics store in Washington, DC takes 12 filings with 10 agencies, starting with the LLC formation (Articles of Organization) and ending with the Certificate of Occupancy. None of them has a fixed government fee, 7 fees are set by the space or the business and 5 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation (Articles of Organization), DC Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection, Corporations Division. Form DLC-1 goes to the Superintendent of Corporations online, by mail or at the counter. Fee: Varies. https://dlcp.dc.gov/node/1616716
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Corporate registration and basic business license, DC Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection. Register the company, then get the basic business license for the activity. Fee: Varies. Takes: DLCP doesn't publish how long a Basic Business License takes; you need a processed FR-500 tax registration and a Clean Hands check before you can apply. https://dlcp.dc.gov
4. DC tax registration, DC Office of Tax and Revenue. Register with the Office of Tax and Revenue on the FR-500. Every basic business license applicant must be registered and in good standing, and the license application checks the tax number for Clean Hands. Fee: Varies. Takes: The Office of Tax and Revenue may take up to 10 business days to process a new registration. https://mytax.dc.gov
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. Unemployment insurance employer registration, DC Department of Employment Services, UI Tax Division. Any business with employees working in DC registers online in the Employer Self-Service Portal, which also takes the wage reports and tax payments. Fee: Varies. https://essp.does.dc.gov
11. Workers' compensation insurance, DC Department of Employment Services, Office of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://does.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/does/page_content/attachments/OWC%20Employer%20brochure.pdf
12. Certificate of Occupancy, DC Department of Buildings. Needed when a new owner or tenant takes over a space, even with the same use, and when the space is used for something new; a new use also needs building permits and final inspections. Applied for online in Certifi. Fee: Varies. https://dob.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/dob/Certificate%20of%20Occupancy--A%20Quick%20Guide.pdf

### Restaurants in Atlanta
https://www.placetta.com/guides/atlanta/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Atlanta takes 10 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the food service permit. None of them has a fixed government fee, 7 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants and dessert shops.
1. LLC formation, Georgia Secretary of State, Corporations. Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: Varies. https://ecorp.sos.ga.gov
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Sales tax registration, Georgia Department of Revenue. Register for sales and withholding tax online. Fee: Free. Takes: After registering online in the Georgia Tax Center, you should get your tax account number by email within 15 minutes. https://gtc.dor.ga.gov
4. Certified food safety manager, Georgia Department of Public Health, Environmental Health. At least one employee with supervisory and management duties passes an accredited food safety manager exam, and is designated to this one place only. A new food service establishment has 60 days from its permit to employ one, and tells the county within 30 days if it loses its manager. Fee: Varies. https://dph.georgia.gov/node/146
5. Building permit for the build-out, City of Atlanta, Office of Buildings. The Office of Buildings issues the permits construction and alteration need under the Atlanta Municipal Code, and inspects the work. Fee: Varies. https://atlantaga.gov/home/showdocument?id=19215
6. Atlanta business license, City of Atlanta, Department of Finance, Office of Revenue. Every business location inside city limits registers. Apply on the city's ATLBiz portal with a government photo ID, the articles of incorporation, notarized SAVE and E-Verify affidavits and the EIN; the city runs the zoning review itself, and some kinds of business also upload a regulatory permit. Fee: Varies. Takes: Atlanta doesn't publish how long a new license takes; the zoning review is done inside the city as part of the application. https://atlbiz.atlantaga.gov/_/
7. Food service plan review, Fulton County Board of Health, Environmental Health Services. Before building or extensively remodeling, mail or bring the application, scaled plans, equipment specifications and the fee to the Environmental Health district office nearest the restaurant. An Atlanta address in DeKalb County applies to the DeKalb County Board of Health instead. Fee: Varies. Takes: The county doesn't publish a review time; Georgia's food service rules ask for plans at least 14 business days before construction starts. https://FultonCountyGa.gov/-/media/Departments/Board-of-Health/Environmental-Health/Restaurant-Inspection/Link-List-Items/Food-Service-Application.pdf
8. Unemployment insurance tax account (DOL-1A), Georgia Department of Labor. Employers with a quarterly payroll of $1,500, or a worker in 20 weeks of a year, file Form DOL-1A and then quarterly tax and wage reports. Fee: Free. https://dol.georgia.gov/node/2291
9. Workers' compensation insurance, Georgia State Board of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://sbwc.georgia.gov/frequently-asked-questions/workers-compensation-law-faqs
10. Food service permit, Fulton County Board of Health, Environmental Health Services. Issued by the county once the application and fee are in, the plans are approved and the place passes its pre-opening inspection; apply by mail or in person at the district office nearest the restaurant. An Atlanta address in DeKalb County gets its permit from the DeKalb County Board of Health instead. Fee: Varies. Takes: Georgia's food service rules ask for the permit application at least 10 business days before opening. https://FultonCountyGa.gov/-/media/Departments/Board-of-Health/Environmental-Health/Restaurant-Inspection/Link-List-Items/Food-Service-Application.pdf

What's different for a bakery in Atlanta:
- The Georgia Department of Agriculture regulates bakeries as food retailers, while restaurants get their food service permit from the county health department (Fulton County in Atlanta). Odelia confirms which licenses yours, by what it sells and where it's eaten. Georgia Department of Agriculture: "regulates and monitors food retailers: grocery stores, convenience stores, bakeries, seafood operations, salvage food operations, mobile meat trucks, and rolling stores." https://agr.ga.gov/retailers (read 2026-10-22)

5. Unemployment insurance tax account (DOL-1A), Georgia Department of Labor. Employers with a quarterly payroll of $1,500, or a worker in 20 weeks of a year, file Form DOL-1A and then quarterly tax and wage reports. Fee: Free. https://dol.georgia.gov/node/2291
6. Workers' compensation insurance, Georgia State Board of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://sbwc.georgia.gov/frequently-asked-questions/workers-compensation-law-faqs

### Restaurants in Philadelphia
https://www.placetta.com/guides/philadelphia/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Philadelphia takes 10 filings with 8 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the food preparation and serving license. The fixed government fees add up to about $155, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 2 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. LLC formation, Pennsylvania Department of State. Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: $125. https://file.dos.pa.gov
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Pennsylvania tax registration (sales tax license and employer accounts), Pennsylvania Department of Revenue. Register in myPATH (new customers don't need to log in) for sales, use and hotel occupancy tax, employer withholding and unemployment compensation. Fee: Varies. Takes: The Department of Revenue doesn't publish how long myPATH registration takes to issue a sales tax license. https://mypath.pa.gov/_/
4. Philadelphia food safety certificate, Philadelphia Department of Public Health, Environmental Health Services. Every food business has at least one person certified in food safety at all times. Take a food manager safety course with an approved provider, send the training certificate to the Health Department for checking, then apply for the city certificate online, or in person or by mail with a money order. Fee: $30. Takes: Checking the training certificate takes up to 10 business days, and the certificate itself up to 30 business days. https://philadph.formstack.com/forms/fscapp
5. Philadelphia tax account (BIRT and Wage Tax), City of Philadelphia Department of Revenue. Register the business as a new taxpayer on the Philadelphia Tax Center to get a Philadelphia Tax Identification Number, used for the Business Income and Receipts Tax and, with staff, the Wage Tax. The paper application can also apply for the Commercial Activity License. Fee: Varies. https://tax-services.phila.gov/
6. Commercial activity license, City of Philadelphia, Department of Licenses and Inspections. Every person or company doing business in Philadelphia needs it, and should get it before any other business license. Apply in eCLIPSE with the EIN and the BIRT ID, under the legal name on the city tax account, or at the Permit and License Center by appointment. Fee: Free. Takes: Issued automatically online, or while you wait in person. https://eclipse.phila.gov/
7. Food business plan review, Philadelphia Department of Public Health, Office of Food Protection. Anyone opening a stationary food business applies after zoning is approved and before construction or installing food equipment. Call 215-685-7495 to submit, book an appointment or walk in at 7801 Essington Ave (weekdays 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.). The application covers 13 items, from the site plan to the menu, with a copy of the city food safety certificate. Fee: Varies. Takes: A worksheet and fee letter within 30 business days; after you return them, the Health Department replies within 30 business days. Expedited review takes 10 business days. https://phila.gov/media/20250423122123/Plan-Review-for-Stationary-Food-Businesses-2025-fillable.pdf
8. Workers' compensation insurance, Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry, Bureau of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dli/resources/for-employers-and-educators/workers--compensation-for-employers/workers--compensation-compliance
9. Building permit for the build-out, City of Philadelphia, Department of Licenses and Inspections. Construction or alterations to the space need a building permit from L&I's Building Unit, filed in eCLIPSE; signs and emission-producing equipment have their own permits. Fee: Varies. https://eclipse.phila.gov/
10. Food preparation and serving license, City of Philadelphia, Department of Licenses and Inspections. For any business that prepares or serves food to the public. Apply in eCLIPSE with the BIRT ID, the Commercial Activity License, proof of occupancy (a license for the same use in the last 3 years, or zoning approval) and the Health Department's License Eligibility Report dated within 30 days. Fee: Varies. Takes: Online applications are reviewed within 5 business days. https://eclipse.phila.gov/

Register in myPATH (new customers don't need to log in) for sales, use and hotel occupancy tax, employer withholding and unemployment compensation. Fee: Varies. Takes: The Department of Revenue doesn't publish how long myPATH registration takes to issue a sales tax license. https://mypath.pa.gov/_/
4. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Children's Product Certificate, from a CPSC-accepted lab's tests, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). Children's furniture is tested by a third-party, CPSC-accepted laboratory to the children's product safety rules that apply, and the importer issues the certificate, with its test reports, in English, citing each rule. Since July 8, 2026 most certificates are eFiled with CBP at entry, so it is ready before the goods ship. There is no government form. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Testing-Certification/Childrens-Product-Certificate-CPC
7. Philadelphia tax account (BIRT and Wage Tax), City of Philadelphia Department of Revenue. Register the business as a new taxpayer on the Philadelphia Tax Center to get a Philadelphia Tax Identification Number, used for the Business Income and Receipts Tax and, with staff, the Wage Tax. The paper application can also apply for the Commercial Activity License. Fee: Varies. https://tax-services.phila.gov/
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Commercial activity license, City of Philadelphia, Department of Licenses and Inspections. Every person or company doing business in Philadelphia needs it, and should get it before any other business license. Apply in eCLIPSE with the EIN and the BIRT ID, under the legal name on the city tax account, or at the Permit and License Center by appointment. Fee: Free. Takes: Issued automatically online, or while you wait in person. https://eclipse.phila.gov/
10. Workers' compensation insurance, Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry, Bureau of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dli/resources/for-employers-and-educators/workers--compensation-for-employers/workers--compensation-compliance

### Importers and online sellers in Philadelphia
https://www.placetta.com/guides/philadelphia/importer-ecommerce.html
Opening an importer or e-commerce seller in Philadelphia takes 9 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the commercial activity license. The fixed government fees add up to about $125, 3 fees are set by the space or the business and 5 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation, Pennsylvania Department of State. Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: $125. https://file.dos.pa.gov
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Pennsylvania tax registration (sales tax license and employer accounts), Pennsylvania Department of Revenue. Register in myPATH (new customers don't need to log in) for sales, use and hotel occupancy tax, employer withholding and unemployment compensation. Fee: Varies. Takes: The Department of Revenue doesn't publish how long myPATH registration takes to issue a sales tax license. https://mypath.pa.gov/_/

Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
7. Philadelphia tax account (BIRT and Wage Tax), City of Philadelphia Department of Revenue. Register the business as a new taxpayer on the Philadelphia Tax Center to get a Philadelphia Tax Identification Number, used for the Business Income and Receipts Tax and, with staff, the Wage Tax. The paper application can also apply for the Commercial Activity License. Fee: Varies. https://tax-services.phila.gov/
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Commercial activity license, City of Philadelphia, Department of Licenses and Inspections. Every person or company doing business in Philadelphia needs it, and should get it before any other business license. Apply in eCLIPSE with the EIN and the BIRT ID, under the legal name on the city tax account, or at the Permit and License Center by appointment. Fee: Free. Takes: Issued automatically online, or while you wait in person. https://eclipse.phila.gov/

### Restaurants in Las Vegas
https://www.placetta.com/guides/las-vegas/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Las Vegas takes 11 filings with 8 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and state business license and ending with the food establishment health permit. The fixed government fees add up to about $35, 8 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. LLC formation and state business license, Nevada Secretary of State (SilverFlume). Form the company and get the state business license together online. Fee: Varies. https://www.nvsilverflume.gov
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Nevada state business license, Nevada Secretary of State. Every business that conducts business in Nevada holds the Secretary of State's business license (or a certificate of exemption), on top of any city or county license. Fee: Varies. https://www.nvsilverflume.gov/
4. Nevada sales tax permit, Nevada Department of Taxation. Register online in My Nevada Tax once you have an EIN and the state business license, or mail the Nevada Business Registration Form. Businesses paying more than $50,000 in wages in a quarter also register for the Modified Business Tax, through DETR. Fee: $15. Takes: Online, the permit number comes within 24 hours; by mail, several weeks. https://mynvtax.nv.gov/tap/_/
5. Certified food safety manager, Southern Nevada Health District. The Health District's permit application asks for a person in charge who is a Certified Food Safety Manager, with a copy of the certificate attached. The certificate comes from an accredited food protection manager exam. Fee: Varies. https://media.southernnevadahealthdistrict.org/download/eh/2022/plan-review/applications/snhd-application-packet-food-202207.pdf
6. Food handler cards for staff, Southern Nevada Health District. Everyone employed in or running a food establishment holds one. A first card means an in-person test at a Health District location with photo ID; some renewals can be done online. A Certified Food Safety Manager card also meets the requirement. Fee: $20. https://www.southernnevadahealthdistrict.org/?p=3661
7. City of Las Vegas business license, City of Las Vegas, Business Licensing. For an address inside City of Las Vegas limits; check the jurisdiction first, since other addresses license with Clark County or their own city. Confirm the zoning allows the business and the building is code compliant, get the state business license and register with the Department of Taxation, then apply on the city's online portal. Fee: Varies. Takes: A license technician emails within 5 business days; the license is issued within 30 days of applying, usually sooner. https://www.lasvegasnevada.gov/dashboard
8. Unemployment insurance employer account, Nevada Department of Employment, Training and Rehabilitation, Employment Security Division. Employers open their unemployment insurance account with DETR's Employment Security Division, whose Registration Unit handles Nevada business registration; DETR shares the details with the Department of Taxation. The account is then managed in the Employer Self-Service portal. Fee: Varies. http://nui.nv.gov/ess
9. Food establishment plan review, Southern Nevada Health District. Plans are needed for new and remodeled places and must be approved before construction starts. Email the application packet, plans in PDF, the menu, the food questionnaire and proof of the lease or deed to FOODREV@SNHD.ORG; a remote plan review follows and the invoice comes by email. Two construction walkthroughs are included. Fee: Varies. https://media.southernnevadahealthdistrict.org/download/eh/2022/plan-review/applications/snhd-application-packet-food-202207.pdf
10. Workers' compensation insurance, Nevada Division of Industrial Relations, Workers' Compensation Section. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.nv.gov/uploadedFiles/dirnvgov/content/WCS/EmployersDocs/EmployerBrochure.7.2026.pdf
11. Food establishment health permit, Southern Nevada Health District. Issued after the final permitting inspection, which needs a Certificate of Occupancy (or a temporary one) after new construction or a remodel, and every fee paid first. Food can't be stocked until the permit is approved. Fee: Varies. https://media.southernnevadahealthdistrict.org/download/eh/2022/plan-review/applications/snhd-application-packet-food-202207.pdf

Fee: Varies. https://dir.nv.gov/uploadedFiles/dirnvgov/content/WCS/EmployersDocs/EmployerBrochure.7.2026.pdf

### Importers and online sellers in Las Vegas
https://www.placetta.com/guides/las-vegas/importer-ecommerce.html
Opening an importer or e-commerce seller in Las Vegas takes 9 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and state business license and ending with the City of Las Vegas business license. The fixed government fees add up to about $15, 4 fees are set by the space or the business and 4 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation and state business license, Nevada Secretary of State (SilverFlume). Form the company and get the state business license together online. Fee: Varies. https://www.nvsilverflume.gov
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Nevada state business license, Nevada Secretary of State. Every business that conducts business in Nevada holds the Secretary of State's business license (or a certificate of exemption), on top of any city or county license. Fee: Varies. https://www.nvsilverflume.gov/
4. Nevada sales tax permit, Nevada Department of Taxation. Register online in My Nevada Tax once you have an EIN and the state business license, or mail the Nevada Business Registration Form. Businesses paying more than $50,000 in wages in a quarter also register for the Modified Business Tax, through DETR. Fee: $15. Takes: Online, the permit number comes within 24 hours; by mail, several weeks. https://mynvtax.nv.gov/tap/_/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. City of Las Vegas business license, City of Las Vegas, Business Licensing. For an address inside City of Las Vegas limits; check the jurisdiction first, since other addresses license with Clark County or their own city. Confirm the zoning allows the business and the building is code compliant, get the state business license and register with the Department of Taxation, then apply on the city's online portal. Fee: Varies. Takes: A license technician emails within 5 business days; the license is issued within 30 days of applying, usually sooner. https://www.lasvegasnevada.gov/dashboard

7. Hazardous materials registration, Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (DOT). Filed online when you ship or offer certain hazardous materials in bulk, such as large lithium battery shipments. Fee: Varies. https://hazmatonline.phmsa.dot.gov/services/
8. City of Las Vegas business license, City of Las Vegas, Business Licensing. For an address inside City of Las Vegas limits; check the jurisdiction first, since other addresses license with Clark County or their own city. Employers open their unemployment insurance account with DETR's Employment Security Division, whose Registration Unit handles Nevada business registration; DETR shares the details with the Department of Taxation. ### Restaurants in San Antonio
https://www.placetta.com/guides/san-antonio/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in San Antonio takes 11 filings with 8 agencies, starting with the Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC) and ending with the franchise tax annual report. The fixed government fees add up to about $325, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 4 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants and dessert shops.
1. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Permit arrives in about 2 to 3 weeks. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Certified food manager, Texas Department of State Health Services. At least one manager passes an exam from a DSHS-licensed certified food manager program. Local health departments require a certified food manager on site whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. Takes: DSHS doesn't issue the certificate itself; the accredited exam provider issues it as soon as you pass the exam. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-managers
6. Food handler certificates for staff, Texas Department of State Health Services. Every employee who works with unpackaged food, equipment or food-contact surfaces finishes an accredited food handler course within 30 days of hire. Certified food managers are exempt. Fee: Varies. Takes: Each food employee must complete an accredited food handler course within 30 days of being hired; the training provider issues the card. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-handlers
7. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. Takes: Account number issued instantly online. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
8. Workers' compensation, or the yearly non-subscriber notice, Texas Department of Insurance, Division of Workers' Compensation. Texas doesn't require private employers to carry workers' compensation. An employer with one or more employees who doesn't carry it is a non-subscriber: it files DWC Form-005 every year between February 1 and April 30, and tells its employees. Fee: Varies. https://Www.Tdi.Texas.Gov/forms/dwc/dwc005nocovst.pdf
9. Certificate of Occupancy, City of San Antonio Development Services. Needed when the new business is a different type of business than the one in the building now; a new owner or tenant with the same use only updates the name on the existing certificate. Expect building, electrical, mechanical, plumbing and fire inspections. Fee: Varies. Takes: San Antonio doesn't publish a processing time for a Certificate of Occupancy; for new construction it's issued once all required inspections are complete. https://www.sanantonio.gov/DSD/Business/CofO
10. Food establishment license, San Antonio Metropolitan Health District (Metro Health). Once the space is zoned for the use and the Certificate of Occupancy requirements are complete, buy the license at the Development and Business Services Center, 1901 S. Alamo. Fee: Varies. Takes: Metro Health doesn't publish a processing time; the license is issued only after all building, health and fire inspections are approved and recorded, and you must show a valid CofO to buy the permit. https://www.sanantonio.gov/Health/FoodLicensing/FAQs
11. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. Takes: The Comptroller doesn't publish a processing time for the report; the annual franchise tax report is due May 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

What's different for a bakery in San Antonio:
- Texas requires a Food Manufacturer license from the Department of State Health Services (DSHS) of a business that packages food for wholesale or for a self-service display, and lists bakeries among its examples. It applies if the bakery packages its goods that way. Texas Department of State Health Services: "Processing and/or packaging any food product, including dietary supplements, ice, and water, for wholesale distribution or for sale via retail customer self-service." https://dshs.texas.gov/foods/manufacturers.aspx (read 2026-10-22)

The fixed government fees add up to about $325, 1 fee is set by the space or the business and 6 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Permit arrives in about 2 to 3 weeks. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. Takes: The Comptroller doesn't publish a processing time for the report; the annual franchise tax report is due May 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

### Warehouses and 3PLs in San Antonio
https://www.placetta.com/guides/san-antonio/warehouse-3pl.html
Opening a warehouse or 3PL in San Antonio takes 12 filings with 8 agencies, starting with the Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC) and ending with the franchise tax annual report. The fixed government fees add up to about $325, 4 fees are set by the space or the business and 6 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf

A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
