4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Permit arrives in about 2 to 3 weeks. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
8. Hazardous materials registration, Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (DOT). Filed online when you ship or offer certain hazardous materials in bulk, such as large lithium battery shipments. Fee: Varies. https://hazmatonline.phmsa.dot.gov/services/
9. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. Takes: Account number issued instantly online. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
10. Workers' compensation, or the yearly non-subscriber notice, Texas Department of Insurance, Division of Workers' Compensation. Texas doesn't require private employers to carry workers' compensation. An employer with one or more employees who doesn't carry it is a non-subscriber: it files DWC Form-005 every year between February 1 and April 30, and tells its employees. Fee: Varies. https://Www.Tdi.Texas.Gov/forms/dwc/dwc005nocovst.pdf
11. Certificate of Occupancy, City of San Antonio Development Services. Needed when the new business is a different type of business than the one in the building now; a new owner or tenant with the same use only updates the name on the existing certificate. Expect building, electrical, mechanical, plumbing and fire inspections. Fee: Varies. Takes: San Antonio doesn't publish a processing time for a Certificate of Occupancy; for new construction it's issued once all required inspections are complete. https://www.sanantonio.gov/DSD/Business/CofO
12. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. Takes: The Comptroller doesn't publish a processing time for the report; the annual franchise tax report is due May 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Tampa
https://www.placetta.com/guides/tampa/milk-tea-shop.html
Opening a milk tea shop in Tampa takes 10 filings with 8 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the florida public food service license. The fixed government fees add up to about $175, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 2 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation, Florida Division of Corporations (Sunbiz). Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: $125. https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Florida sales tax and reemployment tax registration, Florida Department of Revenue. Register online before you start doing business. The same application covers sales and use tax and reemployment tax, Florida's unemployment tax for employers. Fee: Varies. Takes: After registering online, the certificate number is available on the website after three business days. https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/registration
4. Registration of a fictitious name (DBA), Florida Department of State, Division of Corporations. Needed before doing business under any name other than the legal name. Advertise the name once in a newspaper in the county, then register online at Sunbiz or mail the form with the fee. Fee: $50. https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/start-business/efile/fl-fictitious-name-registration/
5. Certified food protection manager, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Food managers complete training and pass a certification exam from an accredited program within 30 days of starting the job, and the restaurant shows proof whenever an inspector asks. Fee: Varies. https://www2.myfloridalicense.com/hotels-restaurants/food-lodging/food-manager/
6. Hillsborough County local business tax receipt, Hillsborough County Tax Collector. Get it before you start trading: apply online in BTExpress in one sitting, with the business name, SSN or EIN, a physical county address and any state or county license the business needs. Fee: Varies. Takes: Reviewed in 3 to 5 business days, then paid and printed online. https://www.hillstaxfl.gov/taxes/business-tax-services/new-regulated-businesses/
7. City of Tampa business tax receipt, City of Tampa Business Tax. A business inside Tampa city limits files the new business application online; the city may inspect the site. Fee: Varies. Takes: Tampa doesn't publish a processing time for a new business tax receipt; applications are made online or by appointment. https://www.tampa.gov/service/new-business-tax-receipt-application
8. Food service plan review, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Required for a space that is newly built, remodeled, converted from another use or reopening after 18 months closed; the state recommends approval before construction. Submit the plan with labeled equipment and a sample menu together with the new license application on DBPR Online. Fee: Free. https://www.myfloridalicense.com/intentions2.asp?chBoard=true&SID=&boardid=200&professionid=2010
9. Workers' compensation insurance, Florida Department of Financial Services, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://www.myfloridacfo.com/division/wc/employer/coverage-requirements
10. Florida public food service license, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Apply and pay on DBPR Online, one license for each operation. Once the plan review requirements are met, call 850-487-1395 several business days before opening to book the opening inspection; serve nobody until it passes and a temporary paper license is issued on the spot. Fee: Varies. Takes: Most applications are processed within a few business days; mailed ones take longer. https://www.myfloridalicense.com/intentions2.asp?chBoard=true&SID=&boardid=200&professionid=2010
What's different for a milk tea shop in Tampa:
- Florida's Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS) permits coffee shops and juice and smoothie bars, and DBPR licenses restaurants and fast food. Neither names tea shops, so Odelia confirms which one licenses yours before anything is filed. Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services: "These food establishments may include supermarkets, grocery stores, convenience stores, coffee shops, bakeries, retail meat markets, retail seafood markets, juice and smoothie bars," https://www.fdacs.gov/Business-Services/Food/Food-Establishments/Retail-Food-Establishment-Permit (read 2026-10-22)

6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. Hillsborough County local business tax receipt, Hillsborough County Tax Collector. Get it before you start trading: apply online in BTExpress in one sitting, with the business name, SSN or EIN, a physical county address and any state or county license the business needs. Fee: Varies. Takes: Reviewed in 3 to 5 business days, then paid and printed online. https://www.hillstaxfl.gov/taxes/business-tax-services/new-regulated-businesses/
11. City of Tampa business tax receipt, City of Tampa Business Tax. A business inside Tampa city limits files the new business application online; the city may inspect the site. Fee: Varies. Takes: Tampa doesn't publish a processing time for a new business tax receipt; applications are made online or by appointment. https://www.tampa.gov/service/new-business-tax-receipt-application
12. Workers' compensation insurance, Florida Department of Financial Services, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://www.myfloridacfo.com/division/wc/employer/coverage-requirements

### Toy stores in Tampa
https://www.placetta.com/guides/tampa/toy-store.html
Opening a toy store in Tampa takes 11 filings with 10 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the workers' compensation insurance. The fixed government fees add up to about $175, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 4 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation, Florida Division of Corporations (Sunbiz). Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: $125. https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Florida sales tax and reemployment tax registration, Florida Department of Revenue. Register online before you start doing business. The same application covers sales and use tax and reemployment tax, Florida's unemployment tax for employers. Fee: Varies. Takes: After registering online, the certificate number is available on the website after three business days. https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/registration
4. Registration of a fictitious name (DBA), Florida Department of State, Division of Corporations. Needed before doing business under any name other than the legal name. Advertise the name once in a newspaper in the county, then register online at Sunbiz or mail the form with the fee. Fee: $50. https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/start-business/efile/fl-fictitious-name-registration/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Children's Product Certificate, from a CPSC-accepted lab's tests, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). Children's furniture is tested by a third-party, CPSC-accepted laboratory to the children's product safety rules that apply, and the importer issues the certificate, with its test reports, in English, citing each rule. Since July 8, 2026 most certificates are eFiled with CBP at entry, so it is ready before the goods ship. There is no government form. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Testing-Certification/Childrens-Product-Certificate-CPC
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling

Get it before you start trading: apply online in BTExpress in one sitting, with the business name, SSN or EIN, a physical county address and any state or county license the business needs. ### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in San Diego
https://www.placetta.com/guides/san-diego/milk-tea-shop.html
Opening a milk tea shop in San Diego takes 13 filings with 10 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the LLC annual tax ($800). The fixed government fees add up to about $890, 7 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to coffee shops.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113947.1
6. Food handler cards for staff, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. Every employee who prepares, stores or handles food gets a California Food Handler Card from an accredited course within 30 days of hire; the card is good for 3 years. Anyone holding a valid food manager certificate is exempt. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113948
7. City of San Diego Business Tax Certificate, City of San Diego, Office of the City Treasurer. Every business operating in the City of San Diego registers, online on the Treasurer's portal, by mail or in person by appointment. Late fees apply to applications received 15 days after the business start date. Fee: Varies. Takes: Allow up to two weeks to receive the certificate. https://pay.sandiego.gov/BTaxApp
8. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
9. Food facility plan check, County of San Diego Department of Environmental Health and Quality. Submit at least three sets of plans with the application and fee to a DEHQ office; plans are approved before the building permit is issued. Fee: Varies. Takes: Plans are approved or rejected within 20 working days of receipt. https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/deh/fhd/food/food_faq.html
10. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
11. Certificate of Occupancy, City of San Diego Development Services. Issued after the final inspection of building permit work. Needed for a change of occupancy classification or a tenant improvement in a shell building; not needed for a change of owner or tenant when the occupancy doesn't change. Fee: Varies. Takes: San Diego doesn't publish a delivery time for a commercial Certificate of Occupancy; it's issued once every inspection under the permit has final approval (only affordable housing and shelters get set deadlines). https://www.sandiego.gov/development-services/forms-publications/information-bulletin/585
12. Public health permit (food facility), County of San Diego Department of Environmental Health and Quality. Required by law for every retail food facility in San Diego County. Fee: Varies. Takes: Plans are approved or rejected within 20 working days of receipt, and plan check staff issue the health permit when the facility passes its final inspection. https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/deh/fhd/food/food_faq.html
13. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
What's different for a milk tea shop in San Diego:
- Under California's food code, a food facility in a building built after January 1, 2004 that gives customers space to eat or drink on the premises must provide clean restrooms for them. The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-22)

13. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
What's different for a bakery in San Diego:
- Under California's food code, a food facility in a building built after January 1, 2004 that gives customers space to eat or drink on the premises must provide clean restrooms for them. The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-22)
- California's Processed Food Registration, from the Department of Public Health, covers bakery products. A retail food facility that sells directly to consumers under a county health permit is exempt, so a bakery selling only over its own counter doesn't need it; making goods for other stores or cafes falls outside that exemption. California Department of Public Health: "General foods such as bakery products, noodles, seafood (except molluscan shellfish)" https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CEH/DFDCS/Pages/FDBPrograms/FoodSafetyProgram/PFRFAQs.aspx (read 2026-10-21)

### Retail stores in San Diego
https://www.placetta.com/guides/san-diego/retail-store.html
Opening a retail store in San Diego takes 10 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the proposition 65 warning labels. The fixed government fees add up to about $890, 3 fees are set by the space or the business and 4 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to grocery stores.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. City of San Diego Business Tax Certificate, City of San Diego, Office of the City Treasurer. Every business operating in the City of San Diego registers, online on the Treasurer's portal, by mail or in person by appointment. Late fees apply to applications received 15 days after the business start date. Fee: Varies. Takes: Allow up to two weeks to receive the certificate. https://pay.sandiego.gov/BTaxApp
6. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
7. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
8. Certificate of Occupancy, City of San Diego Development Services. Issued after the final inspection of building permit work. Needed for a change of occupancy classification or a tenant improvement in a shell building; not needed for a change of owner or tenant when the occupancy doesn't change. Fee: Varies. Takes: San Diego doesn't publish a delivery time for a commercial Certificate of Occupancy; it's issued once every inspection under the permit has final approval (only affordable housing and shelters get set deadlines). https://www.sandiego.gov/development-services/forms-publications/information-bulletin/585
9. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
10. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. Takes: Nothing is filed with or approved by OEHHA, so there's no processing time; the business decides whether a warning is needed and must have it in place itself. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses

9. Packaging producer registration (EPR), CalRecycle, through Circular Action Alliance. A producer of packaged goods sold in California applies to participate in Circular Action Alliance's plan, submits an independent producer application, or obtains a small producer exemption; CalRecycle's PEPRS portal or the PRO takes the registration and the reports. Fee: Varies. https://calrecycle.ca.gov/packaging/packaging-epr/producerguidance/
10. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
11. City of San Diego Business Tax Certificate, City of San Diego, Office of the City Treasurer. Every business operating in the City of San Diego registers, online on the Treasurer's portal, by mail or in person by appointment. Late fees apply to applications received 15 days after the business start date. Fee: Varies. Takes: Allow up to two weeks to receive the certificate. https://pay.sandiego.gov/BTaxApp

Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
13. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Irvine
https://www.placetta.com/guides/irvine/milk-tea-shop.html

5. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113947.1
6. Food handler cards for staff, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. Every employee who prepares, stores or handles food gets a California Food Handler Card from an accredited course within 30 days of hire; the card is good for 3 years. Anyone holding a valid food manager certificate is exempt. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113948
7. Building permit for the tenant improvement, City of Irvine, Building Permits and Inspections. The plans and the permit application go in electronically through the city's IrvineReady! portal; the city inspects the work. Fee: Varies. https://cityofirvine.gov/node/69516
8. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
9. Food facility plan check, Orange County Health Care Agency, Environmental Health. Submit the plan check online with three sets of plans and specifications before construction; the fee is set at conditional approval. Fee: Varies. Takes: The initial plan review usually takes 20 working days. https://www.ochealthinfo.com/services-programs/environmental-health/plan-check
10. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
11. Food facility health permit, Orange County Health Care Agency, Environmental Health. Every food facility that stores, prepares, packages, serves or vends food needs a valid health permit; book inspections 5 working days ahead. Fee: Varies. Takes: Initial plan review usually takes 20 working days; inspections must be requested 5 working days ahead, and the health permit is issued once the final inspection passes. https://ochealthinfo.com/sites/healthcare/files/2023-04/Food%20Health%20Permit%20Application%20W.pdf
12. City of Irvine business license, City of Irvine Community Development, Business Licensing. A city tax rather than a regulatory license: apply online or at the public counter, confirm first that the use is allowed at the address, and display the license at the business. Fee: Varies. Takes: Irvine doesn't publish how long it takes to issue the license; the online application takes minutes, and new businesses must apply within 60 days of starting to avoid late fees. https://cityofirvine.gov/community-development/business-licensing
13. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
What's different for a milk tea shop in Irvine:
- Under California's food code, a food facility in a building built after January 1, 2004 that gives customers space to eat or drink on the premises must provide clean restrooms for them. The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-22)

### Restaurants in Irvine

The fixed government fees add up to about $890, 7 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. 1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113947.1
6. Food handler cards for staff, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. Every employee who prepares, stores or handles food gets a California Food Handler Card from an accredited course within 30 days of hire; the card is good for 3 years. Anyone holding a valid food manager certificate is exempt. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113948
7. Building permit for the tenant improvement, City of Irvine, Building Permits and Inspections. The plans and the permit application go in electronically through the city's IrvineReady! portal; the city inspects the work. Fee: Varies. https://cityofirvine.gov/node/69516
8. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
9. Food facility plan check, Orange County Health Care Agency, Environmental Health. Submit the plan check online with three sets of plans and specifications before construction; the fee is set at conditional approval. Fee: Varies. Takes: The initial plan review usually takes 20 working days. https://www.ochealthinfo.com/services-programs/environmental-health/plan-check
10. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
11. Food facility health permit, Orange County Health Care Agency, Environmental Health. 10. City of Irvine business license, City of Irvine Community Development, Business Licensing. A city tax rather than a regulatory license: apply online or at the public counter, confirm first that the use is allowed at the address, and display the license at the business. Fee: Varies. Takes: Irvine doesn't publish how long it takes to issue the license; the online application takes minutes, and new businesses must apply within 60 days of starting to avoid late fees. https://cityofirvine.gov/community-development/business-licensing
11. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
12. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. Takes: Nothing is filed with or approved by OEHHA, so there's no processing time; the business decides whether a warning is needed and must have it in place itself. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses

### Warehouses and 3PLs in Irvine
https://www.placetta.com/guides/irvine/warehouse-3pl.html
Opening a warehouse or 3PL in Irvine takes 12 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the LLC annual tax ($800). The fixed government fees add up to about $890, 4 fees are set by the space or the business and 5 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
8. Hazardous materials registration, Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (DOT). Filed online when you ship or offer certain hazardous materials in bulk, such as large lithium battery shipments. Fee: Varies. https://hazmatonline.phmsa.dot.gov/services/
9. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
10. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
11. City of Irvine business license, City of Irvine Community Development, Business Licensing. A city tax rather than a regulatory license: apply online or at the public counter, confirm first that the use is allowed at the address, and display the license at the business. Fee: Varies. Takes: Irvine doesn't publish how long it takes to issue the license; the online application takes minutes, and new businesses must apply within 60 days of starting to avoid late fees. https://cityofirvine.gov/community-development/business-licensing
12. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Orlando
https://www.placetta.com/guides/orlando/milk-tea-shop.html
Opening a milk tea shop in Orlando takes 10 filings with 8 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the florida public food service license. The fixed government fees add up to about $175, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 2 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation, Florida Division of Corporations (Sunbiz). Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: $125. https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Florida sales tax and reemployment tax registration, Florida Department of Revenue. Register online before you start doing business. The same application covers sales and use tax and reemployment tax, Florida's unemployment tax for employers. Fee: Varies. Takes: After registering online, the certificate number is available on the website after three business days. https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/registration
4. Registration of a fictitious name (DBA), Florida Department of State, Division of Corporations. Needed before doing business under any name other than the legal name. Advertise the name once in a newspaper in the county, then register online at Sunbiz or mail the form with the fee. Fee: $50. https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/start-business/efile/fl-fictitious-name-registration/
5. Certified food protection manager, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Food managers complete training and pass a certification exam from an accredited program within 30 days of starting the job, and the restaurant shows proof whenever an inspector asks. Fee: Varies. https://www2.myfloridalicense.com/hotels-restaurants/food-lodging/food-manager/
6. City of Orlando business tax receipt and certificate of use, City of Orlando, Permitting Services. Businesses inside city limits apply online with the Sunbiz registration, EIN and any state license; the certificate of use confirms the zoning allows the business. Get it before the county receipt. Fee: Varies. Takes: A billing summary within 10 business days of processing; the receipt is mailed after payment. https://orlando.opencounter.com/permits/business-tax-receipt
7. Orange County (FL) local business tax receipt, Orange County Tax Collector. Apply online or in person after the city receipt, uploading the city receipt, Sunbiz registration, any state license and the EIN. Fee: Varies. Takes: Orange County doesn't publish a processing time; Zoning must approve the business (and a CO is needed for new or altered space) before the Tax Collector issues the receipt. https://county-taxes.net/fl-orange/btexpress
8. Food service plan review, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Required for a space that is newly built, remodeled, converted from another use or reopening after 18 months closed; the state recommends approval before construction. Submit the plan with labeled equipment and a sample menu together with the new license application on DBPR Online. Fee: Free. https://www.myfloridalicense.com/intentions2.asp?chBoard=true&SID=&boardid=200&professionid=2010
9. Workers' compensation insurance, Florida Department of Financial Services, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://www.myfloridacfo.com/division/wc/employer/coverage-requirements
10. Florida public food service license, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Apply and pay on DBPR Online, one license for each operation. Once the plan review requirements are met, call 850-487-1395 several business days before opening to book the opening inspection; serve nobody until it passes and a temporary paper license is issued on the spot. Fee: Varies. Takes: Most applications are processed within a few business days; mailed ones take longer. https://www.myfloridalicense.com/intentions2.asp?chBoard=true&SID=&boardid=200&professionid=2010
What's different for a milk tea shop in Orlando:
- Florida's Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS) permits coffee shops and juice and smoothie bars, and DBPR licenses restaurants and fast food. Neither names tea shops, so Odelia confirms which one licenses yours before anything is filed. Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services: "These food establishments may include supermarkets, grocery stores, convenience stores, coffee shops, bakeries, retail meat markets, retail seafood markets, juice and smoothie bars," https://www.fdacs.gov/Business-Services/Food/Food-Establishments/Retail-Food-Establishment-Permit (read 2026-10-22)

10. City of Orlando business tax receipt and certificate of use, City of Orlando, Permitting Services. Businesses inside city limits apply online with the Sunbiz registration, EIN and any state license; the certificate of use confirms the zoning allows the business. Get it before the county receipt. Fee: Varies. Takes: A billing summary within 10 business days of processing; the receipt is mailed after payment. https://orlando.opencounter.com/permits/business-tax-receipt
11. Orange County (FL) local business tax receipt, Orange County Tax Collector. Apply online or in person after the city receipt, uploading the city receipt, Sunbiz registration, any state license and the EIN. Fee: Varies. Takes: Orange County doesn't publish a processing time; Zoning must approve the business (and a CO is needed for new or altered space) before the Tax Collector issues the receipt. https://county-taxes.net/fl-orange/btexpress
12. Workers' compensation insurance, Florida Department of Financial Services, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://www.myfloridacfo.com/division/wc/employer/coverage-requirements

### Toy stores in Orlando
https://www.placetta.com/guides/orlando/toy-store.html
Opening a toy store in Orlando takes 11 filings with 10 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the workers' compensation insurance. The fixed government fees add up to about $175, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 4 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation, Florida Division of Corporations (Sunbiz). Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: $125. https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Florida sales tax and reemployment tax registration, Florida Department of Revenue. Register online before you start doing business. The same application covers sales and use tax and reemployment tax, Florida's unemployment tax for employers. Fee: Varies. Takes: After registering online, the certificate number is available on the website after three business days. https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/registration
4. Registration of a fictitious name (DBA), Florida Department of State, Division of Corporations. Needed before doing business under any name other than the legal name. Advertise the name once in a newspaper in the county, then register online at Sunbiz or mail the form with the fee. Fee: $50. https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/start-business/efile/fl-fictitious-name-registration/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Children's Product Certificate, from a CPSC-accepted lab's tests, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). Children's furniture is tested by a third-party, CPSC-accepted laboratory to the children's product safety rules that apply, and the importer issues the certificate, with its test reports, in English, citing each rule. Since July 8, 2026 most certificates are eFiled with CBP at entry, so it is ready before the goods ship. There is no government form. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Testing-Certification/Childrens-Product-Certificate-CPC
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. City of Orlando business tax receipt and certificate of use, City of Orlando, Permitting Services. Businesses inside city limits apply online with the Sunbiz registration, EIN and any state license; the certificate of use confirms the zoning allows the business. Get it before the county receipt. Fee: Varies. Takes: A billing summary within 10 business days of processing; the receipt is mailed after payment. https://orlando.opencounter.com/permits/business-tax-receipt
10. Orange County (FL) local business tax receipt, Orange County Tax Collector. Apply online or in person after the city receipt, uploading the city receipt, Sunbiz registration, any state license and the EIN. Fee: Varies. Takes: Orange County doesn't publish a processing time; Zoning must approve the business (and a CO is needed for new or altered space) before the Tax Collector issues the receipt. https://county-taxes.net/fl-orange/btexpress
11. Workers' compensation insurance, Florida Department of Financial Services, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://www.myfloridacfo.com/division/wc/employer/coverage-requirements

### Restaurants in Fort Worth
https://www.placetta.com/guides/fort-worth/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Fort Worth takes 12 filings with 8 agencies, starting with the Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC) and ending with the franchise tax annual report. The fixed government fees add up to about $325, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 4 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants and dessert shops.
1. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Permit arrives in about 2 to 3 weeks. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Certified food manager, Texas Department of State Health Services. At least one manager passes an exam from a DSHS-licensed certified food manager program. Local health departments require a certified food manager on site whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. Takes: DSHS doesn't issue the certificate itself; the accredited exam provider issues it as soon as you pass the exam. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-managers
6. Food handler certificates for staff, Texas Department of State Health Services. Every employee who works with unpackaged food, equipment or food-contact surfaces finishes an accredited food handler course within 30 days of hire. Certified food managers are exempt. Fee: Varies. Takes: Each food employee must complete an accredited food handler course within 30 days of being hired; the training provider issues the card. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-handlers
7. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. Takes: Account number issued instantly online. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
8. Food establishment plan review, City of Fort Worth Consumer Health. Needed before a food establishment is built, extensively remodeled or converted; fees are paid before the review starts. Fee: Varies. Takes: Fort Worth Consumer Health doesn't publish a plan review time for food establishments. https://www.fortworthtexas.gov/departments/environmental-services/consumer-health/plan-review
9. Workers' compensation, or the yearly non-subscriber notice, Texas Department of Insurance, Division of Workers' Compensation. Texas doesn't require private employers to carry workers' compensation. An employer with one or more employees who doesn't carry it is a non-subscriber: it files DWC Form-005 every year between February 1 and April 30, and tells its employees. Fee: Varies. https://Www.Tdi.Texas.Gov/forms/dwc/dwc005nocovst.pdf
10. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Fort Worth Development Services. Every building used in Fort Worth needs one. Apply on Accela Citizen Access: same use as before is an existing-ordinance permit, a new use is a change of use with plan review. Issued after all final inspections pass. Fee: Varies. Takes: The CO is emailed to the permit contact on the business day after final approval. https://aca-prod.accela.com/CFW
11. Food establishment permit, City of Fort Worth Consumer Health. Issued by Consumer Health after the Certificate of Occupancy and a permit inspection, before any food preparation starts. Fee: Varies. Takes: Contact the inspector at least one week before your expected opening to schedule the inspection; the permit is issued once all requirements are met and fees are paid. https://www.fortworthtexas.gov/departments/environmental-services/consumer-health/plan-review
12. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. Takes: The Comptroller doesn't publish a processing time for the report; the annual franchise tax report is due May 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

What's different for a bakery in Fort Worth:
- Texas requires a Food Manufacturer license from the Department of State Health Services (DSHS) of a business that packages food for wholesale or for a self-service display, and lists bakeries among its examples. It applies if the bakery packages its goods that way. Texas Department of State Health Services: "Processing and/or packaging any food product, including dietary supplements, ice, and water, for wholesale distribution or for sale via retail customer self-service." https://dshs.texas.gov/foods/manufacturers.aspx (read 2026-10-22)

Apply on Accela Citizen Access: same use as before is an existing-ordinance permit, a new use is a change of use with plan review. Issued after all final inspections pass. Fee: Varies. Takes: The CO is emailed to the permit contact on the business day after final approval. https://aca-prod.accela.com/CFW
13. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. Takes: The Comptroller doesn't publish a processing time for the report; the annual franchise tax report is due May 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

### Toy stores in Fort Worth
https://www.placetta.com/guides/fort-worth/toy-store.html
Opening a toy store in Fort Worth takes 12 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC) and ending with the franchise tax annual report. The fixed government fees add up to about $325, 3 fees are set by the space or the business and 7 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Permit arrives in about 2 to 3 weeks. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Children's Product Certificate, from a CPSC-accepted lab's tests, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). Children's furniture is tested by a third-party, CPSC-accepted laboratory to the children's product safety rules that apply, and the importer issues the certificate, with its test reports, in English, citing each rule. Since July 8, 2026 most certificates are eFiled with CBP at entry, so it is ready before the goods ship. There is no government form. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Testing-Certification/Childrens-Product-Certificate-CPC
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. Takes: Account number issued instantly online. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
10. Workers' compensation, or the yearly non-subscriber notice, Texas Department of Insurance, Division of Workers' Compensation. Texas doesn't require private employers to carry workers' compensation. An employer with one or more employees who doesn't carry it is a non-subscriber: it files DWC Form-005 every year between February 1 and April 30, and tells its employees. Fee: Varies. https://Www.Tdi.Texas.Gov/forms/dwc/dwc005nocovst.pdf
11. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Fort Worth Development Services. Every building used in Fort Worth needs one. Apply on Accela Citizen Access: same use as before is an existing-ordinance permit, a new use is a change of use with plan review. Issued after all final inspections pass. Fee: Varies. Takes: The CO is emailed to the permit contact on the business day after final approval. https://aca-prod.accela.com/CFW
12. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. Takes: The Comptroller doesn't publish a processing time for the report; the annual franchise tax report is due May 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Phoenix
https://www.placetta.com/guides/phoenix/milk-tea-shop.html
Opening a milk tea shop in Phoenix takes 8 filings with 6 agencies, starting with the arizona LLC formation and ending with the food establishment permit. None of them has a fixed government fee, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 2 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to coffee shops.
1. Arizona LLC formation, Arizona Corporation Commission. File the Articles of Organization online, by mail or in person. Publication is required: if the statutory agent is in Maricopa or Pima County the Commission publishes it, otherwise publish a notice in a newspaper. Fee: Varies. Takes: Regular processing is typically 14 to 16 days. https://www.azcc.gov/docs/default-source/corps-files/forms/l010-articles-of-organization.pdf
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Transaction privilege tax (TPT) license, Arizona Department of Revenue. A business selling taxable products or services gets a license for each location, online on AZTaxes.gov or with the paper JT-1. The same application registers employers with the Department of Economic Security for unemployment insurance. Fee: Varies. Takes: Online, the license number is issued the same day and the certificate is mailed in 7 to 10 business days. https://azdor.gov/transaction-privilege-tax/tpt-license/applying-tpt-license
4. Certified food protection manager, Maricopa County Environmental Services. Each food establishment keeps at least one certified food protection manager on staff, and replaces one who leaves within 90 days. Fee: Varies. https://www.maricopa.gov/DocumentCenter/View/5475/Chapter-7---Food-Employees-Certified-Food-Protection-Managers-PDF
5. Food establishment plan review, Maricopa County Environmental Services. Apply in the county Permit Center with the supporting documents before construction starts; the county advises applying 6 to 8 weeks ahead. Fee: Varies. Takes: Maricopa County recommends applying at least 6 to 8 weeks before construction starts; if you'll finish within 15 business days of submitting, you must pay for expedited review. https://maricopacountyaz-energovweb.tylerhost.net/apps/selfservice#/home
6. Employer registration for withholding and unemployment insurance (JT-1), Arizona Department of Revenue, with the Arizona Department of Economic Security. An employer that withholds Arizona income tax registers its EIN with ADOR on the Joint Tax Application in AZTaxes.gov; the same form starts the unemployment insurance registration with DES. Fee: Free. https://www.aztaxes.gov
7. Building permit and Certificate of Occupancy, City of Phoenix Planning and Development. Tenant improvements of a newly occupied space or a change of occupancy go through plan review; the Certificate of Occupancy is generated once all inspections pass and stays with the address. Phoenix doesn't issue a general business license. Fee: Varies. Takes: Phoenix issues the Certificate of Occupancy 24 hours after the final inspection and mails it to the owner. https://www.phoenix.gov/administration/departments/pdd/commercial-multifamily-building/commercial-process-overview.html
8. Food establishment permit, Maricopa County Environmental Services. Apply in the county Permit Center; after the final inspection, pay the annual permit fee to receive the permit and open. Fee: Varies. Takes: After you apply, expect an email with your permit number and payment instructions within 2 business days; the permit itself follows plan review, inspection and fee payment. https://maricopacountyaz-energovweb.tylerhost.net/apps/selfservice#/home
What's different for a milk tea shop in Phoenix:
- Maricopa County sets an Eating and Drinking permit's class by the menu: quick service with only limited preparation is Class 2, the lowest; advanced preparation of three or more menu items is Class 4. The department decides which yours is. Maricopa County Environmental Services: "Quick service operations with only limited preparation of menu items or as approved by the Department." https://listos.maricopa.gov/DocumentCenter/View/44074/Permit-Type-Class-and-Inspection-Frequency-PDF (read 2026-10-22)

Tenant improvements of a newly occupied space or a change of occupancy go through plan review; the Certificate of Occupancy is generated once all inspections pass and stays with the address. Phoenix doesn't issue a general business license. Fee: Varies. Takes: Phoenix issues the Certificate of Occupancy 24 hours after the final inspection and mails it to the owner. https://www.phoenix.gov/administration/departments/pdd/commercial-multifamily-building/commercial-process-overview.html

### Cosmetics stores in Phoenix
https://www.placetta.com/guides/phoenix/cosmetics-store.html
Opening a cosmetics store in Phoenix takes 10 filings with 8 agencies, starting with the arizona LLC formation and ending with the Building permit and Certificate of Occupancy. None of them has a fixed government fee, 4 fees are set by the space or the business and 6 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Arizona LLC formation, Arizona Corporation Commission. File the Articles of Organization online, by mail or in person. Publication is required: if the statutory agent is in Maricopa or Pima County the Commission publishes it, otherwise publish a notice in a newspaper. Fee: Varies. Takes: Regular processing is typically 14 to 16 days. https://www.azcc.gov/docs/default-source/corps-files/forms/l010-articles-of-organization.pdf
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Transaction privilege tax (TPT) license, Arizona Department of Revenue. A business selling taxable products or services gets a license for each location, online on AZTaxes.gov or with the paper JT-1. The same application registers employers with the Department of Economic Security for unemployment insurance. Fee: Varies. Takes: Online, the license number is issued the same day and the certificate is mailed in 7 to 10 business days. https://azdor.gov/transaction-privilege-tax/tpt-license/applying-tpt-license
4. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Employer registration for withholding and unemployment insurance (JT-1), Arizona Department of Revenue, with the Arizona Department of Economic Security. An employer that withholds Arizona income tax registers its EIN with ADOR on the Joint Tax Application in AZTaxes.gov; the same form starts the unemployment insurance registration with DES. Fee: Free. https://www.aztaxes.gov
10. Building permit and Certificate of Occupancy, City of Phoenix Planning and Development. Tenant improvements of a newly occupied space or a change of occupancy go through plan review; the Certificate of Occupancy is generated once all inspections pass and stays with the address. Phoenix doesn't issue a general business license. Fee: Varies. Takes: Phoenix issues the Certificate of Occupancy 24 hours after the final inspection and mails it to the owner. https://www.phoenix.gov/administration/departments/pdd/commercial-multifamily-building/commercial-process-overview.html

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Oakland
https://www.placetta.com/guides/oakland/milk-tea-shop.html
Opening a milk tea shop in Oakland takes 13 filings with 10 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the LLC annual tax ($800). The fixed government fees add up to about $890, 7 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to coffee shops.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113947.1
6. Food handler cards for staff, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. Every employee who prepares, stores or handles food gets a California Food Handler Card from an accredited course within 30 days of hire; the card is good for 3 years. Anyone holding a valid food manager certificate is exempt. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113948
7. Oakland zoning clearance, City of Oakland Planning and Building Department. Every business operating in Oakland gets one for its location before the business tax certificate, and again when it moves or changes owner. Apply in the city's Online Permit Center with the street address, parcel number and a description of the business; payment is due when you submit. Some uses first need a conditional use permit. Fee: Varies. https://aca-prod.accela.com/OAKLAND/urlrouting.ashx?type=1002&IsSkipDisclaimer=Y&module=Planning&CAPType=Planning/Applications/Counter/Zoning+Clearance
8. City of Oakland business tax certificate, City of Oakland Finance Department, Business Tax Office. Apply online or at the Business Tax Office, listing the zoning clearance and, if you sell goods, the California seller's permit. Fees are due within 30 days of the business start date. Fee: Varies. Takes: Once the application is accepted and paid, the certificate is emailed within 5 days. https://oakland.hdlgov.com/
9. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
10. Food facility plan check, Alameda County Environmental Health Department. Plans must be approved before any new construction or remodel starts. Bring one set of plans drawn at 1/4 inch per foot with equipment spec sheets, the menu, the water heater and hood worksheets, and the plan check questionnaire and worksheet with payment to 1131 Harbor Bay Parkway, Alameda. After approval, three sets are stamped and two go to the city for the building permits. Fee: Varies. Takes: A first response within 20 working days, or 7 with expedited review; approved plans stay valid for half a year. https://health.alamedacountyca.gov/alameda-county-plan-check-guide-for-retail-food-facilities/
11. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
12. Health permit to operate a food facility, Alameda County Environmental Health Department. After the rough plumbing, pre-final and final inspections (book each at least 48 hours ahead), complete the permit application; the permit is issued once the fees are paid. Fee: Varies. https://health.alamedacountyca.gov/alameda-county-plan-check-guide-for-retail-food-facilities/
13. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
What's different for a milk tea shop in Oakland:
- Under California's food code, a food facility in a building built after January 1, 2004 that gives customers space to eat or drink on the premises must provide clean restrooms for them. The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-22)
