Bring one set of plans drawn at 1/4 inch per foot with equipment spec sheets, the menu, the water heater and hood worksheets, and the plan check questionnaire and worksheet with payment to 1131 Harbor Bay Parkway, Alameda. After approval, three sets are stamped and two go to the city for the building permits. Fee: Varies. Takes: A first response within 20 working days, or 7 with expedited review; approved plans stay valid for half a year. https://health.alamedacountyca.gov/alameda-county-plan-check-guide-for-retail-food-facilities/
11. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
12. Health permit to operate a food facility, Alameda County Environmental Health Department. After the rough plumbing, pre-final and final inspections (book each at least 48 hours ahead), complete the permit application; the permit is issued once the fees are paid. Fee: Varies. https://health.alamedacountyca.gov/alameda-county-plan-check-guide-for-retail-food-facilities/
13. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
What's different for a bakery in Oakland:
- Under California's food code, a food facility in a building built after January 1, 2004 that gives customers space to eat or drink on the premises must provide clean restrooms for them. The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-22)
- California's Processed Food Registration, from the Department of Public Health, covers bakery products. A retail food facility that sells directly to consumers under a county health permit is exempt, so a bakery selling only over its own counter doesn't need it; making goods for other stores or cafes falls outside that exemption. California Department of Public Health: "General foods such as bakery products, noodles, seafood (except molluscan shellfish)" https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CEH/DFDCS/Pages/FDBPrograms/FoodSafetyProgram/PFRFAQs.aspx (read 2026-10-21)

### Grocery stores in Oakland
https://www.placetta.com/guides/oakland/grocery-store.html
Opening a grocery store in Oakland takes 11 filings with 10 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the proposition 65 warning labels. The fixed government fees add up to about $890, 4 fees are set by the space or the business and 4 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. Oakland zoning clearance, City of Oakland Planning and Building Department. Every business operating in Oakland gets one for its location before the business tax certificate, and again when it moves or changes owner. Apply in the city's Online Permit Center with the street address, parcel number and a description of the business; payment is due when you submit. Some uses first need a conditional use permit. Fee: Varies. https://aca-prod.accela.com/OAKLAND/urlrouting.ashx?type=1002&IsSkipDisclaimer=Y&module=Planning&CAPType=Planning/Applications/Counter/Zoning+Clearance
6. City of Oakland business tax certificate, City of Oakland Finance Department, Business Tax Office. Apply online or at the Business Tax Office, listing the zoning clearance and, if you sell goods, the California seller's permit. Fees are due within 30 days of the business start date. Fee: Varies. Takes: Once the application is accepted and paid, the certificate is emailed within 5 days. https://oakland.hdlgov.com/
7. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
8. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
9. Health permit to operate a food facility, Alameda County Environmental Health Department. After the rough plumbing, pre-final and final inspections (book each at least 48 hours ahead), complete the permit application; the permit is issued once the fees are paid. Fee: Varies. https://health.alamedacountyca.gov/alameda-county-plan-check-guide-for-retail-food-facilities/
10. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
11. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. Takes: Nothing is filed with or approved by OEHHA, so there's no processing time; the business decides whether a warning is needed and must have it in place itself. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses

Fee: Varies. https://aca-prod.accela.com/OAKLAND/urlrouting.ashx?type=1002&IsSkipDisclaimer=Y&module=Planning&CAPType=Planning/Applications/Counter/Zoning+Clearance
9. City of Oakland business tax certificate, City of Oakland Finance Department, Business Tax Office. Apply online or at the Business Tax Office, listing the zoning clearance and, if you sell goods, the California seller's permit. Fees are due within 30 days of the business start date. Fee: Varies. Takes: Once the application is accepted and paid, the certificate is emailed within 5 days. https://oakland.hdlgov.com/
10. Hazardous materials registration, Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (DOT). Filed online when you ship or offer certain hazardous materials in bulk, such as large lithium battery shipments. Fee: Varies. https://hazmatonline.phmsa.dot.gov/services/
11. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
12. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
13. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Sacramento
https://www.placetta.com/guides/sacramento/milk-tea-shop.html
Opening a milk tea shop in Sacramento takes 12 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the LLC annual tax ($800). The fixed government fees add up to about $890, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to coffee shops.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113947.1
6. Food handler cards for staff, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. Every employee who prepares, stores or handles food gets a California Food Handler Card from an accredited course within 30 days of hire; the card is good for 3 years. Anyone holding a valid food manager certificate is exempt. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113948
7. City of Sacramento business tax certificate (Business Operations Tax), City of Sacramento Finance Department, Revenue Division. Every business operating in the City of Sacramento pays this yearly tax; the city issues no separate business license. Apply online, by email to finance@cityofsacramento.org, by mail or in person, and pay when you apply. The city sends the application to Community Development to confirm the zoning, then mails the certificate. Fee: Varies. https://cityofsacramento.gov/finance/revenue/business-operations-tax
8. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
9. Food facility plan review, Sacramento County Environmental Management Department. Needed to build a new food facility or convert a space into one. Mail or bring the application with one complete set of scaled plans and equipment spec sheets to 11080 White Rock Rd, Suite 200, Rancho Cordova, or email EHPlanReview@SacCounty.gov to submit electronically; three sets are needed at final approval. You're directed to the application to operate when you submit the plans. Fee: Varies. Takes: The county doesn't publish a review time; the application and its approval expire a year after submittal. https://emd.saccounty.gov/content/dam/emd/docs/transition/Application%20for%20Food%20Facility%20Plan%20Review%202026-2027.pdf
10. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
11. Health permit to operate a food facility, Sacramento County Environmental Management Department. Submit the application to operate and pay the fees before the place opens. A certified food manager is needed within 60 days of opening, and every food employee needs a current food handler card. Fee: Varies. https://emd.saccounty.gov/us/en/environmental-health/retail-food-protection-program/selling-food-in-sacramento-county.html
12. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
What's different for a milk tea shop in Sacramento:
- Under California's food code, a food facility in a building built after January 1, 2004 that gives customers space to eat or drink on the premises must provide clean restrooms for them. The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-22)

5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
9. Packaging producer registration (EPR), CalRecycle, through Circular Action Alliance. A producer of packaged goods sold in California applies to participate in Circular Action Alliance's plan, submits an independent producer application, or obtains a small producer exemption; CalRecycle's PEPRS portal or the PRO takes the registration and the reports. Fee: Varies. https://calrecycle.ca.gov/packaging/packaging-epr/producerguidance/
10. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
11. City of Sacramento business tax certificate (Business Operations Tax), City of Sacramento Finance Department, Revenue Division. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
13. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
14. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
15. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. Takes: Nothing is filed with or approved by OEHHA, so there's no processing time; the business decides whether a warning is needed and must have it in place itself. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses

### Toy stores in Sacramento
https://www.placetta.com/guides/sacramento/toy-store.html
Opening a toy store in Sacramento takes 14 filings with 12 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the proposition 65 warning labels. The fixed government fees add up to about $890, 4 fees are set by the space or the business and 7 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Children's Product Certificate, from a CPSC-accepted lab's tests, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). Children's furniture is tested by a third-party, CPSC-accepted laboratory to the children's product safety rules that apply, and the importer issues the certificate, with its test reports, in English, citing each rule. Since July 8, 2026 most certificates are eFiled with CBP at entry, so it is ready before the goods ship. There is no government form. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Testing-Certification/Childrens-Product-Certificate-CPC
8. Packaging producer registration (EPR), CalRecycle, through Circular Action Alliance. A producer of packaged goods sold in California applies to participate in Circular Action Alliance's plan, submits an independent producer application, or obtains a small producer exemption; CalRecycle's PEPRS portal or the PRO takes the registration and the reports. Fee: Varies. https://calrecycle.ca.gov/packaging/packaging-epr/producerguidance/
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. City of Sacramento business tax certificate (Business Operations Tax), City of Sacramento Finance Department, Revenue Division. Every business operating in the City of Sacramento pays this yearly tax; the city issues no separate business license. Apply online, by email to finance@cityofsacramento.org, by mail or in person, and pay when you apply. The city sends the application to Community Development to confirm the zoning, then mails the certificate. Fee: Varies. https://cityofsacramento.gov/finance/revenue/business-operations-tax
11. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
12. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm

### Restaurants in Portland
https://www.placetta.com/guides/portland/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Portland takes 7 filings with 6 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (Oregon LLC) and ending with the Multnomah County restaurant license. The fixed government fees add up to about $100, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants and dessert shops.
1. Articles of Organization (Oregon LLC), Oregon Secretary of State, Corporation Division. Filed online with the Corporation Division's business registry, or on the paper form. Fee: $100. https://sos.oregon.gov/business/Documents/business-registry-forms/llc-articles.pdf
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Portland business tax registration, City of Portland Revenue Division. One Revenue Division account covers the Portland Business License Tax, the Multnomah County Business Income Tax and the Metro Supportive Housing Services tax. Register online in Portland Revenue Online with the tax ID, entity type, locations and owners, or mail, fax or bring the paper form. Fee: Varies. https://pro.portland.gov/?Link=Register
4. Oregon employer registration (payroll taxes), Oregon Department of Revenue, with the Oregon Employment Department. Every employer with paid employees in Oregon registers before the first paycheck, online in Revenue Online or the Oregon Business Registry, or on the paper Combined Employer's Registration sent to the Employment Department. One number covers withholding, unemployment tax, the Workers' Benefit Fund and transit taxes. Fee: Varies. Takes: The state gives 30 business days online (60 on paper), and up to 14 business days through the Oregon Business Registry. https://revenueonline.dor.oregon.gov/tap/_/?Link=BIN
5. Restaurant plan review, Multnomah County Environmental Health. Needed before opening a new restaurant or remodeling one. Send the plan review application, the plans and the fee; construction can start once the approval letter arrives. Fee: Varies. Takes: A response within 15 business days of receiving it. https://multco.us/file/restaurant_plan_review_application/download
6. Workers' compensation insurance, Oregon Department of Consumer and Business Services, Workers' Compensation Division. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://wcd.oregon.gov/employer/pages/compensation-insurance-overview.aspx
7. Multnomah County restaurant license, Multnomah County Environmental Health. Send the license application and fee (it can go with the plan review), then call for the pre-opening inspection once construction is done; you get the license and can open after it passes. Restaurant workers need food handler cards. Fee: Varies. Takes: The pre-opening inspection can take up to 5 business days to schedule. https://multco.us/file/restaurant/bed_&_breakfast_license_application/download

What's different for a bakery in Portland:
- In Oregon the Department of Agriculture (ODA) licenses bakeries, and the county health department licenses restaurants. A bakery with a cafe is licensed by one of them, by its predominant activity: food for later (ODA) or food to eat right away (the county). Oregon Department of Agriculture: "ODA licenses and inspects firms including grocery stores, wineries, breweries, food processors, and bakeries." https://www.oregon.gov/oda/Documents/Publications/foodsafety/CombinationFacilities.pdf (read 2026-10-22)

Children's furniture is tested by a third-party, CPSC-accepted laboratory to the children's product safety rules that apply, and the importer issues the certificate, with its test reports, in English, citing each rule. Since July 8, 2026 most certificates are eFiled with CBP at entry, so it is ready before the goods ship. There is no government form. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Testing-Certification/Childrens-Product-Certificate-CPC
6. Oregon packaging producer responsibility (EPR): join the PRO, unless exempt, Oregon Department of Environmental Quality, through Circular Action Alliance. The brand that imports packaged goods sold into Oregon registers with the producer responsibility organization (Circular Action Alliance) and pays its annual membership fee. Exempt: under $5 million gross revenue, under one metric ton of covered products into Oregon, or a single store with no online sales. Fee: Varies. https://www.oregon.gov/deq/recycling/Documents/RMAProducerObligationsSummary.pdf
7. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
8. Portland business tax registration, City of Portland Revenue Division. One Revenue Division account covers the Portland Business License Tax, the Multnomah County Business Income Tax and the Metro Supportive Housing Services tax. Register online in Portland Revenue Online with the tax ID, entity type, locations and owners, or mail, fax or bring the paper form. Fee: Varies. https://pro.portland.gov/?Link=Register
9. Oregon employer registration (payroll taxes), Oregon Department of Revenue, with the Oregon Employment Department. Every employer with paid employees in Oregon registers before the first paycheck, online in Revenue Online or the Oregon Business Registry, or on the paper Combined Employer's Registration sent to the Employment Department. One number covers withholding, unemployment tax, the Workers' Benefit Fund and transit taxes. Fee: Varies. Takes: The state gives 30 business days online (60 on paper), and up to 14 business days through the Oregon Business Registry. https://revenueonline.dor.oregon.gov/tap/_/?Link=BIN
10. Workers' compensation insurance, Oregon Department of Consumer and Business Services, Workers' Compensation Division. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://wcd.oregon.gov/employer/pages/compensation-insurance-overview.aspx

### Importers and online sellers in Portland
https://www.placetta.com/guides/portland/importer-ecommerce.html
Opening an importer or e-commerce seller in Portland takes 8 filings with 6 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (Oregon LLC) and ending with the portland business tax registration. The fixed government fees add up to about $100, 3 fees are set by the space or the business and 4 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Articles of Organization (Oregon LLC), Oregon Secretary of State, Corporation Division. Filed online with the Corporation Division's business registry, or on the paper form. Fee: $100. https://sos.oregon.gov/business/Documents/business-registry-forms/llc-articles.pdf
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
4. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
5. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
6. Oregon packaging producer responsibility (EPR): join the PRO, unless exempt, Oregon Department of Environmental Quality, through Circular Action Alliance. The brand that imports packaged goods sold into Oregon registers with the producer responsibility organization (Circular Action Alliance) and pays its annual membership fee. Exempt: under $5 million gross revenue, under one metric ton of covered products into Oregon, or a single store with no online sales. Fee: Varies. https://www.oregon.gov/deq/recycling/Documents/RMAProducerObligationsSummary.pdf
7. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
8. Portland business tax registration, City of Portland Revenue Division. One Revenue Division account covers the Portland Business License Tax, the Multnomah County Business Income Tax and the Metro Supportive Housing Services tax. Register online in Portland Revenue Online with the tax ID, entity type, locations and owners, or mail, fax or bring the paper form. Fee: Varies. https://pro.portland.gov/?Link=Register

### Restaurants in Plano
https://www.placetta.com/guides/plano/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Plano takes 12 filings with 8 agencies, starting with the Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC) and ending with the franchise tax annual report. The fixed government fees add up to about $800, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 4 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants and dessert shops.
1. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Permit arrives in about 2 to 3 weeks. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Certified food manager, Texas Department of State Health Services. At least one manager passes an exam from a DSHS-licensed certified food manager program. Local health departments require a certified food manager on site whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. Takes: DSHS doesn't issue the certificate itself; the accredited exam provider issues it as soon as you pass the exam. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-managers
6. Food handler certificates for staff, Texas Department of State Health Services. Every employee who works with unpackaged food, equipment or food-contact surfaces finishes an accredited food handler course within 30 days of hire. Certified food managers are exempt. Fee: Varies. Takes: Each food employee must complete an accredited food handler course within 30 days of being hired; the training provider issues the card. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-handlers
7. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. Takes: Account number issued instantly online. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
8. Food establishment plan review, City of Plano Environmental Health and Sustainability. Submit the plans to Building Inspections with the Environmental Health review form and the fee; construction starts only after written approval. The fee covers the two required inspections, and every fee is paid before approval to operate. Fee: $475. Takes: Notice within 10 business days of submission; revised plans can take another 10. Reviews aren't expedited. https://content.civicplus.com/api/assets/234824a7-ef4c-481f-8b7b-ab68b680a9fb
9. Workers' compensation, or the yearly non-subscriber notice, Texas Department of Insurance, Division of Workers' Compensation. Texas doesn't require private employers to carry workers' compensation. An employer with one or more employees who doesn't carry it is a non-subscriber: it files DWC Form-005 every year between February 1 and April 30, and tells its employees. Fee: Varies. https://Www.Tdi.Texas.Gov/forms/dwc/dwc005nocovst.pdf
10. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Plano Building Inspections. Required to occupy any nonresidential space, and again when the business, its name or owner changes or a new tenant moves in. Submit the packet with the application fee; Building Inspections, Planning and, for a restaurant, Environmental Health review it and inspect. It must be approved before staff move in, stock arrives or the doors open, and it's posted on site. Fee: Varies. https://content.civicplus.com/api/assets/tx-plano/d2490980-662a-4f38-8def-66070c8691e5
11. Food establishment permit, City of Plano Environmental Health and Sustainability. Issued by the city's Environmental Health division once the fee is paid; the business may not open before its Certificate of Occupancy is issued. Fee: Varies. https://www.plano.gov/food-permits
12. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. Takes: The Comptroller doesn't publish a processing time for the report; the annual franchise tax report is due May 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

- Texas requires a Food Manufacturer license from the Department of State Health Services (DSHS) of a business that packages food for wholesale or for a self-service display, and lists bakeries among its examples. It applies if the bakery packages its goods that way. Texas Department of State Health Services: "Processing and/or packaging any food product, including dietary supplements, ice, and water, for wholesale distribution or for sale via retail customer self-service." https://dshs.texas.gov/foods/manufacturers.aspx (read 2026-10-22)

It must be approved before staff move in, stock arrives or the doors open, and it's posted on site. Fee: Varies. https://content.civicplus.com/api/assets/tx-plano/d2490980-662a-4f38-8def-66070c8691e5
13. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. Takes: The Comptroller doesn't publish a processing time for the report; the annual franchise tax report is due May 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

### Toy stores in Plano
https://www.placetta.com/guides/plano/toy-store.html
Opening a toy store in Plano takes 12 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC) and ending with the franchise tax annual report. The fixed government fees add up to about $325, 3 fees are set by the space or the business and 7 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Permit arrives in about 2 to 3 weeks. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Children's Product Certificate, from a CPSC-accepted lab's tests, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). Children's furniture is tested by a third-party, CPSC-accepted laboratory to the children's product safety rules that apply, and the importer issues the certificate, with its test reports, in English, citing each rule. Since July 8, 2026 most certificates are eFiled with CBP at entry, so it is ready before the goods ship. There is no government form. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Testing-Certification/Childrens-Product-Certificate-CPC
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. Takes: Account number issued instantly online. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
10. Workers' compensation, or the yearly non-subscriber notice, Texas Department of Insurance, Division of Workers' Compensation. Texas doesn't require private employers to carry workers' compensation. An employer with one or more employees who doesn't carry it is a non-subscriber: it files DWC Form-005 every year between February 1 and April 30, and tells its employees. Fee: Varies. https://Www.Tdi.Texas.Gov/forms/dwc/dwc005nocovst.pdf
11. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Plano Building Inspections. Required to occupy any nonresidential space, and again when the business, its name or owner changes or a new tenant moves in. Submit the packet with the application fee; Building Inspections, Planning and, for a restaurant, Environmental Health review it and inspect. It must be approved before staff move in, stock arrives or the doors open, and it's posted on site. Fee: Varies. https://content.civicplus.com/api/assets/tx-plano/d2490980-662a-4f38-8def-66070c8691e5
12. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. Takes: The Comptroller doesn't publish a processing time for the report; the annual franchise tax report is due May 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

### Coffee shops in Arlington
https://www.placetta.com/guides/arlington/coffee-shop.html
Opening a coffee shop in Arlington takes 10 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the LLC formation (Articles of Organization) and ending with the Arlington County food establishment license. The fixed government fees add up to about $40, 8 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation (Articles of Organization), Virginia State Corporation Commission, Clerk's Office. Formed online in the Clerk's Information System: Online Services, Virginia Entity, Limited Liability Company, Articles of Organization; the system builds the filing image, and the fee is paid at checkout. Fee: Varies. https://cis.scc.virginia.gov/
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Virginia business tax registration, Virginia Department of Taxation. Every new business registers online with Virginia Tax, or on paper Form R-1 if it can't: sales and use tax for dealers, and employer withholding with Virginia employees. Fee: Varies. https://account.tax.virginia.gov/online-services/?link=businessregistration
4. Certified food protection manager, Virginia Department of Health, with local health departments. Every Virginia food establishment, unless exempt, has at least one employee with authority over food preparation and service who holds a food protection manager certificate from a program accredited through the Conference for Food Protection. Arlington and Fairfax County check for it before opening. Fee: Varies. https://www.vdh.virginia.gov/environmental-health/food-safety-in-virginia/cfpm/
5. Commercial building permit, Arlington County Permit Office. A new establishment or an alteration goes through the county's Permit Office with its commercial building permit submission. Fee: Varies. https://arlingtonva.us/Government/Programs/Health/Environmental-Health/Food-Establishment-Plans-Construction
6. Arlington County business license, Arlington County Commissioner of Revenue, Business Tax Division. After the state requirements and the county permits, register the business in CAPP, the county's online system; a Business Tax Inspector then contacts you to finish the license. Fee: Varies. https://www.arlingtonva.us/Government/Programs/Taxes/Business-License-and-Taxes
7. Unemployment insurance employer registration, Virginia Employment Commission. A business with employees in Virginia must by law register with the VEC: online through iFile and iReg, or by mailing the FC-27. Fee: Varies. https://vec.virginia.gov/tax-filing-registration
8. Food service plan review, Arlington County Public Health Division, Environmental Health Program. For a new place or a major alteration. Send the application with the building plans, site plan, equipment schedule and the certified food protection manager certificate to ehealth@arlingtonva.us or 2110 Washington Blvd, Suite 350, and pay the fee online. A pre-opening inspection with the equipment in place and working follows. Fee: $40. https://www.arlingtonva.us/files/sharedassets/public/v/7/health/documents/eh-applications/food-service-plan-review-application_2025.06.20.pdf
9. Workers' compensation insurance, Virginia Workers' Compensation Commission. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://workcomp.virginia.gov/content/employers
10. Arlington County food establishment license, Arlington County Public Health Division, Environmental Health Program. Any place selling prepared or packaged food needs the county's food establishment license. Before opening, a certified food protection manager must be in place and present during all operating hours. Fee: Varies. https://arlingtonva.us/Government/Programs/Health/Environmental-Health/Food-Establishment-Plans-Construction
What's different for a coffee shop in Arlington:
- Under Virginia's agreement between its health and agriculture departments, a shop serving coffee and baked goods to eat on site, with no wholesale, is the health department's to license and inspect. Selling baked goods wholesale brings in the Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services. Virginia Department of Health: "there is no wholesale distribution (e.g., coffee and baked goods without wholesale)" https://www.vdh.virginia.gov/content/uploads/sites/20/VDH-VDACS-Retail-MOU-Signed-2025.pdf (read 2026-10-22)

3. Virginia business tax registration, Virginia Department of Taxation. 4. Arlington County business license, Arlington County Commissioner of Revenue, Business Tax Division. Fee: Varies. https://www.arlingtonva.us/Government/Programs/Taxes/Business-License-and-Taxes

8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling

### Coffee shops in Fairfax County
https://www.placetta.com/guides/fairfax-county/coffee-shop.html
Opening a coffee shop in Fairfax County takes 10 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the LLC formation (Articles of Organization) and ending with the food establishment permit to operate. None of them has a fixed government fee, 9 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation (Articles of Organization), Virginia State Corporation Commission, Clerk's Office. Formed online in the Clerk's Information System: Online Services, Virginia Entity, Limited Liability Company, Articles of Organization; the system builds the filing image, and the fee is paid at checkout. Fee: Varies. https://cis.scc.virginia.gov/
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Virginia business tax registration, Virginia Department of Taxation. Every new business registers online with Virginia Tax, or on paper Form R-1 if it can't: sales and use tax for dealers, and employer withholding with Virginia employees. Fee: Varies. https://account.tax.virginia.gov/online-services/?link=businessregistration
4. Certified food protection manager, Virginia Department of Health, with local health departments. Every Virginia food establishment, unless exempt, has at least one employee with authority over food preparation and service who holds a food protection manager certificate from a program accredited through the Conference for Food Protection. Arlington and Fairfax County check for it before opening. Fee: Varies. https://www.vdh.virginia.gov/environmental-health/food-safety-in-virginia/cfpm/
5. Fairfax County business license (BPOL), Fairfax County Department of Tax Administration. Every business with a physical location in the county files within 75 days of starting there, or pays a 10% late penalty; no tax is owed until gross receipts pass $10,000 in a year. Inside the cities of Fairfax and Falls Church and the towns of Clifton, Herndon and Vienna, the license comes from that city or town instead. Fee: Varies. Takes: The official license can take 4 to 6 weeks; the filed receipt serves until then. https://www.fairfaxcounty.gov/taxes/business/business-forms
6. Unemployment insurance employer registration, Virginia Employment Commission. A business with employees in Virginia must by law register with the VEC: online through iFile and iReg, or by mailing the FC-27. Fee: Varies. https://vec.virginia.gov/tax-filing-registration
7. Food establishment plan review, Fairfax County Health Department, Division of Environmental Health. Plans go in through the PLUS portal before construction, remodeling or conversion starts; work can't begin until the Health Department finishes its commercial plan review. Fee: Varies. https://plus.fairfaxcounty.gov
8. Workers' compensation insurance, Virginia Workers' Compensation Commission. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://workcomp.virginia.gov/content/employers
9. Non-Residential Use Permit, Fairfax County Land Development Services. Under the zoning ordinance no commercial space may be occupied, and no use changed, until this permit is approved; it is the county's certificate of use and occupancy. Applied for in PLUS. After opening, book the Fire Marshal's post-occupancy inspection within 10 days. Fee: Varies. https://plus.fairfaxcounty.gov/CitizenAccess/Welcome.aspx
10. Food establishment permit to operate, Fairfax County Health Department, Division of Environmental Health. Apply in PLUS, then call at least 3 days ahead for the pre-occupancy inspection, where a food manager with an accredited exam certificate must be present. The permit to operate is issued once the inspection passes. Fee: Varies. Takes: Mailed within 5 to 7 days of passing the pre-occupancy inspection. https://plus.fairfaxcounty.gov
What's different for a coffee shop in Fairfax County:
- Under Virginia's agreement between its health and agriculture departments, a shop serving coffee and baked goods to eat on site, with no wholesale, is the health department's to license and inspect. Selling baked goods wholesale brings in the Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services. Virginia Department of Health: "there is no wholesale distribution (e.g., coffee and baked goods without wholesale)" https://www.vdh.virginia.gov/content/uploads/sites/20/VDH-VDACS-Retail-MOU-Signed-2025.pdf (read 2026-10-22)

Arlington and Fairfax County check for it before opening. Fee: Varies. https://www.vdh.virginia.gov/environmental-health/food-safety-in-virginia/cfpm/
5. Fairfax County business license (BPOL), Fairfax County Department of Tax Administration. Every business with a physical location in the county files within 75 days of starting there, or pays a 10% late penalty; no tax is owed until gross receipts pass $10,000 in a year. Inside the cities of Fairfax and Falls Church and the towns of Clifton, Herndon and Vienna, the license comes from that city or town instead. Fee: Varies. Takes: The official license can take 4 to 6 weeks; the filed receipt serves until then. https://www.fairfaxcounty.gov/taxes/business/business-forms
6. Unemployment insurance employer registration, Virginia Employment Commission. A business with employees in Virginia must by law register with the VEC: online through iFile and iReg, or by mailing the FC-27. Fee: Varies. https://vec.virginia.gov/tax-filing-registration
7. Workers' compensation insurance, Virginia Workers' Compensation Commission. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://workcomp.virginia.gov/content/employers
8. Non-Residential Use Permit, Fairfax County Land Development Services. Under the zoning ordinance no commercial space may be occupied, and no use changed, until this permit is approved; it is the county's certificate of use and occupancy. Applied for in PLUS. After opening, book the Fire Marshal's post-occupancy inspection within 10 days. Fee: Varies. https://plus.fairfaxcounty.gov/CitizenAccess/Welcome.aspx
9. Food establishment permit to operate, Fairfax County Health Department, Division of Environmental Health. Apply in PLUS, then call at least 3 days ahead for the pre-occupancy inspection, where a food manager with an accredited exam certificate must be present. The permit to operate is issued once the inspection passes. Fee: Varies. Takes: Mailed within 5 to 7 days of passing the pre-occupancy inspection. https://plus.fairfaxcounty.gov

### Retail stores in Fairfax County
https://www.placetta.com/guides/fairfax-county/retail-store.html
Opening a retail store in Fairfax County takes 7 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the LLC formation (Articles of Organization) and ending with the Non-Residential Use Permit. None of them has a fixed government fee, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation (Articles of Organization), Virginia State Corporation Commission, Clerk's Office. Formed online in the Clerk's Information System: Online Services, Virginia Entity, Limited Liability Company, Articles of Organization; the system builds the filing image, and the fee is paid at checkout. Fee: Varies. https://cis.scc.virginia.gov/
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Virginia business tax registration, Virginia Department of Taxation. Every new business registers online with Virginia Tax, or on paper Form R-1 if it can't: sales and use tax for dealers, and employer withholding with Virginia employees. Fee: Varies. https://account.tax.virginia.gov/online-services/?link=businessregistration
4. Fairfax County business license (BPOL), Fairfax County Department of Tax Administration. Every business with a physical location in the county files within 75 days of starting there, or pays a 10% late penalty; no tax is owed until gross receipts pass $10,000 in a year. Inside the cities of Fairfax and Falls Church and the towns of Clifton, Herndon and Vienna, the license comes from that city or town instead. Fee: Varies. Takes: The official license can take 4 to 6 weeks; the filed receipt serves until then. https://www.fairfaxcounty.gov/taxes/business/business-forms
5. Unemployment insurance employer registration, Virginia Employment Commission. A business with employees in Virginia must by law register with the VEC: online through iFile and iReg, or by mailing the FC-27. Fee: Varies. https://vec.virginia.gov/tax-filing-registration

Under the zoning ordinance no commercial space may be occupied, and no use changed, until this permit is approved; it is the county's certificate of use and occupancy. Applied for in PLUS. After opening, book the Fire Marshal's post-occupancy inspection within 10 days. Fee: Varies. https://plus.fairfaxcounty.gov/CitizenAccess/Welcome.aspx

### Cosmetics stores in Fairfax County
https://www.placetta.com/guides/fairfax-county/cosmetics-store.html

None of them has a fixed government fee, 7 fees are set by the space or the business and 5 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation (Articles of Organization), Virginia State Corporation Commission, Clerk's Office. Fee: Varies. https://account.tax.virginia.gov/online-services/?link=businessregistration
4. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Fairfax County business license (BPOL), Fairfax County Department of Tax Administration. Every business with a physical location in the county files within 75 days of starting there, or pays a 10% late penalty; no tax is owed until gross receipts pass $10,000 in a year. Inside the cities of Fairfax and Falls Church and the towns of Clifton, Herndon and Vienna, the license comes from that city or town instead. Fee: Varies. Takes: The official license can take 4 to 6 weeks; the filed receipt serves until then. https://www.fairfaxcounty.gov/taxes/business/business-forms

### Restaurants in Edison
https://www.placetta.com/guides/edison/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Edison takes 6 filings with 4 agencies, starting with the business formation and tax registration and ending with the edison retail food license. The fixed government fees add up to about $100, 4 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Business formation and tax registration, NJ Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services. Form or register the company, then register for state taxes. Fee: Varies. https://www.nj.gov/treasury/revenue/
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. New Jersey tax and employer registration (NJ-REG), NJ Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services. Everyone doing business in New Jersey registers; NJ-REG is the tax and employer registration, filed online at least 15 business days before opening. A corporation or LLC files its certificate of formation first. A business collecting sales tax gets a Certificate of Authority. Fee: Varies. Takes: File at least 15 business days before opening. https://www.njportal.com/DOR/BusinessRegistration/Home/FirstStep
4. Food establishment plan review, Edison Township Department of Health. Edison's Division of Health reviews plans for food establishments, for a fee the township code sets. Ask the Health Department at 100 Municipal Boulevard (732-287-0900) how to submit. Fee: $100. https://www.nj.gov/health/ceohs/documents/phfpp/Chapter%2024%20w%20Cottage%20Food%20Rules%201-18-22.pdf
5. Workers' compensation insurance, New Jersey Department of Labor, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://www.nj.gov/labor/workerscompensation/employer-requirements/
6. Edison retail food license, Edison Township Department of Health. Restaurants and food stores apply to the township with Division of Health approval, at 100 Municipal Boulevard. Every food handler and supervisor completes a food handling course the Division of Health accepts within a year of starting work. Fee: Varies. https://cms2.revize.com/revize/edisonnj/document_center/Retail%20Food%20Fillable%20Application.pdf

7. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Workers' compensation insurance, New Jersey Department of Labor, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://www.nj.gov/labor/workerscompensation/employer-requirements/

3. New Jersey tax and employer registration (NJ-REG), NJ Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services. Everyone doing business in New Jersey registers; NJ-REG is the tax and employer registration, filed online at least 15 business days before opening. Takes: File at least 15 business days before opening. https://www.njportal.com/DOR/BusinessRegistration/Home/FirstStep

7. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling

### Restaurants in Jersey City
https://www.placetta.com/guides/jersey-city/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Jersey City takes 8 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the business formation and tax registration and ending with the Jersey City retail food establishment license. None of them has a fixed government fee, 7 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Business formation and tax registration, NJ Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services. Form or register the company, then register for state taxes. Fee: Varies. https://www.nj.gov/treasury/revenue/
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. New Jersey tax and employer registration (NJ-REG), NJ Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services. Everyone doing business in New Jersey registers; NJ-REG is the tax and employer registration, filed online at least 15 business days before opening. A corporation or LLC files its certificate of formation first. A business collecting sales tax gets a Certificate of Authority. Fee: Varies. Takes: File at least 15 business days before opening. https://www.njportal.com/DOR/BusinessRegistration/Home/FirstStep
4. Construction permit for the build-out, City of Jersey City. Construction applications and their inspections come before the Certificate of Occupancy. Fee: Varies. https://www.jerseycitynj.gov/cityhall/HousingAndDevelopment/businesses
5. Food establishment plan review, Your municipal health department (N.J.A.C. 8:24-9.1). New Jersey's food code: plans go to the local health authority for approval before building, converting or remodeling a food establishment. Fee: Varies. https://www.nj.gov/health/ceohs/documents/phfpp/Chapter%2024%20w%20Cottage%20Food%20Rules%201-18-22.pdf
6. Workers' compensation insurance, New Jersey Department of Labor, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://www.nj.gov/labor/workerscompensation/employer-requirements/
7. Jersey City Certificate of Occupancy, City of Jersey City, Department of Housing, Economic Development and Commerce. Needed to operate legally, and for new construction, major renovations or a change in the building's use. Apply through the Jersey City Permit Portal after any construction permits and inspections; open violations on the property block it. Fee: Varies. http://jcnj.org/permitportal
8. Jersey City retail food establishment license, Jersey City Department of Health and Human Services, Division of Environmental Health. New licenses are in person by appointment only (201-547-5285 or 201-547-5173) at 1 Jackson Square (364 MLK Drive). Bring the documents for the pre-operational inspection; once they're approved the inspection is booked, and the license follows a satisfactory one. Renewals are online. Fee: Varies. https://www.jerseycitynj.gov/cityhall/health/divisionofhealth

6. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
7. Hazardous materials registration, Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (DOT). Filed online when you ship or offer certain hazardous materials in bulk, such as large lithium battery shipments. Fee: Varies. https://hazmatonline.phmsa.dot.gov/services/
8. Workers' compensation insurance, New Jersey Department of Labor, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://www.nj.gov/labor/workerscompensation/employer-requirements/
9. Jersey City Certificate of Occupancy, City of Jersey City, Department of Housing, Economic Development and Commerce. Needed to operate legally, and for new construction, major renovations or a change in the building's use. Apply through the Jersey City Permit Portal after any construction permits and inspections; open violations on the property block it. Fee: Varies. http://jcnj.org/permitportal

### Restaurants in Denver
https://www.placetta.com/guides/denver/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Denver takes 9 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the denver retail food establishment license. The fixed government fees add up to about $16, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. LLC formation, Colorado Secretary of State. Form the LLC online with the Secretary of State, or register a company formed elsewhere. Fee: Varies. https://www.coloradosos.gov
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Colorado sales tax and withholding registration, Colorado Department of Revenue. A business with a Colorado location applies in MyBizColorado for the sales tax license and the wage withholding account (or on paper Form CR0100); MyBizColorado also connects you with the Department of Labor and Employment to set up unemployment insurance. Fee: $16. Takes: Applied for online, the account number is shown online; the sales tax license arrives by mail. https://mybiz.colorado.gov/
4. Denver sales tax license, City and County of Denver, Department of Finance, Treasury. Denver collects its own sales tax: a Denver business making retail sales registers in the eBiz Tax Center. With staff working in Denver, also register for the Occupational Privilege Tax. Fee: Free. https://www.denvergov.org/ebiztax
5. Denver zoning use permit, Denver Community Planning and Development. Apply on e-permits (select Zoning Permit); the permit is issued once its fee is paid, and lapses unless a building permit or certificate of occupancy follows within 180 days. Denver's retail food license won't issue without it. Fee: Varies. https://denvergov.org/Government/Agencies-Departments-Offices/Agencies-Departments-Offices-Directory/Community-Planning-and-Development/Plan-Review-Permits-and-Inspections/Zoning-Permits/Apply-for-Commercial-Zoning-Permits
6. Unemployment insurance employer account, Colorado Department of Labor and Employment (CDLE). A new employer opens its unemployment insurance account with CDLE in MyUI Employer+ (Create an Employer User Account), or finishes one started in MyBizColorado. Fee: Free. https://myui.clouduim.cdle.state.co.us/Employer/Core/Login.aspx
7. Food establishment plan review, Denver Department of Public Health and Environment. Denver Public Health lists plan review among the steps to open a food business, and its inspection comes before the retail food license. Fee: Varies. https://denvergov.org/Government/Agencies-Departments-Offices/Agencies-Departments-Offices-Directory/Public-Health-Environment/Public-Health-Investigations/Plan-Review-and-Inspections
8. Workers' compensation insurance, Colorado Department of Labor and Employment, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://cdle.colorado.gov/dwc
9. Denver retail food establishment license, City and County of Denver, Business Licensing. Apply in Denver's Online Permitting and Licensing Center with the entity and on-site manager details, and the Denver sales tax license if you sell taxable goods. After review, Development Services, the Fire Department, Public Health and Zoning inspect. Fee: Varies. Takes: Denver aims to review a complete application within seven business days; the inspections follow. https://www.denvergov.org/Government/Agencies-Departments-Offices/Agencies-Departments-Offices-Directory/Business-Licensing/Business-licenses/Retail-Food/Retail-food/New

### Cosmetics stores in Denver
https://www.placetta.com/guides/denver/cosmetics-store.html
Opening a cosmetics store in Denver takes 13 filings with 11 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the workers' compensation insurance. The fixed government fees add up to about $16, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 7 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation, Colorado Secretary of State. Form the LLC online with the Secretary of State, or register a company formed elsewhere. Fee: Varies. https://www.coloradosos.gov
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf

Fee: $16. Takes: Applied for online, the account number is shown online; the sales tax license arrives by mail. https://mybiz.colorado.gov/
4. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Colorado packaging producer responsibility (EPR): join before selling, unless exempt, Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment, through Circular Action Alliance. The brand registers with Circular Action Alliance and submits a supply report before selling packaged goods in Colorado, then pays dues on covered materials every year, starting January 2026. Producers under the state's revenue threshold, adjusted for inflation each year, are exempt. Fee: Varies. https://cdphe.colorado.gov/hm/epr-program
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. Denver sales tax license, City and County of Denver, Department of Finance, Treasury. Denver collects its own sales tax: a Denver business making retail sales registers in the eBiz Tax Center. With staff working in Denver, also register for the Occupational Privilege Tax. Fee: Free. https://www.denvergov.org/ebiztax
11. Denver zoning use permit, Denver Community Planning and Development. Apply on e-permits (select Zoning Permit); the permit is issued once its fee is paid, and lapses unless a building permit or certificate of occupancy follows within 180 days. Denver's retail food license won't issue without it. Fee: Varies. https://denvergov.org/Government/Agencies-Departments-Offices/Agencies-Departments-Offices-Directory/Community-Planning-and-Development/Plan-Review-Permits-and-Inspections/Zoning-Permits/Apply-for-Commercial-Zoning-Permits
12. Unemployment insurance employer account, Colorado Department of Labor and Employment (CDLE). A new employer opens its unemployment insurance account with CDLE in MyUI Employer+ (Create an Employer User Account), or finishes one started in MyBizColorado. Fee: Free. https://myui.clouduim.cdle.state.co.us/Employer/Core/Login.aspx
13. Workers' compensation insurance, Colorado Department of Labor and Employment, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://cdle.colorado.gov/dwc
