### Coffee shops in Minneapolis
https://www.placetta.com/guides/minneapolis/coffee-shop.html
Opening a coffee shop in Minneapolis takes 8 filings with 8 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (Minnesota LLC) and ending with the minneapolis restaurant license. The fixed government fees add up to about $155, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Articles of Organization (Minnesota LLC), Minnesota Secretary of State, Business Services. Filed online or in person with the Secretary of State ($155, expedited), or by mail ($135). Fee: $155. https://www.sos.mn.gov/media/1824/llcarticlesoforganization.pdf
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Minnesota tax ID and sales tax registration, Minnesota Department of Revenue. Before any taxable sale, get a Minnesota Tax ID and a sales and use tax account in e-Services, or by phone at 651-282-5225. Fee: Varies. https://www.mndor.state.mn.us/tp/eservices/_/?link=NewBusinessReg
4. Minnesota certified food protection manager, Minnesota Department of Health. Food establishments, unless exempt, employ a Minnesota CFPM and display the certificate. Pass an approved course and exam, then apply online within six months of the exam. A newly opening place may start with someone who passed within the last six months, who then has 60 days to get certified. Fee: Varies. https://mn-mdh.portal.opengov.com/categories/1087/record-types/6498
5. Unemployment insurance employer registration, Minnesota Unemployment Insurance Program (DEED). Every employer paying covered wages in Minnesota registers in Employer Self-Service, online or by phone, as soon as possible after the first wages and before the first quarterly wage detail report is due. Fee: Varies. https://www1.ui.mn.gov/ui_employer/ui/employer/login
6. Food plan review, City of Minneapolis, Development Review. The city approves the plans before any work on a new food business, a remodel or expansion, equipment that needs gas, mechanical or plumbing permits, or ventless cooking. Email the application to Development@minneapolismn.gov, upload the documents through the ProjectDox link you get back, and a plan reviewer visits the site. Fee: Varies. https://www.minneapolismn.gov/media/-www-content-assets/documents/Food-Plan-Review-Application-(July-2026).pdf
7. Workers' compensation insurance, Minnesota Department of Labor and Industry. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dli.mn.gov/business/workers-compensation/work-comp-who-needs-workers-compensation-coverage
8. Minneapolis restaurant license, City of Minneapolis, Business Licenses, with Environmental Health. Needed for food or drinks made for dining in, carryout or delivery: a restaurant license with 13 or more seats, a food manufacturer license with 12 or fewer (one application covers both). Apply at least four weeks before opening, after the plans are approved. Fee: Varies. Takes: Apply at least four weeks before opening. https://www.minneapolismn.gov/business-services/licenses-permits-inspections/business-licenses/food-restaurants/restaurant-coffee-cafe/restaurant/application/
What's different for a coffee shop in Minneapolis:
- Minnesota lists coffee beverages with restaurant food: a shop making them is licensed by the Department of Health or the local health department (in Minneapolis, the city), not the Department of Agriculture. Minnesota Department of Health: "sells foods such as burgers, tacos, pizzas, egg rolls, hot entrees, fresh lemonade, coffee beverages, or dirty sodas." https://www.mda.state.mn.us/food-feed/food-licenses (read 2026-10-22)

### Cosmetics stores in Minneapolis
https://www.placetta.com/guides/minneapolis/cosmetics-store.html
Opening a cosmetics store in Minneapolis takes 10 filings with 8 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (Minnesota LLC) and ending with the workers' compensation insurance. The fixed government fees add up to about $155, 4 fees are set by the space or the business and 5 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Articles of Organization (Minnesota LLC), Minnesota Secretary of State, Business Services. Filed online or in person with the Secretary of State ($155, expedited), or by mail ($135). Fee: $155. https://www.sos.mn.gov/media/1824/llcarticlesoforganization.pdf
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Minnesota tax ID and sales tax registration, Minnesota Department of Revenue. Before any taxable sale, get a Minnesota Tax ID and a sales and use tax account in e-Services, or by phone at 651-282-5225. Fee: Varies. https://www.mndor.state.mn.us/tp/eservices/_/?link=NewBusinessReg
4. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Unemployment insurance employer registration, Minnesota Unemployment Insurance Program (DEED). Every employer paying covered wages in Minnesota registers in Employer Self-Service, online or by phone, as soon as possible after the first wages and before the first quarterly wage detail report is due. Fee: Varies. https://www1.ui.mn.gov/ui_employer/ui/employer/login
10. Workers' compensation insurance, Minnesota Department of Labor and Industry. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dli.mn.gov/business/workers-compensation/work-comp-who-needs-workers-compensation-coverage

### Coffee shops in Columbus
https://www.placetta.com/guides/columbus/coffee-shop.html
Opening a coffee shop in Columbus takes 8 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (Ohio LLC) and ending with the columbus food service license. The fixed government fees add up to about $50, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Articles of Organization (Ohio LLC), Ohio Secretary of State, Business Services. Filed online with the Secretary of State, or on the paper form. Fee: Varies. https://www.ohiosos.gov/businesses/filing-forms--fee-schedule/
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Ohio vendor's license (sales tax), Franklin County Auditor, for the Ohio Department of Taxation. A business with a location in Franklin County gets its sales tax account from the County Auditor: complete the ST 1 online, or mail it with the fee to 373 S High St, 21st floor, Columbus. Check with the local zoning department about the address first. Fee: $50. https://franklincountyohio.jotform.com/form/222723544220143
4. Food safety certification for the person in charge, Ohio Department of Health, with the local health district. Ohio's rule asks a food service operation of risk level I to IV, first licensed after March 1, 2010, for at least one person in charge on every shift with person in charge certification; someone with manager certification in food protection doesn't need it. Columbus Public Health teaches a 4-hour person in charge course and the 16-hour ServSafe course. Fee: Varies. https://odh.ohio.gov/know-our-programs/food-safety-program/food-safety-certification/
5. Unemployment insurance employer account, Ohio Department of Job and Family Services, Office of Unemployment Insurance Operations. A new employer creates an OHIO UI account and registers it in the Ohio Unemployment SOURCE employer portal. Fee: Varies. https://thesource.jfs.ohio.gov/employer.html
6. Food service plan review, Columbus Public Health, Food Protection Program. Needed for a new site, a major remodel, or a change of business type or owner, before licensing. Send the plan review packet with payment to EH@Columbus.gov. Covers the cities of Columbus and Worthington. Fee: Varies. Takes: Up to 30 days once the payment and a complete application are in. https://www.columbus.gov/files/sharedassets/city/v/10/public-health/planreview-application.pdf
7. Workers' compensation insurance, Ohio Bureau of Workers' Compensation (the state fund). Ohio employers buy coverage from the state's own fund, the Bureau of Workers' Compensation, not from a private insurer (unless self-insured). Fee: Varies. https://bwc.ohio.gov/employer/forms/coverage
8. Columbus food service license, Columbus Public Health, Food Protection Program. Once the plans are approved and the work is done, complete the license application and ask for the final inspection at least three business days before opening; a new building needs Building Services' final approval first. The license fee is collected at the inspection and the printed license is mailed. Fee: Varies. https://www.columbus.gov/Services/Food-Protection-Program
What's different for a coffee shop in Columbus:
- Ohio rates serving coffee as a risk level I activity, the lowest. The license takes the risk level of the highest-risk activity on the menu, so preparing food moves it up. Ohio Department of Health (licensed locally by Columbus Public Health): "Coffee, self-service hot beverage dispenser drinks, self-service fountain drinks, prepackaged non-time/temperature controlled for safety beverages;" https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-administrative-code/rule-3701-21-02.3 (read 2026-10-22)

### Restaurants in Columbus

Opening a restaurant in Columbus takes 8 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (Ohio LLC) and ending with the columbus food service license. The fixed government fees add up to about $50, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Articles of Organization (Ohio LLC), Ohio Secretary of State, Business Services. Filed online with the Secretary of State, or on the paper form. Fee: Varies. https://www.ohiosos.gov/businesses/filing-forms--fee-schedule/
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Ohio vendor's license (sales tax), Franklin County Auditor, for the Ohio Department of Taxation. A business with a location in Franklin County gets its sales tax account from the County Auditor: complete the ST 1 online, or mail it with the fee to 373 S High St, 21st floor, Columbus. Check with the local zoning department about the address first. Fee: $50. https://franklincountyohio.jotform.com/form/222723544220143
4. Food safety certification for the person in charge, Ohio Department of Health, with the local health district. Ohio's rule asks a food service operation of risk level I to IV, first licensed after March 1, 2010, for at least one person in charge on every shift with person in charge certification; someone with manager certification in food protection doesn't need it. Columbus Public Health teaches a 4-hour person in charge course and the 16-hour ServSafe course. Fee: Varies. https://odh.ohio.gov/know-our-programs/food-safety-program/food-safety-certification/
5. Unemployment insurance employer account, Ohio Department of Job and Family Services, Office of Unemployment Insurance Operations. A new employer creates an OHIO UI account and registers it in the Ohio Unemployment SOURCE employer portal. Fee: Varies. https://thesource.jfs.ohio.gov/employer.html
6. Food service plan review, Columbus Public Health, Food Protection Program. Needed for a new site, a major remodel, or a change of business type or owner, before licensing. Send the plan review packet with payment to EH@Columbus.gov. Covers the cities of Columbus and Worthington. Fee: Varies. Takes: Up to 30 days once the payment and a complete application are in. https://www.columbus.gov/files/sharedassets/city/v/10/public-health/planreview-application.pdf
7. Workers' compensation insurance, Ohio Bureau of Workers' Compensation (the state fund). Ohio employers buy coverage from the state's own fund, the Bureau of Workers' Compensation, not from a private insurer (unless self-insured). Fee: Varies. https://bwc.ohio.gov/employer/forms/coverage
8. Columbus food service license, Columbus Public Health, Food Protection Program. Once the plans are approved and the work is done, complete the license application and ask for the final inspection at least three business days before opening; a new building needs Building Services' final approval first. The license fee is collected at the inspection and the printed license is mailed. Fee: Varies. https://www.columbus.gov/Services/Food-Protection-Program

Opening a cosmetics store in Columbus takes 10 filings with 8 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (Ohio LLC) and ending with the workers' compensation insurance. The fixed government fees add up to about $50, 4 fees are set by the space or the business and 5 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Articles of Organization (Ohio LLC), Ohio Secretary of State, Business Services. Filed online with the Secretary of State, or on the paper form. Fee: Varies. https://www.ohiosos.gov/businesses/filing-forms--fee-schedule/
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf

Check with the local zoning department about the address first. Fee: $50. https://franklincountyohio.jotform.com/form/222723544220143
4. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Unemployment insurance employer account, Ohio Department of Job and Family Services, Office of Unemployment Insurance Operations. A new employer creates an OHIO UI account and registers it in the Ohio Unemployment SOURCE employer portal. Fee: Varies. https://thesource.jfs.ohio.gov/employer.html

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Cupertino
https://www.placetta.com/guides/cupertino/milk-tea-shop.html
Opening a milk tea shop in Cupertino takes 13 filings with 10 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the LLC annual tax ($800). The fixed government fees add up to about $1,075, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to coffee shops.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113947.1
6. Food handler cards for staff, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. Every employee who prepares, stores or handles food gets a California Food Handler Card from an accredited course within 30 days of hire; the card is good for 3 years. Anyone holding a valid food manager certificate is exempt. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113948
7. City of Cupertino business license, City of Cupertino, Business License (administered by HdL). Business license services moved to HdL on September 22, 2025: apply at cupertino.hdlgov.com. Fee: $185. https://cupertino.hdlgov.com/
8. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
9. Food facility plan check, County of Santa Clara Department of Environmental Health. Email the application, scaled plans, menu and equipment sheets to dehplancheck@deh.sccgov.org, then pay the invoiced review fee. The city needs the county's stamped plans before its own plan check. Fee: Varies. Takes: After payment, inspector review may take up to 20 business days. https://deh.santaclaracounty.gov/food-and-retail/compliance-retail-food-operations/submit-plan-review-restaurants-grocery-stores-and
10. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
11. Building permit for the tenant improvement, City of Cupertino Building Division. Apply through the city's online permit portal; food facilities bring the county-approved plans. Fee: Varies. https://www.cupertino.gov/Your-City/Departments/Community-Development/Building/Building-Division-FAQ
12. Health permit to operate a food facility, County of Santa Clara Department of Environmental Health. Submit the permit application by email or in person at or before the final inspection; the operating fee is invoiced after the final. Fee: Varies. Takes: The county's plan review can take up to 20 business days, and the invoice for the operating permit is sent after the final inspection passes. https://deh.santaclaracounty.gov/food-and-retail/compliance-retail-food-operations/submit-plan-review-restaurants-grocery-stores-and
13. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
What's different for a milk tea shop in Cupertino:
- Under California's food code, a food facility in a building built after January 1, 2004 that gives customers space to eat or drink on the premises must provide clean restrooms for them. The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-22)

Every employee who prepares, stores or handles food gets a California Food Handler Card from an accredited course within 30 days of hire; the card is good for 3 years. Anyone holding a valid food manager certificate is exempt. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113948

9. Food facility plan check, County of Santa Clara Department of Environmental Health. Fee: Varies. ### Bakeries in Cupertino
https://www.placetta.com/guides/cupertino/bakery.html
Opening a bakery in Cupertino takes 13 filings with 10 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the LLC annual tax ($800). The fixed government fees add up to about $1,075, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113947.1
6. Food handler cards for staff, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. Every employee who prepares, stores or handles food gets a California Food Handler Card from an accredited course within 30 days of hire; the card is good for 3 years. Anyone holding a valid food manager certificate is exempt. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113948
7. City of Cupertino business license, City of Cupertino, Business License (administered by HdL). Business license services moved to HdL on September 22, 2025: apply at cupertino.hdlgov.com. Fee: $185. https://cupertino.hdlgov.com/
8. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
9. Food facility plan check, County of Santa Clara Department of Environmental Health. Fee: Varies. Takes: After payment, inspector review may take up to 20 business days. https://deh.santaclaracounty.gov/food-and-retail/compliance-retail-food-operations/submit-plan-review-restaurants-grocery-stores-and

Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
11. Building permit for the tenant improvement, City of Cupertino Building Division. Apply through the city's online permit portal; food facilities bring the county-approved plans. Fee: Varies. https://www.cupertino.gov/Your-City/Departments/Community-Development/Building/Building-Division-FAQ
12. Health permit to operate a food facility, County of Santa Clara Department of Environmental Health. Submit the permit application by email or in person at or before the final inspection; the operating fee is invoiced after the final. Fee: Varies. Takes: The county's plan review can take up to 20 business days, and the invoice for the operating permit is sent after the final inspection passes. https://deh.santaclaracounty.gov/food-and-retail/compliance-retail-food-operations/submit-plan-review-restaurants-grocery-stores-and
13. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
What's different for a bakery in Cupertino:
- Under California's food code, a food facility in a building built after January 1, 2004 that gives customers space to eat or drink on the premises must provide clean restrooms for them. The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-22)
- California's Processed Food Registration, from the Department of Public Health, covers bakery products. A retail food facility that sells directly to consumers under a county health permit is exempt, so a bakery selling only over its own counter doesn't need it; making goods for other stores or cafes falls outside that exemption. California Department of Public Health: "General foods such as bakery products, noodles, seafood (except molluscan shellfish)" https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CEH/DFDCS/Pages/FDBPrograms/FoodSafetyProgram/PFRFAQs.aspx (read 2026-10-21)

### Warehouses and 3PLs in Cupertino
https://www.placetta.com/guides/cupertino/warehouse-3pl.html
Opening a warehouse or 3PL in Cupertino takes 12 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the LLC annual tax ($800). The fixed government fees add up to about $1,075, 3 fees are set by the space or the business and 5 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
8. City of Cupertino business license, City of Cupertino, Business License (administered by HdL). Business license services moved to HdL on September 22, 2025: apply at cupertino.hdlgov.com. Fee: $185. https://cupertino.hdlgov.com/
9. Hazardous materials registration, Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (DOT). Filed online when you ship or offer certain hazardous materials in bulk, such as large lithium battery shipments. Fee: Varies. https://hazmatonline.phmsa.dot.gov/services/
10. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
11. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
12. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Milpitas
https://www.placetta.com/guides/milpitas/milk-tea-shop.html
Opening a milk tea shop in Milpitas takes 13 filings with 10 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the LLC annual tax ($800). The fixed government fees add up to about $890, 7 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to coffee shops.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113947.1
6. Food handler cards for staff, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. Every employee who prepares, stores or handles food gets a California Food Handler Card from an accredited course within 30 days of hire; the card is good for 3 years. Anyone holding a valid food manager certificate is exempt. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113948
7. City of Milpitas business license, City of Milpitas Finance Department. A commercial application is reviewed and approved by Building and Planning before the license issues. Fee: Varies. https://milpitas.gov/243/Apply
8. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
9. Food facility plan check, County of Santa Clara Department of Environmental Health. Email the application, scaled plans, menu and equipment sheets to dehplancheck@deh.sccgov.org, then pay the invoiced review fee. The city needs the county's stamped plans before its own plan check. Fee: Varies. Takes: After payment, inspector review may take up to 20 business days. https://deh.santaclaracounty.gov/food-and-retail/compliance-retail-food-operations/submit-plan-review-restaurants-grocery-stores-and
10. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
11. Building permit for the tenant improvement, City of Milpitas Building Safety and Housing. Submit the items on the city's tenant improvement list; a food facility brings drawings approved by Santa Clara County first. Fee: Varies. https://www.milpitas.gov/DocumentCenter/View/165/Tenant-Improvement-PDF
12. Health permit to operate a food facility, County of Santa Clara Department of Environmental Health. Submit the permit application by email or in person at or before the final inspection; the operating fee is invoiced after the final. Fee: Varies. Takes: The county's plan review can take up to 20 business days, and the invoice for the operating permit is sent after the final inspection passes. https://deh.santaclaracounty.gov/food-and-retail/compliance-retail-food-operations/submit-plan-review-restaurants-grocery-stores-and
13. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
What's different for a milk tea shop in Milpitas:
- Under California's food code, a food facility in a building built after January 1, 2004 that gives customers space to eat or drink on the premises must provide clean restrooms for them. The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-22)

Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
9. Packaging producer registration (EPR), CalRecycle, through Circular Action Alliance. A producer of packaged goods sold in California applies to participate in Circular Action Alliance's plan, submits an independent producer application, or obtains a small producer exemption; CalRecycle's PEPRS portal or the PRO takes the registration and the reports. Fee: Varies. https://calrecycle.ca.gov/packaging/packaging-epr/producerguidance/
10. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
11. City of Milpitas business license, City of Milpitas Finance Department. A commercial application is reviewed and approved by Building and Planning before the license issues. Fee: Varies. https://milpitas.gov/243/Apply
12. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
13. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
14. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
15. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. Takes: Nothing is filed with or approved by OEHHA, so there's no processing time; the business decides whether a warning is needed and must have it in place itself. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses

5. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113947.1
6. Food handler cards for staff, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. Every employee who prepares, stores or handles food gets a California Food Handler Card from an accredited course within 30 days of hire; the card is good for 3 years. Anyone holding a valid food manager certificate is exempt. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113948
7. Food facility plan check, San Mateo County Environmental Health Services. Plans for a new or remodeled food facility go to Environmental Health for review before construction; applications are made through the county's MyEHS portal. Fee: Varies. https://smcehs.my.site.com/s/?language=en_US
8. Daly City business license tax certificate, City of Daly City Finance Department. Return the completed application with the fee before starting business; the license year runs October 1 to September 30. Fee: Varies. https://www.dalycity.org/DocumentCenter/View/1175/Business-License-Application-Located-in-Daly-City-PDF
9. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
10. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
11. Building permit for the tenant improvement, City of Daly City Building Division. Apply with the city's tenant improvement submittal; a restaurant includes plans approved by San Mateo County Health. Permits must be obtained within 180 days of applying. Fee: Varies. https://dalycity.org/206/Guide-to-Commercial-Tenant-Improvement
12. Health permit to operate a food facility, San Mateo County Environmental Health Services. Create a MyEHS account (staff confirm it), then apply for the permit there, uploading the documents it asks for as PDFs. Fee: Varies. https://smcehs.my.site.com/s/?language=en_US
13. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
What's different for a milk tea shop in Daly City:
- Under California's food code, a food facility in a building built after January 1, 2004 that gives customers space to eat or drink on the premises must provide clean restrooms for them. The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-22)

Apply with the city's tenant improvement submittal; a restaurant includes plans approved by San Mateo County Health. Permits must be obtained within 180 days of applying. Fee: Varies. https://dalycity.org/206/Guide-to-Commercial-Tenant-Improvement
12. Health permit to operate a food facility, San Mateo County Environmental Health Services. Create a MyEHS account (staff confirm it), then apply for the permit there, uploading the documents it asks for as PDFs. Fee: Varies. https://smcehs.my.site.com/s/?language=en_US
13. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
What's different for a bakery in Daly City:
- Under California's food code, a food facility in a building built after January 1, 2004 that gives customers space to eat or drink on the premises must provide clean restrooms for them. The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-22)
- California's Processed Food Registration, from the Department of Public Health, covers bakery products. A retail food facility that sells directly to consumers under a county health permit is exempt, so a bakery selling only over its own counter doesn't need it; making goods for other stores or cafes falls outside that exemption. California Department of Public Health: "General foods such as bakery products, noodles, seafood (except molluscan shellfish)" https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CEH/DFDCS/Pages/FDBPrograms/FoodSafetyProgram/PFRFAQs.aspx (read 2026-10-21)

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Arcadia
https://www.placetta.com/guides/arcadia/milk-tea-shop.html
Opening a milk tea shop in Arcadia takes 13 filings with 10 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the LLC annual tax ($800). The fixed government fees add up to about $890, 7 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to coffee shops.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/

A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113947.1
6. Food handler cards for staff, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. Every employee who prepares, stores or handles food gets a California Food Handler Card from an accredited course within 30 days of hire; the card is good for 3 years. Anyone holding a valid food manager certificate is exempt. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113948
7. Food facility plan check, Los Angeles County Department of Public Health, Environmental Health. Submit plans before building out; approval comes before the public health permit. Fee: Varies. Takes: Plan review within 20 working days. http://publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/i-want-to/submit-electronic-plan.htm
8. City of Arcadia business license, City of Arcadia Development Services, Business License Division. Every business in Arcadia gets one; check the zoning with Planning before signing a lease. Applying after opening adds a late charge. Fee: Varies. https://www.arcadiaca.gov/government/development_services/business_license/index.php
9. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
10. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
11. Building permit for the build-out, City of Arcadia Building Services. After the county health plan check approves a food facility's plans, the city's building and safety office approves them before construction. Fee: Varies. https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/how-to-obtain-restaurant-food-facility-permit.htm
12. Public health permit (food facility), Los Angeles County Department of Public Health, Environmental Health. Apply after plan approval and before opening; an inspector visits first. Fee: Varies. Takes: Plan review is completed within 20 working days after payment (10 if you pay for expedited review); the inspector needs at least 3 working days' notice for the final inspection, and the permit is issued after the permit fee is paid. http://publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/docs/permit/Public-Health-Permit-License-Application.pdf
13. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
What's different for a milk tea shop in Arcadia:
- Under California's food code, a food facility in a building built after January 1, 2004 that gives customers space to eat or drink on the premises must provide clean restrooms for them. The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-22)

7. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
8. Packaging producer registration (EPR), CalRecycle, through Circular Action Alliance. A producer of packaged goods sold in California applies to participate in Circular Action Alliance's plan, submits an independent producer application, or obtains a small producer exemption; CalRecycle's PEPRS portal or the PRO takes the registration and the reports. Fee: Varies. https://calrecycle.ca.gov/packaging/packaging-epr/producerguidance/
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. City of Arcadia business license, City of Arcadia Development Services, Business License Division. Every business in Arcadia gets one; check the zoning with Planning before signing a lease. Applying after opening adds a late charge. Fee: Varies. https://www.arcadiaca.gov/government/development_services/business_license/index.php
11. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
12. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. Takes: Nothing is filed with or approved by OEHHA, so there's no processing time; the business decides whether a warning is needed and must have it in place itself. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses

### Warehouses and 3PLs in Arcadia
https://www.placetta.com/guides/arcadia/warehouse-3pl.html
Opening a warehouse or 3PL in Arcadia takes 12 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the LLC annual tax ($800). The fixed government fees add up to about $890, 4 fees are set by the space or the business and 5 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
8. City of Arcadia business license, City of Arcadia Development Services, Business License Division. Every business in Arcadia gets one; check the zoning with Planning before signing a lease. Applying after opening adds a late charge. Fee: Varies. https://www.arcadiaca.gov/government/development_services/business_license/index.php
9. Hazardous materials registration, Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (DOT). Filed online when you ship or offer certain hazardous materials in bulk, such as large lithium battery shipments. Fee: Varies. https://hazmatonline.phmsa.dot.gov/services/
10. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
11. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
12. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Alhambra
https://www.placetta.com/guides/alhambra/milk-tea-shop.html
Opening a milk tea shop in Alhambra takes 14 filings with 11 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the LLC annual tax ($800). The fixed government fees add up to about $890, 8 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to coffee shops.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113947.1
6. Food handler cards for staff, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. Every employee who prepares, stores or handles food gets a California Food Handler Card from an accredited course within 30 days of hire; the card is good for 3 years. Anyone holding a valid food manager certificate is exempt. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113948
7. Food facility plan check, Los Angeles County Department of Public Health, Environmental Health. Submit plans before building out; approval comes before the public health permit. Fee: Varies. Takes: Plan review within 20 working days. http://publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/i-want-to/submit-electronic-plan.htm
8. City of Alhambra business license, City of Alhambra Business License Section. Apply online for an in-city license with your Alhambra start date; an occupancy permit application goes with it. Fee: Varies. https://secure.alhambraca.gov/BusinessLicenseApplication/
9. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
10. Workers' compensation insurance, California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://dir.ca.gov/DWC/Employer.htm
11. Certificate of Occupancy (occupancy permit), City of Alhambra Development Services Department. Mail or bring the form to City Hall, Development Services, 111 South First Street. Fee: Varies. https://secure.alhambraca.gov/BusinessLicenseApplication/
12. Building permit for the build-out, City of Alhambra Building Division. After the county health plan check approves a food facility's plans, the city's building and safety office approves them before construction. Fee: Varies. https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/how-to-obtain-restaurant-food-facility-permit.htm
13. Public health permit (food facility), Los Angeles County Department of Public Health, Environmental Health. Apply after plan approval and before opening; an inspector visits first. Fee: Varies. Takes: Plan review is completed within 20 working days after payment (10 if you pay for expedited review); the inspector needs at least 3 working days' notice for the final inspection, and the permit is issued after the permit fee is paid. http://publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/docs/permit/Public-Health-Permit-License-Application.pdf
14. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
What's different for a milk tea shop in Alhambra:
- Under California's food code, a food facility in a building built after January 1, 2004 that gives customers space to eat or drink on the premises must provide clean restrooms for them. The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-22)

Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Testing-Certification/Childrens-Product-Certificate-CPC
8. Packaging producer registration (EPR), CalRecycle, through Circular Action Alliance. A producer of packaged goods sold in California applies to participate in Circular Action Alliance's plan, submits an independent producer application, or obtains a small producer exemption; CalRecycle's PEPRS portal or the PRO takes the registration and the reports. Fee: Varies. https://calrecycle.ca.gov/packaging/packaging-epr/producerguidance/

### Restaurants in Fort Lee
https://www.placetta.com/guides/fort-lee/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Fort Lee takes 7 filings with 5 agencies, starting with the business formation and tax registration and ending with the Fort Lee retail food establishment license. None of them has a fixed government fee, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Business formation and tax registration, NJ Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services. Form or register the company, then register for state taxes. Fee: Varies. https://www.nj.gov/treasury/revenue/
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. New Jersey tax and employer registration (NJ-REG), NJ Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services. Everyone doing business in New Jersey registers; NJ-REG is the tax and employer registration, filed online at least 15 business days before opening. A corporation or LLC files its certificate of formation first. A business collecting sales tax gets a Certificate of Authority. Fee: Varies. Takes: File at least 15 business days before opening. https://www.njportal.com/DOR/BusinessRegistration/Home/FirstStep
4. Food establishment plan review, Borough of Fort Lee Health Department. Under New Jersey's food code, plans go to the local health authority for approval before building or converting a food establishment. Fee: Varies. https://www.nj.gov/health/ceohs/documents/phfpp/Chapter%2024%20w%20Cottage%20Food%20Rules%201-18-22.pdf
5. Workers' compensation insurance, New Jersey Department of Labor, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://www.nj.gov/labor/workerscompensation/employer-requirements/
6. Construction permit for the build-out, Borough of Fort Lee Building Department. The Building Department's state-licensed inspectors permit and inspect construction under the Uniform Construction Code. Fee: Varies. https://www.fortleenj.org/101/Departments
7. Fort Lee retail food establishment license, Borough of Fort Lee Health Department. The Health Department's license for a restaurant or food store, applied for on its form with the fee. Fee: Varies. https://www.fortleenj.org/192/Applications-Permits-Informational-Mater

A corporation or LLC files its certificate of formation first. A business collecting sales tax gets a Certificate of Authority. Fee: Varies. Takes: File at least 15 business days before opening. https://www.njportal.com/DOR/BusinessRegistration/Home/FirstStep
4. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
7. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling

### Warehouses and 3PLs in Fort Lee
https://www.placetta.com/guides/fort-lee/warehouse-3pl.html
Opening a warehouse or 3PL in Fort Lee takes 8 filings with 5 agencies, starting with the business formation and tax registration and ending with the workers' compensation insurance. None of them has a fixed government fee, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Business formation and tax registration, NJ Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services. Form or register the company, then register for state taxes. Fee: Varies. https://www.nj.gov/treasury/revenue/
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. New Jersey tax and employer registration (NJ-REG), NJ Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services. Everyone doing business in New Jersey registers; NJ-REG is the tax and employer registration, filed online at least 15 business days before opening. A corporation or LLC files its certificate of formation first. A business collecting sales tax gets a Certificate of Authority. Fee: Varies. Takes: File at least 15 business days before opening. https://www.njportal.com/DOR/BusinessRegistration/Home/FirstStep
4. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
7. Hazardous materials registration, Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (DOT). Filed online when you ship or offer certain hazardous materials in bulk, such as large lithium battery shipments. Fee: Varies. https://hazmatonline.phmsa.dot.gov/services/
8. Workers' compensation insurance, New Jersey Department of Labor, Division of Workers' Compensation. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://www.nj.gov/labor/workerscompensation/employer-requirements/

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Bellevue
https://www.placetta.com/guides/bellevue/milk-tea-shop.html
Opening a milk tea shop in Bellevue takes 8 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the food service business permit. The fixed government fees add up to about $129, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation, Washington Secretary of State, Corporations. Form the company or register a foreign company online. Fee: Varies. https://ccfs.sos.wa.gov
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Washington business license (state tax registration), Washington Department of Revenue, Business Licensing Service. File online in My DOR, or by mail. It gives the business its UBI number and tax registration, registers trade names and city and state endorsements, and passes your details to Employment Security and Labor and Industries, which open the unemployment insurance and workers' comp accounts. Fee: Varies. Takes: About 10 business days; city or state endorsements can add another 2 to 3 weeks. https://secure.dor.wa.gov/home
4. Food worker cards for staff, Washington State Department of Health, with local health departments. Everyone who works with unpackaged food, food equipment or utensils takes the state training and exam, online only at foodworkercard.wa.gov or through a local health department. A new worker may start before getting the card, for up to 14 days, if the employer gives food safety training. Fee: $10. https://www.foodworkercard.wa.gov
5. City of Bellevue business license, City of Bellevue Finance, Tax Division. Needed once Bellevue gross receipts reach $4,000 a year (or for a regulated activity), after the Washington business license; apply through FileLocal. It doesn't expire, but tax returns are due on the assigned schedule. Fee: $119. https://www.filelocal-wa.gov/Default_FileLocal.aspx
6. Food establishment plan review, Public Health, Seattle and King County. Plans are reviewed before construction, remodeling or a change of owner. Apply and pay in the Public Health Permit Center with the site plan, menu, floor plan, equipment list with make and model, the plan review questionnaire, the finish schedule and the seating layout. Fee: Varies. Takes: An initial review may take up to 8 to 10 weeks at current volumes. https://kingcounty.gov/en/dept/dph/certificates-permits-licenses/food-business-permits/permanent-food-plan-review
7. Building permit for the tenant improvement, City of Bellevue Development Services. Tenant improvements need building and land-use permits from Development Services. Fee: Varies. https://bellevuewa.gov/city-government/departments/finance/business-taxes/business-licenses
8. Food service business permit, Public Health, Seattle and King County. Once plan review is approved, submit the application to operate in the Public Health Permit Center, pay the operating fee and book the pre-operational inspection at least a week before opening. Opening without that inspection can mean closure and a fee of half the yearly permit. Every employee needs a Washington food worker card. Fee: Varies. Takes: Book the pre-operational inspection at least 1 week before opening. https://kingcounty.gov/en/dept/dph/certificates-permits-licenses/food-business-permits/permanent-food-business-permit
What's different for a milk tea shop in Bellevue:
- King County sets the risk category by the menu: drinks made only from commercially packaged products are Category 1 (low), but using Time as a Public Health Control, holding a food out of temperature control for a set time, makes it Category 3 (high), with two routine inspections a year. Public Health – Seattle & King County: "Using Time as a Public Health Control" https://cdn.kingcounty.gov/-/media/king-county/depts/dph/documents/certificates-permits-licenses/food-worker-business-permits/permanent-businesses/food-establishment-risk-levels.pdf?rev=fa5058bfe2344c0da374012f74cac082&hash=6343EB80E0FD05EB643F9899D4DA212D (read 2026-10-22)
