Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Children's Product Certificate, from a CPSC-accepted lab's tests, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). Children's furniture is tested by a third-party, CPSC-accepted laboratory to the children's product safety rules that apply, and the importer issues the certificate, with its test reports, in English, citing each rule. Since July 8, 2026 most certificates are eFiled with CBP at entry, so it is ready before the goods ship. There is no government form. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Testing-Certification/Childrens-Product-Certificate-CPC
7. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
8. City of Bellevue business license, City of Bellevue Finance, Tax Division. Needed once Bellevue gross receipts reach $4,000 a year (or for a regulated activity), after the Washington business license; apply through FileLocal. It doesn't expire, but tax returns are due on the assigned schedule. Fee: $119. https://www.filelocal-wa.gov/Default_FileLocal.aspx

It gives the business its UBI number and tax registration, registers trade names and city and state endorsements, and passes your details to Employment Security and Labor and Industries, which open the unemployment insurance and workers' comp accounts. Fee: Varies. Takes: About 10 business days; city or state endorsements can add another 2 to 3 weeks. https://secure.dor.wa.gov/home
4. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
7. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling

### Restaurants in Rockville
https://www.placetta.com/guides/rockville/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Rockville takes 9 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the LLC formation (Articles of Organization) and ending with the Montgomery County food service facility license. The fixed government fees add up to about $100, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 2 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. LLC formation (Articles of Organization), Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). File online in Maryland Business Express, or mail the signed Articles with a $100 check to SDAT's Charter Division in Baltimore. The resident agent signs too. Fee: $100. Takes: Standard review takes 6 to 8 weeks. https://egov.maryland.gov/businessexpress
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Maryland sales and use tax, withholding and unemployment insurance registration, Comptroller of Maryland, Central Registration. One application opens the sales and use tax license, employer withholding and the unemployment insurance account: online, by fax (410-260-7908) or by mail to Central Registration in Annapolis. Fee: Free. https://interactive.marylandtaxes.gov/webapps/comptrollercra/entrance.asp
4. Certified food service manager, Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services. The facility must be under the immediate control of a Certified Food Service Manager, licensed by the county. Fee: Varies. https://www.montgomerycountymd.gov/HHS-Special/LandRLicenseFoodService.html
5. Food service plan review, Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services, Licensure & Regulatory Services. Health and Human Services reviews the plans of any place that sells or prepares food before a building permit issues. The plans go in with the building permit to the office for the address: the county's Department of Permitting Services (restaurant interior alteration permit), or the City of Rockville's or Gaithersburg's own permitting office. Fee: Varies. https://montgomerycountymd.gov/HHS/Resources/Files/L%26R/Guidance%20-%20DHHS%20Plan%20Review%20via%20DPS%2010_2024.pdf
6. Workers' compensation insurance, Maryland Workers' Compensation Commission. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://www.wcc.state.md.us/PDF/Publications/QandA_Emplr.pdf
7. Commercial occupancy permit, City of Rockville Inspection Services. A commercial tenant applies through MGO Connect; the city inspects before the permit issues. Fee: Varies. https://www.rockvillemd.gov/mgoconnect
8. Building permit for the build-out, City of Rockville Inspection Services. Apply through MGO Connect before construction; most permits need inspections before the work is final. Fee: Varies. https://www.rockvillemd.gov/mgoconnect
9. Montgomery County food service facility license, Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services, Licensure & Regulatory Services. A license is needed before opening: apply and pay on the county's CivicGov portal, or mail or fax the application to Licensure & Regulatory Services in Wheaton. The county answers in 10 to 14 business days and mails the license. Fee: Varies. https://www.civicgov4.com/md_montgomery/portal/

Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
7. Hazardous materials registration, Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (DOT). Filed online when you ship or offer certain hazardous materials in bulk, such as large lithium battery shipments. Fee: Varies. https://hazmatonline.phmsa.dot.gov/services/
8. Workers' compensation insurance, Maryland Workers' Compensation Commission. Bought from an insurer licensed in the state (or the state fund) before the first employee starts; the insurer reports the policy to the state. Fee: Varies. https://www.wcc.state.md.us/PDF/Publications/QandA_Emplr.pdf
9. Commercial occupancy permit, City of Rockville Inspection Services. A commercial tenant applies through MGO Connect; the city inspects before the permit issues. Fee: Varies. https://www.rockvillemd.gov/mgoconnect
